units.english_cohort_translation: **On a Sunday** The Rule of the Service of the Holy Fathers is the same as for a Saint with Polyeleos. However, at Matins, from the beginning to the canon, everything only Resurrectional is taken, as usual; to the Fathers – only the Troparion at *“God is the Lord”*, after the Resurrectional one. After the Exaposteilarion of the Fathers the Theotokion of the Resurrectional Exaposteilarion is not taken, for the Theotokion of the Fathers is separate. At Glory of the Praises there will be not the Gospel Stichera, but of the Holy Fathers; and the Gospel one is taken at the dismissal of Matins According to this rule the Service of the Holy Fathers is taken also on 16 July

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Great Matins** At *“God is the Lord”*: Troparion of the Earthquake twice, Glory: to the Saint, Both now: of the Earthquake. Everything else – to the Saint, only, instead of the Canon to the Theotokos, there will be the Canon of the Earthquake. After the 9th ode, after the Exaposteilarion of the Saint – Glory, Both now: Exaposteilarion of the Earthquake. After the Great Doxology – Troparion of the Saint, Glory, Both now: Troparion of the Earthquake.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 64 пид час спивання видпустового тропаря диякони кадят
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 64.  Під час співання відпустового тропаря диякони кадять тетрапод від чотирьох боків: спочатку обидва – спереду, потім 1-й диякон – від правого боку, 2-й диякон – від лівого, потім ідуть обидва за тетрапод і кадять його від сходу, а після цього – тільки настоятеля і священика.
units.english_cohort_translation: **At Great Vespers** Everything according to the general rule of a Saint with All-Night Vigil; only at *“Lord, I have cried”*: 3 Resurrectional stichera, 3 of the Earthquake and 4 to the Saint. After the Prokimenon the first two readings – to the Earthquake and one – to the Saint. At the blessing of loaves: Troparion "Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos" twice and to the Saint once.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 69 по виголоси нехай буде влада виходит священик
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 69. По виголосі „Нехай буде влада” виходить священик з хрестом в руках північними або, якщо існує звичай, святими дверми. Звідси йде до самого притвору або на місце поблизу вхідних дверей. Хор і свіченосці також згромаджуються у притворі. Священик бере кадильницю, кадить ікони, якщо вони будуть в притворі, хор і людей. По закінченні литійних стихир сам читає єктенії.
units.english_cohort_translation: Notes The fast of this Forty Days the Lviv Synod limits only to three days of each week, that is Monday, Wednesday and Friday, permitting even on those days dairy, and on other days – to eat meat, but on the condition of the 50th Psalm for the clergy, and 5 "Our Father" and 5 "Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos"[^278]  for the faithful, before dinner and before supper. Our custom [is] – to adhere to the fast on the Eve of the Nativity of Christ and Theophany, even if it falls on one of the meat days; we eat nothing with dairy, or very little, until evening. Simple people abstain also from dairy and fast until evening Regarding church services: in the first 35 days of this Forty Days the church rule prescribes a Lenten type of service with prostrations, as in Great Lent, however, only on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. On other days – of the usual type. In view of the Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ, which begins on 20 December, for the last five days of the Forty Days this rule does not give a Lenten service. But today with us and with the Greeks the Lenten service is limited only to Great Lent

70.   Співслужителі   роблять   вхід   і   після   нього вертаються до престолу, як зазначено перед тим в уставі вечірні без всенічного (дар. ч. 51). Зробивши малий поклін, не відходять, але чекають на литію.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 71 потим пид час походу на литии роблят
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 71. Потім, під час походу на литії, роблять всі перед св. трапезою малий поклін і виходять, попереду – молодші, чи то північними, а чи, якщо існує звичай, святими дверми, опустивши долу фелони і руки.
units.english_cohort_translation: After the canon – Kontakion of the Saint [female], Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the Feast.
units.slavonic_text: 71. Потім, під час походу на литії, роблять всі перед св. трапезою малий поклін і виходять, попереду – молодші, чи то північними, а чи, якщо існує звичай, святими дверми, опустивши долу фелони і руки.

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: 71. Потім, під час походу на литії, роблять всі перед св. трапезою малий поклін і виходять, попереду – молодші, чи то північними, а чи, якщо існує звичай, святими дверми, опустивши долу фелони і руки. В притворі або на місці поблизу церковних дверей стають у два ряди, один поруч одного, а головний служитель – посередині, позаду всіх. Диякон або диякони стають поблизу головного служителя.

Потім, під час походу на литії, роблять всі перед св. трапезою малий поклін і виходять, попереду – молодші, чи то північними, а чи, якщо існує звичай, святими дверми, опустивши долу фелони і руки. В притворі або на місці поблизу церковних дверей стають у два ряди, один поруч одного, а головний служитель – посередині, позаду всіх. Диякон або диякони стають поблизу головного служителя.

units.english_cohort_translation: **On a Sunday** If 24 November falls on a Sunday, then the service of St. Mercurius is taken at Compline or is transferred to another day, at the decision of the Superior. The service sung is Resurrectional, of the Feast and of the Saint [female], according to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos with Afterfeast on Sunday.

units.english_cohort_translation: **3.3.4 November: Apodosis of the Entry of the Most Holy Theotokos** and of the Holy Hieromartyrs Clement Pope of Rome and Peter of Alexandria Note The peculiarity of the divine service of this day consists in the fact that on it is taken not only the service of the feast, or on Sunday – also the Resurrectional one, as usually happens on the Apodosis of other feasts, but the service of these two saints is also taken. The reason for this is that the service of these two saints is not transferred to another day, as happens on the Apodosis of other feasts. This can be [the case] when on the Apodosis of other feasts only one service of a saint falls, but here – two, and therefore it is not convenient to transfer it to another day, for then one would have to take three services of saints, and the church rule does not give more than two services. This transfer is all the more inconvenient because these saints have a common troparion and kontakion, although later, in Slavic editions, separate troparia were added to them.

units.english_cohort_translation: **On a Sunday** The service of St. Peter is transferred to another day, at the decision of the Superior. Here is sung the Resurrectional, of the Feast and of Clement, according to the general rule of a saint on 4, that falls with Afterfeast on a Sunday. Only at the Hours the troparion of the saint is not said, but only Resurrectional and Glory: of the feast. Kontakia – alternating: on the 1st and 6th – Resurrectional, on the 3rd and 9th – of the feast. At the Liturgy – everything only of the Sunday and of the feast with the Apostle-Gospel of the feast itself[^287].

units.english_cohort_translation: After the proclamation of the dogma of the Immaculate Conception of the Most Holy Theotokos, our hierarchs ordered in their eparchies to celebrate this feast with the same type of divine service as great feasts of the Theotokos are celebrated. And since the old divine service of this feast under the title "Conception of St. Anne" is limited only to one day[^288]  and is not purely of the Theotokos, the Lviv Synod approved the newly composed service of the Immaculate Conception of the Most Holy Theotokos and ordered it to be sung in all our churches for 9 days, of which the first, that is 8 December, comprises the Forefeast, the second – the Feast, the following six – the Afterfeast, and the last (16 December) – the Apodosis of the feast. And in order not to discard the old service (9 December), it ordered to transfer it back to 8 December, as the service of the Forefeast, however, giving it a small type, that is, ordinary.

units.english_cohort_translation: The Forefeast, Feast, Afterfeast and Apodosis of this feast are celebrated exactly according to the general rule of great feasts of the Theotokos, as is prescribed in the newly published *Anthologion*. However, if its Afterfeast or Apodosis falls on the Sunday of the Forefathers (the second before the Nativity of Christ), which begins on 11 December, then according to the rule approved by the Synod, the divine service is celebrated according to the rule of the Sunday of the Holy Fathers of the First Nicene Council, which is before the Descent of the Holy Spirit, since in both these cases three homogeneous services are taken: Resurrectional, Afterfeast (here – of the Immaculate Conception, there – of the Ascension) and of the Fathers. We will give the rule for this case below, in the rule for the Sunday of the Forefathers.

units.english_cohort_translation: ABOUT THE SEQUENTIAL GOSPELS OF THE LAST FIVE SUNDAYS and about the Gospels of the five Sundays of the *Menaion*, that relate to the Nativity of Christ and Theophany The last five sequential Sundays before the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee, the 10th before the Resurrection, in which the *Triodion* begins, are: 28, 29, 30, 31 and 32. And the five Sundays of the *Menaion* that relate to the feasts of the Nativity of Christ and Theophany [are]: 1. Forefathers, the second before the Nativity of Christ; 2. Fathers, the first before the Nativity of Christ; 3. After the Nativity; 4. Before the Enlightenment (Theophany), 5. After the Enlightenment.

units.english_cohort_translation: The Gospel of this Sunday is the same as that of the Sunday of the Forefathers, that is, about the man Who prepared a great supper. If the 28th Sunday falls on the Sunday of the Forefathers, then at the Liturgy only one, the above-mentioned, Gospel is read; but Apostles – two: of the Forefathers, and also of the 28th Sunday. If the 28th Sunday falls directly before or after the Sunday of the Forefathers, read one Gospel about the man Who prepared a great supper, and "on the 28th Sunday read the sequential one which falls on another Sunday"[^289]. If the 28th Sunday falls directly before the Sunday of the Forefathers, then on the Sunday of the Forefathers the 29th sequential Sunday falls, and it is transferred back, to the 28th Sunday. If the 28th Sunday falls directly after the Sunday of the Forefathers, then on the Sunday of the Forefathers the 27th sequential Sunday falls and it is transferred forward, to the 28th Sunday. Similar will be with the Apostle of the 29th sequential Sunday, which will be the same as that of the Sunday of the Forefathers, that is "Brethren, when Christ appears", although the typikon says nothing about this.

units.english_cohort_translation: The Gospels of these Sundays are usually combined with the Gospels of the *Menaion* Sundays that relate to the Nativity of Christ and Theophany, however, not always identically, but more or less, depending on the greater or lesser distance of the Sunday of the Publican from Theophany. This distance will be greater when Pascha falls later and smaller when Pascha falls earlier. For Pascha can fall on one of 35 days: from 22 March to 25 April, both inclusive. The greater distance between Theophany and the Sunday of the Publican, that is the *Triodion*, will be when Pascha falls on 25 April, for in this case the Sunday of the Publican, the tenth before the Resurrection, falls on 14 February and the distance between Theophany and the *Triodion* will be 38 days, that is 5 weeks and three days, for, having subtracted 6 days from January, 25 will remain, to them are added 13 days of February, and it will be 38; and dividing by 7, it will be 5 integers and 3 remainder. The smaller distance will be when Pascha falls on 22 March, for then the Sunday of the Publican falls on 11 January, and the distance between Theophany and the *Triodion*, that is between 6 and 11 January, will be only 4 days, in the number of which there will not be a single Sunday, for the 4 days before the Sunday of the Publican will be weekdays, namely Saturday, Friday, Thursday and Wednesday.

units.english_cohort_translation: If between Theophany and the *Triodion* there are 5 Sundays, then immediately after Theophany the Sunday after the Enlightenment is taken, and after it – the 4 last sequential ones: 29th, 30th, 31st and 32nd, for they, in this case, are not combined with the *Menaion* ones that are in the cycle of the Nativity of Christ and Theophany, but are transferred here to fill the Sundays that are lacking before the *Triodion*.

units.english_cohort_translation: If between Theophany and the *Triodion* there is not a single Sunday, then the Sunday after the Enlightenment is combined together with the Sunday of the Publican (and according to the rule of the Greek Evangelistarion it is transferred to 7 January and combined with the Synaxis of the Forerunner), and the 32nd sequential Sunday – together with the Sunday before the Enlightenment[^291].

units.english_cohort_translation: Note If the last sequential Sundays are transferred to the Sundays that are lacking between the Sunday after the Enlightenment and the *Triodion*, then according to the rule of our Sluzhebnik[^292], with the Sunday Gospels the weekday Gospels are also transferred. Therefore, even on the weekdays which belong to the cycle of *Menaion* Sundays that relate to the Nativity of Christ and to Theophany, the above-mentioned Gospels of the weekday days should be discarded and the Apostle-Gospel of the services of the saints of the menologion or of various services for every need should be read. If someone wants to repeat the past ones, He can repeat any past week, at His own desire, as the Evangelistarion prescribes: Αναποδιζειν δει όπισθεν, και αναγινωσκειν όθεν ύελεις.

units.slavonic_incipit: Якщо кадить тільки один диякон, то,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: якщо кадит тильки один диякон то покадивши икони
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Якщо кадить тільки один диякон, то, покадивши ікони у притворі, кадить спочатку головного служителя, потім – співслужителів праворуч, і нарешті тих, що стоять ліворуч головного служителя. Якщо кадять обидва диякони, Кожний кадить тих, що стоять по його боці.
units.english_cohort_translation: Answer: We learn about this with the help of the boundary key, which is at the end of the *Horologion* and this typikon, and is given for every year. Having seen which of the 35 boundary keys and which of the 35 Paschal days corresponding to them falls then, we calculate all the days that are between Theophany and the nearest Pascha, and having subtracted from them 10 weeks, that is 70 days, which will be from Pascha back to the Publican, we divide the remainder by 7, and the quotient will give the number of Sundays. If the remainder is not divisible by 7, then there will not be a single one. We give two examples: one, if Pascha falls earlier, and the second – if later.

units.english_cohort_translation: This table consists of six rows, of which the first two encompass March, and the four last – April. The first row has only three letters, the sixth – only four, and the middle ones – seven each. In the case of the first three letters [keys] between Theophany and the *Triodion* there will be no Sunday; in the case of the seven letters of the second row – there will be one Sunday; in the case of the third row there will be two Sundays; in the case of the fourth – three Sundays; and in the case of the sixth – five Sundays[^293].

units.english_cohort_translation: According to this, if you wish to know which Gospel you must take this year 1899 after Theophany before the *Triodion*, then, having looked at the table of boundary keys, which is at the end of the *Horologion(*or of this typikon, you will find for this year the boundary key "Щ"; also having looked at the table presented here before, you will find this letter in the fifth row, and on the right side of the table – the number "IV". Therefore, between Theophany and the*)Triodion* there will be four Sundays, of which the first will be the Sunday after the Enlightenment, the second – the sequential 30th, the third – the 31st Sunday, the fourth – the 32nd Sunday, which is about Zacchaeus; also the *Triodion*.

units.english_cohort_translation: Regarding the superfluous ones, we think that this will never take place. Regarding the lack, we consider that Apostle-Gospels can be lacking at most for five Sundays. To understand this, one must know that Pascha, which follows directly, can fall one or two weeks earlier, or two or three weeks later, than the past one. This conclusion can be made if one compares all the boundary keys of a whole indiction, year after year. Thus, the latest Pascha can fall five weeks later than the previous one, however, with intervals, and not directly from year to year. In that case, if from Pascha to Pascha a whole year ran sequentially, that is 52 weeks, then Apostle-Gospels would be lacking for two Sundays, for they exist only for 50, namely: 18 of the *Triodion* and 32 outside the *Triodion*. If, therefore, the following Pascha falls two weeks earlier than the past one, then from Pascha to Pascha only 50 weeks pass and, thus, the number of Apostle-Gospels equals the number of weeks that pass from Pascha to Pascha, for of those too – 50, thus, there will be no superfluous ones. If from Pascha to Pascha 51 weeks pass, then Apostle-Gospels will be lacking for one week, if 53 (52, namely exactly one year, cannot be), then they will be lacking for 3 weeks; if 54, then they will be lacking for four weeks; if 55, then they will be lacking for five weeks. This lack of sequential Sundays can be filled by the *Menaion* Sundays which belong to the cycle of the Nativity of Christ and Theophany, however, not by all five, but only by four, for the Sunday of the Forefathers and the 28th sequential have the same Gospel, and therefore merge into one Sunday. Therefore one of the past sequential Sundays must be repeated after the Sunday after the Enlightenment.

units.english_cohort_translation: > **Note:** This Sunday, the second before the Nativity of Christ, can fall during the course of seven days, from 11 to 17 December inclusive. Therefore it can fall either in the middle of the feast of the Conception, which is given up on 16 December, or outside, namely 17 December. And since the one that is in the middle of the feast can fall with a Saint either without Polyeleos, which usually happens, or with Polyeleos, as on 13 December, when the Service of St. Eustratius, according to our and Russian typikons, is taken with Polyeleos[^295], the Sunday of the Holy Forefathers has three cases: 1. In the middle of the feast (of the Immaculate Conception) with a Saint without Polyeleos; 2. In the middle of the feast with a Saint with Polyeleos; 3. Outside the feast, that is 17 December. Thus, the Sunday of the Forefathers limits the service of a Saint without Polyeleos to Compline, with the exception of the service of 17 December, that is of the Holy Prophet Daniel and the three youths. Although this service is without Polyeleos, nevertheless, because it has a special relationship to the service of the Forefathers, it is combined with the service of the Forefathers. Now we will give the rule for the three above-mentioned cases.

units.english_cohort_translation: Note When the service of these martyrs falls on weekdays, then their order will be according to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos that falls with Afterfeast on weekdays. If on Sunday, then their service is combined with the Resurrectional and the Forefathers. The service of the Afterfeast is not taken, as in the case of John the Theologian on 8 May, when it falls on the Sunday of the Holy Fathers, which is before the Descent. From here we borrow the rule for this case, since the typikon gives nothing. And it will be such:

units.english_cohort_translation: Note This Sunday can fall on one of seven days, starting from 18 to 24 December. But since 20 December the Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ begins, this Sunday can fall either outside, or in the middle of the Forefeast. Furthermore, if this Sunday falls on the last day of the Forefeast, that is 24 December, on the very Eve of the Nativity of Christ, then it has a separate rule. Therefore this Sunday has three separate rules: one for outside the Forefeast, that is on 18 and 19 December; the second for in the middle of the Forefeast, with the exception of the Eve, that is 20, 21, 22 or 23 December; the third for the Eve, that is for 24 December, as we present.

units.english_cohort_translation: 3. **Canons:** *Distribution:* Canons 3 on 14: Resurrectional with Heirmos on 4, Forefeast on 4 and Fathers on 6. (After the Heirmos of each ode of the Canon of the Fathers the first two troparia – Resurrectional, which are not taken here, but are taken only when the Sunday of the Holy Fathers falls on the very Eve, 24 December, for then the Resurrectional Canon of the *Octoechos* is not taken, but instead of it, these two Resurrectional troparia of the Canon of the Fathers).

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Compline** From 20 December to 14 January, that is until the Apodosis of Theophany, the *Octoechos* canon to the Theotokos is not taken; in the Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ and Theophany the canon of the Forefeast is taken: sometimes one three-ode canon (22, 23 December), sometimes one three-ode canon and a second two-ode canon with it (20 December, 2 January); sometimes two three-ode canons (3 January), sometimes an eight-ode canon (22, 24 December, 4, 5 January). These canons are taken thus: if there is only one canon, then the Heirmoi of each of its odes are taken twice each, troparia on 6 and, again the same Heirmos once for conclusion (instead of Katavasia); if there are two canons, then only the Heirmoi of the first canon are taken twice each, and the Heirmoi of the second canon are taken only once, and this only at the end of each ode; troparia of both canons together on 6. The refrain to the troparia of the canon will be: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", "Glory" – on the penultimate, "Both now" – on the last, only instead of "Glory" at the 8th ode, we sing: "Let us bless the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, the Lord"[^304]; and to the Katavasia we sing: "We praise, we bless" and the rest, as at Matins. The Katavasia is sung by both choirs together with a bow at its end, at the 8th and 9th odes; also after the Heirmos of the 9th ode, before the troparia, a bow is prescribed[^305]. Otherwise at the 3rd, 6th and 9th odes the canon has nothing. After the canon – either *“It is truly meet”*, as the Moscow Typikon gives on 20 December, or only the Heirmos of the 9th ode, as the Pochaiv and Lviv Trefologia give on 2 January.

units.english_cohort_translation: **At the Divine Liturgy** Nothing special, except the Liturgy of Basil the Great with Vespers of the Feast on the Eve of the Nativity and Theophany, if they fall on one of the five fast days, from Monday to Friday. For if they fall on Saturday or on Sunday, then on the Eve there will be the Liturgy of Chrysostom, at its proper time without Vespers, and afterwards – Vespers of the Feast, at its proper time. On the Feast itself – Liturgy of Basil the Great without Vespers. On Friday, before the Eve, to which the Royal Hours are transferred, the typikon gives no Liturgy, this is adhered to also by the Lviv Synod[^307].

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 73 якщо по вечирни наступае безпосередньо утреня то
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 73. Якщо по вечірні наступає безпосередньо утреня, то вони скинувши з себе святі ризи, не виходять зі святилища, але лишаються на сидіннях під апсидою до самого полієлея.
units.english_cohort_translation: Everything – according to the rule given above for the Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ, however, instead of the usual Hours we sing the Great Hours and the Liturgy of Basil with Vespers. Only, if the Eve falls on Saturday or on Sunday, we sing the Hours before that, on Friday, and the Liturgy of Basil – on the very day of the Feast. On the Eve – Liturgy of Chrysostom, at its proper time, and afterwards – Vespers, at its proper time.

units.english_cohort_translation: These Hours are celebrated in the morning, earlier or later, at the decision of the Superior; according to the custom of the arch-cathedral church – at 9 o'clock before noon[^309], so that there would be a certain distance between the Hours and the Liturgy, which according to the custom of the same church begins at 11 o'clock. If the Hours begin earlier, then the Liturgy can also begin earlier, but since it is celebrated with Vespers, it should begin around 10 o'clock, as the Lviv Synod decreed about Vespers with the Presanctified The composition and form of the Great Hours is the same as of the usual Hours, with the exception of three troparia and three readings, given after the Theotokion "What shall we call Thee" at the 1st Hour and after the corresponding ones at the other Hours. Regarding the essence, the Royal Hours differ from the usual ones also by the tripalm, which at the Royal Hours is special, appropriate to the given feast[^311]

units.english_cohort_translation: In the temple, before the Holy Doors, opposite the people, two analogia are placed, on the first of which the Gospel is placed; the second, slightly lower, – opposite the Holy Doors, from which the Paremia and Apostle are to be read. Where there is no analogion for the Gospel, it lies on the Holy Table and is brought out by the Priest through the Holy Doors only for reading, and is supported by servers The Royal Hours are celebrated with the Holy Doors closed, which are opened only for the reading of the Gospel Candles on the altar are lit only for the reading of the Gospel

units.english_cohort_translation: At the appointed time the Priest enters the temple and, having approached the Holy Table and having bowed low, kisses the Gospel, marks four Gospel readings and, having bowed again, goes out to the sacristy; puts on an epitrachelion, goes out before the closed Holy Doors, makes a low bow to the Holy Mysteries and begins the usual: "Blessed is our God". Choir: "Amen", also "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", "O Heavenly King" and everything else, as usual, up to "O come, let us worship" inclusive[^313]. At the second "O come, let us worship" the Priest, having bowed low, enters the sanctuary and, while the choirs sing the tripalm, reads it sitting in his place.

units.english_cohort_translation: When, after the Troparion of the Forefeast "Once Mary was registered", the Theotokion is also read, the choirs sing three stichera idiomesa[^314]  on 6, that is twice each. The first stichera both the first and the second time is sung without a refrain; the second – the first time with a separate refrain, and the second – with another separate refrain; the third – the first time with the refrain "Glory", and the second – with the refrain "Both now". All four above-mentioned refrains at all Hours – are the same. At the 9th Hour the third stichera is taken three times, that is the first time it is read loudly and piously by the canonarch in the middle of the church, without a refrain, then the second time – by one choir with the refrain "Glory", and the third – by the other with the refrain "Both now"[^315].

units.english_cohort_translation: After the singing of the three stichera there will be three readings: the first – of the Prophecy with a Prokimenon, the second – of the Apostle without a Prokimenon and without Alleluia, the third – of the Gospel, beginning it from "Wisdom, attend!", "Let us hear". All this is accompanied by the following actions: when the stichera end, the Priest puts on a phelonion and, having gone out before the steps of the altar and having bowed, opens the Holy Doors and exclaims: "Let us attend! Peace be unto all!" (blessing the people), "Wisdom! Let us attend!". The choirs sing the Prokimenon. After its conclusion the Priest, having exclaimed before the title of the Prophecy "Wisdom!" and before the reading "Let us attend!", waits before the steps of the altar for the end of the reading of the Prophecy and, after its conclusion, having exclaimed "Wisdom!" and "Let us attend!" before the reading of the Apostle, as usual, puts incense into the censer with the short prayer "Incense we offer to Thee" and, having blessed the incense with the words "Blessed is our God", censes everything as usual, that is the Holy Table from four sides, the iconostasis, the choirs and the people[^316]. At the end of the Apostle, and together with it the censing, the candle-bearers go out before the analogion, and the Priest approaches the Holy Table and, having bowed, takes the Holy Gospel and, having placed it on the analogion, begins to sing the Gospel from "Wisdom, attend". After the singing of the Gospel the Priest, having kissed the beginning of the reading, leaves it there, closes the Holy Doors and, having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, goes out to the sacristy, takes off the phelonion, goes out through the side doors before the Holy Doors for "Thou Who at all times" and remains there until the end of the Hour.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 75 священик накладае на рясу епитрахил попередньо поблагословивши
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 75.  Священик накладає на рясу епітрахиль, попередньо поблагословивши його, йде перед св. двері та починає так: „Благословенний Бог наш”. Хор: „Амінь”, „Слава Тобі, Боже наш, слава Тобі”, „Царю небесний”, трисвяте, „Пресвята Тройце”, „Отче наш”. Священик: „Бо Твоє є царство”. Хор: „Амінь”, „Господи, помилуй” (12), „Слава, і нині”, „Прийдіте, поклонімся” (3).  Священик входить південними дверми у святилище, проказує молитву кадила, бере кадильницю, кадить престіл від чотирьох боків, запрестольну ікону та інші ікони святилища. Відтак виходить зі святилища північними дверми, приходить перед св. двері і, вклонившись, кадить ікони південної частини іконостасу, починаючи від образа Спасителя, ікони північної частини, починаючи від ікони Богородиці, потім – хори, правий та лівий.
units.english_cohort_translation: If there be deacons, they put on dalmatics with an orarion before the beginning of the 1st Hour and remain vested until the end of the Typika. At the Prokimenon, together with the Priest, they go before the steps of the altar and, having bowed low all together to the Holy Mysteries, open the Holy Doors. The right Deacon exclaims: "Let us attend!", and the left, after the giving of peace by the Priest: "Wisdom! Let us attend!". Also before the first and second reading – the right: "Wisdom!", and the left: "Let us attend!" and they cense everything as usual, as at the beginning of the Liturgy. At the end of the Apostle, and together with it the censing, both deacons stand with the Priest before the steps of the altar and, having bowed all three together to the Holy Mysteries, go out from the sanctuary: the Priest with the Gospel through the middle [doors], and the deacons, having swapped their sides, through the side doors to the analogion. The right Deacon exclaims: "Wisdom, attend!", "Let us hear", the Priest: "The reading from the Holy Gospel according to (Name)", and the left deacon: "Let us attend!". The Priest sings the Gospel. Having finished, the Priest kisses the beginning of the reading, also the right deacon, and after him the left. Having bowed low, the deacons return through their doors to the sanctuary and, together with the Priest, close the Holy Doors. Having bowed low all three together to the Holy Mysteries, they withdraw: the deacons to their places, and the Priest before the iconostasis for "Thou Who at all times".

units.slavonic_incipit: Людей кадить або з солеї або
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: людей кадит або з солеи або переходячи цилий
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Людей кадить або з солеї або переходячи цілий храм, доки хор читає 20(19) псалом „Нехай Господь” і 21(20) „О Господи, в силі Твоїй”, коли хор починає трисвяте, священик вертається перед св. двері, кадить їх і по „Отче наш” виголошує: „Бо Твоє є царство”, входить південними дверми у святилище, стає перед св. трапезою і, по закінченні тропарів „Спаси, Господи, людей Твоїх”, виголошує єктенію за царів. По виголосі „Бо милостивий”, хор: „Амінь”, „Іменем Господнім благослови, отче”.
units.english_cohort_translation: If the hierarch or other sacred dignitaries be present in the church, the deacons should cense them before the choirs, and neither the Priest nor the deacons should kiss the Gospel before the hierarch and sacred dignitaries, and therefore both deacons together carry the open Gospel to them for kissing, also to the Priest standing in the Holy Doors and, when he kisses it, the deacons themselves kiss [it], after which they place it on the analogion and, having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, return, each through his doors, to the sanctuary.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 76.  Під час читання шестипсалмія  священик, стоячи перед св. трапезою, починає проказувати утренні молитви. Після трьох перших псалмів виходить північними дверми і, ставши перед св. дверми, продовжує читати утренні молитви.
units.english_cohort_translation: Answer: The Typikon mentions the Troparion and Kontakion of the Eve, therefore we think that one should take [those] of the Eve. If someone thinks that this will not be good and takes one Troparion for two days, that is on the Eve and before the Eve, let him consider that the Troparion of the Forefeast is also taken the same on two different days of the Forefeast.

units.slavonic_incipit: На кінці шестипсалмія диякон, одягнений у
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: на кинци шестипсалмия диякон одягнений у стихар з
units.slavonic_diplomatic: На кінці шестипсалмія диякон, одягнений у стихар з орарем, виходить північними дверми, віддає священикові шану, стає на своєму звичайному місці та виголошує велику єктенію. Священик виголошує: „Бо Тобі належить”. Під час співання хором „Бог – Господь” диякон проказує стихи і, після малого поклону, вертається південними дверми у святилище.
units.english_cohort_translation: After the concluding prayer of the 9th Hour we immediately read the Typika just as in the *Horologion*, however, without the introductory verse that is before the first psalm, without the stichera on the "Beatitudes", without the Apostle-Gospel; also, if there be Liturgy, then also without the "Creed" and without "Blessed be the name of the Lord", and without the following 33rd Psalm, for all this will be taken at the Liturgy. When the Royal Hours are transferred back, to Friday, then since then there will be no Liturgy, here both the "Creed" and "Blessed be the name of the Lord" with the 33rd Psalm is read. Instead of the kontakia of the temple, of the day and others, one Kontakion of the Eve is taken. Here is the detailed rule for you.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 77.  По тропарях читає читець чергову катизму, після якої диякон перед св. дверми – малу єктенію, а священик виголошує: „Бо Твоя держава”. Відтак читець читає другу чергову катизму, диякон – другу малу єктенію, а священик – виголос „Бо ти благий”.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: диякон господеви помолимся хор господи помилуй священик виголошуе
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Диякон: „Господеві помолімся”. Хор: „Господи, помилуй”. Священик виголошує: „Бо Ти святий сси, Боже наш”. Диякон кадить св. трапезу від чотирьох боків та все інше, за звичаєм (див. ч. 33). Хор: „Усе, що живе, нехай хвалить Господа”. Диякон проказує обидва стихи, а хор повторює: „Усе, що живе”, після чого диякон: „І щоб удостоїтися нам”.
units.english_cohort_translation: The Priest goes out before the Holy Doors in an epitrachelion, reads the prayer "O All-Holy Trinity" (if there be Liturgy, then the Choir immediately: *“It is truly meet”* and the rest; if not, then before *“It is truly meet”* the Choir sings: "Blessed be the name of the Lord" (3) and Psalm "I will bless the Lord", and the Priest then waits before the Holy Doors until the end)

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: Диякон: „Господеві помолімся”. Хор: „Господи, помилуй”. Священик виголошує: „Бо Ти святий сси, Боже наш”. Диякон кадить св. трапезу від чотирьох боків та все інше, за звичаєм (див. ч. 33). Хор: „Усе, що живе, нехай хвалить Господа”. units.english_cohort_translation: **3.4.8.3 Vespers of this feast will be either with the Service of Basil, or separately, as on Saturday or on Sunday. It is never served completely, but, if it be with the Service, only until the end of the readings, after which the Small Litany is exclaimed and the exclamation of the Trisagion; and from here, according to the order, the Service of Basil. If it be separately, then only until the end of the litany "Let us complete", that is until the end of its second exclamation ("For Thine is the kingdom"), because the Aposticha and everything else is taken at the All-Night Vigil after the Litya** Vespers has not only 3 readings, as on other feasts, but 8 (on Theophany – 11); therefore, after the first three and after the second three readings, it has a separate troparion with its verses Compline is served only until the end of "Glory to God in the highest" and immediately the Litya begins with the blessing of loaves and everything else, as at the All-Night Vigil with Vespers Theophany has the Great Blessing of Water directly after Vespers; also, according to our custom, more solemnly – on the very day of the feast, after the Prayer behind the Ambo

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Після стихири диякон на своєму звичайному місці: „Спаси, Боже, людей Твоїх”. Хор: „Господи, помилуй” (12) і священик виголошує: „Благодаттю і щедротами”. Хор: „Амінь”. Починається канон. Святі двері, якщо не було всенічного, зачиняються.
units.english_cohort_translation: On the Eve of the Nativity of Christ and Theophany, when there is to be the Service of Basil with Vespers, the Lviv Synod forbids read services. If several priests wish to serve, it orders them to sing only one service in the cathedral (Title IV, chap. I, part 5)

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 80 якщо було всеничне священик по виголоси благодаттю
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 80.  Якщо було всенічне, священик по виголосі „Благодаттю”, тримаючи в руках хрест, виходить святими, а диякон з єлеєм, поблагословленим на вечірні, та мирником, – північними дверми і стають по правому боці тетраподу. Там помазує священик навхрест чоло кожного, хто підходить цілувати святу Євангелію. По закінченні мирування вертаються у святилище: ієрей – святими, а диякон – південними дверми і, зачинивши святі двері, священик скидає з себе фелон.
units.english_cohort_translation: **3.4.8.8 In the arch-cathedral church Vespers with the Service of Basil begins at 10.30. If the Eve falls on Saturday or on Sunday, then the Service of Chrysostom without Vespers will be at 08.30, and Vespers separately begins at 11.00, in order to hasten the Holy Supper, which according to the typikon should begin later, that is at 3 o'clock in the afternoon (current 1 o'clock after noon) on the Eve of the Nativity, and on the ### 3.5.3 Eve of Theophany – in the evening hours, that is at the usual time. All-Night Vigil with Compline – at the usual time[^318]. Now we will give three detailed rules: one – for the case of Vespers with the Service of Basil, one – for the case of Vespers which is celebrated separately, without the Service, and one – for the All-Night Vigil with Great Compline** VESPERS WITH THE SERVICE OF BASIL with the Eve on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday From the beginning to "Blessed is the Kingdom" everything is exactly as usual at the Service without Vespers After "Blessed is the Kingdom", immediately after "Amen" – "O Heavenly King" and the rest with the Trisagion, as usual, up to "O come, let us worship" inclusive

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 81 по третий и шостий писнях спивае диякон
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 81. По третій і шостій піснях співає диякон малу єктенію чи то перед св. дверми, чи то коло тетраподу, якщо мирування ще не було закінчене, а священик виголошує виголос або зі святилища, або від тетраподу.
units.english_cohort_translation: At the introductory Psalm the Priest, standing near the Holy Table, reads with uncovered head the usual evening prayers and afterwards from there exclaims the litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord". If there be also a Deacon, then he goes out at this litany before the Holy Doors

units.english_cohort_translation: **On a Sunday** 1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 8 stichera, Glory, Both now: Stichera from the Heirmologion, if there be none, then according to the tone of the idiomesa 2. **Entrance:** Entrance with the Gospel, with the usual prayer of the Entrance. If there be deacons, then the first of them, who is to the right of the Priest, carries the Gospel, and the second goes before him with the censer; and they do in this everything as at the Entrance with the Gospel at the Liturgy Prokimenon of the day from the *Horologion*, only on Friday evening for Saturday there will be the Great Prokimenon of the Feast, given for the very day of the Feast at Vespers on 26 December. After the singing before the steps of the altar "Let us attend! Peace be unto all!", "Wisdom, let us attend!" the Priest withdraws behind the Holy Table and sits there during the readings in his place. The deacons, if there be [any], remain at the Holy Doors and from here exclaim according to the order "Wisdom" and "Let us attend" with the lifting of the orarion towards the people, as the order of All-Night Vigil prescribes There will be 8 readings, and on Theophany – 11. After the first three and the second three readings of both feasts there will be a separate troparion with its verses; there will be three of them[^321], besides "Glory, Both now", for the whole troparion is sung only twice, namely: once before the first verse and once before the last verse, that is before "Both now", and after the other verses – only up to the half[^322]

units.english_cohort_translation: 9. After the singing of the Gospel the Priest, having kissed the beginning of the Gospel reading and having given [it] to the first deacon to kiss, also to the second, approaches the Holy Table, on which he places the Holy Gospel, which remains there. The deacons, having bowed low before the steps of the Holy Table, go out, each through HIS doors, before the Holy Doors and, having bowed low, first the second Deacon exclaims "Let us all say", and also the first after "Vouchsafe" – the litany "Let us complete". If there be no deacons, then the Priest himself sings the litanies from the Holy Table and immediately after the second exclamation of the litany "Let us complete" gives the Great Dismissal of the Feast itself. (On Theophany there is no dismissal here, but it will be after the Blessing of Water)

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: 82. По хвалитних стихирах, на „Слава”, диякон відчиняє св. двері. Священик у фелоні стає перед престолом, праворуч нього стає диякон і, по закінченні останньої стихири священик, обернений до сходу, виголошує: „Слава Тобі, що Світло нам показав”. units.english_cohort_translation: After the end of the second tripalm the choirs sing alternatingly "God is with us", that is selected verses of the eighth ode of the prophecies of Isaiah. They sing thus: 1st choir: "God is with us, understand ye nations,... for God is with us", afterwards the second choir sings the same. Also other verses the choirs sing alternatingly, ending each verse with the words "For God is with us". After the end of all verses they sing "God is with us" three times[^327]. The custom of singing the whole first verse after each of the following ones as is usually done here, we do not find in any typikon[^328]. The Lviv Synod also adds that the Priest should not go out before the Holy Doors and sing these verses alternatingly with the choirs, but only there/, where there will be only one choir, for then the Priest replaces one of the choirs. Similarly he should not go out for the moleben verses "O Most Holy Lady", which the choirs say twice, that is once one, and once the other choir, but only, if there be one choir Instead of the troparia of the day, given after the moleben verses "O Most Holy Lady", the Troparion of the Feast is sung; and instead of the troparia "Have mercy on us, O Lord", given after the Trisagion, which is after the Prayer of Manasses, the Kontakion of the Feast is sung The Priest goes out before the Holy Doors for three prayers: of Basil, of Manasses and the second of Basil After "Glory to God in the highest" the Priest, having put on a phelonion, opens the Holy Doors and there will be Litya and everything else until the end of Matins exactly as at the All-Night Vigil with Vespers

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: 83.  Після цього стає диякон на своє звичайне місце і виголошує єктенії „Помилуй нас, Боже” і „Сповнім”. Священик благословляє людей і виголошує: „Мир всім”. Хор: „І духові твоєму”. Диякон: „Голови ваші перед Господом схиліть”. Хор: „Тобі, Господи”. Священик проказує потиху молитву „Господи святий”, після чого виголошує: „Бо до Тебе належить”. Наступає відпуст, що його починає диякон: „Премудрість” (див. ч. 36).

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 84 по видпусти читец видразу починае 1 й час
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 84. По відпусті читець відразу починає 1-й час: „Прийдіте, поклонімся” (3) і псалми. По „Отче наш” священик в епітрахилі: „Бо Твоє є царство”. Читець – кондак і „Господи, помилуй” (40). Священик виходить зі святилища північними дверми і перед святими, обернений до сходу, голосно: „Ти, що повсякчас”. Читець: „Господи, помилуй” (3), „Слава, і нині”, „Чеснішу від херувимів”, „Іменем Господнім благослови, отче”. Священик: „Боже, змилуйся над нами”. Читець: „Амінь”. Священик проказує молитву „Христе, світло істинне”, „Слава Тобі, Христе Боже”. Читець: „Слава, і нині”, „Господи, помилуй” (3), „Благослови”.
units.english_cohort_translation: **3.4.9 December: Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos** and of St. Joseph the Betrothed and of the Holy Hieromartyr Euthymius Notes The Service of the Hieromartyr is sung at Compline on another day St. Joseph has nothing in the divine service, except one troparion and kontakion, and this only in our horologia and sluzhebnyky. And the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos also has almost nothing. Vespers of this feast has an entrance not for the sake of the Synaxis, but for the sake of the Great Prokimenon of the Feast. Matins from the beginning to the canon – of small type, from the canon to the end – of great type Although the divine service of this day, as also of the following, does not have All-Night Vigil, as also Polyeleos, however, our custom, approved by the Synod of Zamość (Titolo de Jeiuniis et Festis) /On fast and feasts/ and Lviv (Title IV, chap. 6) orders during the first three days of this feast to abstain from heavy work and to participate in the divine service; to these days belong: 25, 26 and 27 December

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: катавасии восьмои писни 1 й диякон бере кадильницю
units.slavonic_diplomatic: По катавасії восьмої пісні 1-й диякон бере кадильницю, виходить північними дверми, стає перед іконою Богородиці і закликає: „Богородицю і Матір Світла”, потім вертається південними дверми у святилище і, разом з 2-им дияконом кадить престіл та все інше, як зазначалось вище (див. 4.39), а після кадження вертаються у святилище: 1-й диякон – південними, а 2-й – північними дверми.
units.english_cohort_translation: **At Matins** 1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Troparion of the Feast twice, Glory: to the Kinsmen of God, Both now: to the Feast 2. units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 90 по закинченни шестипсалмия не вертаеться у святилище
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 90.  По закінченні шестипсалмія не вертається у святилище, але, стоячи перед св. дверми, виголошує велику єктенію та її виголос: „Бо Тобі належить”, а також під час співання хором „Бог Господь” – стихи. По закінченні цього робить малий поклін і південними дверми вертається у святилище.
units.english_cohort_translation: > **Note:** This Saturday has three cases: it can fall either on the first, or on the last day of the Afterfeast of the Nativity of Christ, or on others. When it falls on the first day, that is 26 December, then it is taken with the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos and has a separate rule; when – on the last, that is 31 December, then it is taken with the Apodosis of the feast of the Nativity and has a separate rule; if on others, that is 27, 28, 29 and 30 December, then it also has a separate rule. We will give consistently all three rules.

units.slavonic_diplomatic:
4. У співслужінні священиків
94. Співслужителі, в паристій кількості, накладають на ряси епітрахилі й одягають фелони під час читання катизми та стають по боках св. трапези, як на вечірні (дав* ч. 50). Під час співання полієлея виходять усі, зробивши малий поклін, св. дверми, опустивши фелон і руки долу, попереду – молодші.
units.english_cohort_translation: King David and James, Brother of the Lord > **Note:** Also this Sunday, as the Saturday, can fall on 26 December with the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos or on 31 December with the Apodosis of the Nativity, or on 27, 28, 29, 30 December with the Afterfeast of the Nativity. We will give the rules for all these three cases.

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source:
4. У співслужінні священиків
94. Співслужителі, в паристій кількості, накладають на ряси епітрахилі й одягають фелони під час читання катизми та стають по боках св. трапези, як на вечірні (дав* ч. 50). Під час співання полієлея виходять усі, зробивши малий поклін, св. дверми, опустивши фелон і руки долу, попереду – молодші. Два перші несуть ікону свята або святого, якщо вона не була ще покладена на лівому боці тетраподу поміж обома хорами, і кладуть її на тетрапод; всі стають по боках тетраподу в два ряди, один напроти одного, головний служитель стоїть посередині перед тетраподом, а праворуч нього – диякон.

units.english_cohort_translation: After the Entrance: Resurrectional Troparion, of the Feast and of the Saints; Glory: Kontakion of the Saints, Both now: of the Feast. Everything else – only to the Saints, except the Prokimenon, which according to Slavic typikons, will be first Resurrectional of the tone, and then of the Saints. The Communion Hymn will be "Praise the Lord" and of the Saints[^336].

25      26      27      28      29      30      31      1       2       3       4       5       6
Su      Mo      Tu      We      Th      Fr      Sa      Su      Mo      Tu      We      Th      Fr

Regarding the second question, that is what to do with one Saturday or Sunday which sometimes has no place, we answer: Greek books give no rule for this and therefore this Saturday or Sunday should not have been taken. However, the Slavs do not wish to discard anything and give the following rules for this case. between the Nativity of Christ and Theophany SATURDAY

units.english_cohort_translation: The Saturday, which will be the one between the Nativity and Theophany can fall either in the middle, or outside the feast of the Nativity: in the middle, namely 30 or 31 December so, as in the first and second rows; outside the feast, namely 1 January, as in the 7th row. If, therefore, it falls in the middle of the feast, then the Apostle-Gospel will be first of the ### 3.4.10 Saturday after the Nativity, and after – of the Saturday before Theophany. Prokimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn on 30 December will be only of the ### 3.4.10 Saturday after the Nativity; on 31 December, that is on the Apodosis of the feast – will be only of the Feast. If, therefore, it falls outside the feast, as in the 6th row, that is 1 January, then the Apostle-Gospel will be first to the Circumcision, for the Saturday does not have them. On ### 3.4.10 Saturday after the Nativity the Apostle-Gospel is taken on the Apodosis of the feast, 31 December. Prokimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn – only of the Feast.

units.english_cohort_translation: If there be one Sunday between the Nativity and Theophany, then, similarly as for Saturday, it falls either in the middle of the feast, that is 30 or 31 December, as in the 3rd and 2nd rows, or outside the feast, that is 1 January with the Circumcision, as in the 1st row. And if it falls in the middle of the feast, then the Sunday after the Nativity is taken on 30 or 31 December according to the rule given here on p. 182-183. And the Sunday before Theophany is taken on 1 January in the first place, also the Circumcision and everything else according to the rule which is given for 1 January, when it falls on a Sunday. If the Sunday is one and falls on 1 January, as in the 1st row, then the Sunday after the Nativity is taken on 26 December with the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos according to the rule given here on p. 181[^337].

units.english_cohort_translation: **3.4.13 December: Holy First-Martyr Stephen** and Venerable Theodore The Service of these Saints – without Polyeleos, according to the general rule of two saints on 4 in the Afterfeast, although in the Pochaiv *Anthologion* the Service of St. Stephen is given with Polyeleos. One peculiarity of this day – at Matins, for St. Protomartyr (according to others also the Feast) has both Stichera of the Praises, and afterwards – Small Doxology, and Aposticha in its place. Finally our people even on this day abstain from work and take part in the divine service.

Everything here according to the general rule of the Apodosis of a Feast of the Lord, only here on Friday evening, at the end of the stichera at *“Lord, I have cried”*, there will not be the 1st Theotokion of the tone that is being given up (Dogmatikon), but there will be the stichera of the very day of the Feast "To Augustus".

units.english_cohort_translation: Note In general typikons the divine service of this day is not given with All-Night Vigil, but only with Polyeleos. However, probably for the sake of the beginning of the civil year, or also for Basil the Great, for many years All-Night Vigil has been served with us, because it is already given in the Pochaiv *Anthologion* of 1777[^339]. We will present the rule first for weekdays, and then for Sunday.

units.english_cohort_translation: After the Prayer behind the Ambo, if Saturday or Sunday, then after the dismissal of Vespers, the church cross-bearer stands between two candle-bearers in the middle of the church, and before Him – a church server with three candlesticks, with a censer and with a vessel for incense. The Deacon takes the Holy Gospel from the table, the Priest takes the cross with his right hand and, having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, they go out through the Holy Doors: first the Deacon with the Gospel, behind him – the Priest with the cross, vested in all sacred vestments of his rank, and the Choir sings the Troparion "The voice of the Lord"[^347]; all proceed to the narthex of the church. When all have gone out there, the Deacon places the Holy Gospel, and the Priest – the cross on a table covered with a tablecloth or a clean cloth, on which there will be also a wide vessel with water; and immediately the Priest censes the table from four sides and all present, according to the order.

units.english_cohort_translation: After the singing of the Gospel the Deacon says the litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord", during which the Priest reads quietly the prayer "O Lord Jesus Christ"; and after the prayer He does not exclaim, but says to Himself: "Amen". And when "For the precipitous, pure" is said, the Priest begins loudly this prayer: "Great Art Thou, O Lord"[^348]. The prayer "O Trinity beyond all being", since it is given only in some editions, may be omitted; this is allowed by the *Euchologion* of Benedict, although our typikons do not allow this[^349].

units.english_cohort_translation: In the prayer "Great Art Thou, O Lord" three members are exclaimed three times, namely the first member "Great Art Thou, O Lord", at which the Priest three times crosswise signs the water with three lit candles[^350]; the second "Thou Thyself, therefore", at which He blesses the water with His hand, immersing His fingers crosswise; the third "Thou Thyself and now", at which He breathes three times crosswise on the water. When He exclaims: "And save, O Lord, Thy servants, the Most Holy Ecumenical Primate (Name) the Pope of Rome[^351]  and our faithful Emperor (Name)" the Choir sings "Many Years".

units.english_cohort_translation: At the end of this prayer the Choir: "Amen"; priest: "Peace be unto all" and, after the prayer at the bowing of heads, which he says quietly, he exclaims: "For Thou Art the sanctification" and immediately blesses with the cross: immerses it simply into the water, holding with both hands, and sings this troparion: "When in Jordan"[^352], and all the people sing with Him. "And the second time singing the same troparion"[^353], and all the people sing with Him. Then the server pours holy water onto a tray or into a sprinkler. The Priest turns his face to the west, holding the precious cross with his left hand, and with the right – the sprinkler, and sprinkles all the people with holy water. After this the choirs sing Glory, Both now: Stichera "Let us praise, O faithful", the procession returns to the church in the same way, and the Priest sprinkles on all sides[^354], and thus they enter the sanctuary through the Holy Doors: the Deacon with the Gospel, and after him the Priest with the cross. And when the Priest has sprinkled the entire sanctuary, the Deacon places the Gospel, and the Priest the cross on the Holy Table, in its place, and the Choir sings "Blessed be the name of the Lord", if there be Vespers with the Service of Basil; if Vespers – separate from the Holy Liturgy, then immediately the Great Dismissal of the Feast; at the end: Troparion, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the Feast, which both choirs sing together in the middle of the church, as at Vespers with the Service of Basil on 25 December.

And when the Priest has sprinkled the entire sanctuary, the Deacon places the Gospel, and the Priest the cross on the Holy Table, in its place, and the Choir sings "Blessed be the name of the Lord", if there be Vespers with the Service of Basil; if Vespers – separate from the Holy Liturgy, then immediately the Great Dismissal of the Feast; at the end: Troparion, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the Feast, which both choirs sing together in the middle of the church, as at Vespers with the Service of Basil on 25 December.

units.english_cohort_translation: This Synaxis can fall either on weekdays, or on a Sunday. Its service has the appearance of a Saint on 6 without Polyeleos, but with the Great Doxology. Vespers will be with an Entrance, in view of the Great Prokimenon of the Feast. Matins from the beginning to the canon – of small type, from the canon to the end – of great type. Here is the rule for both cases.

units.english_cohort_translation: Translation of the relics of Saint John Chrysostom Note In January fall five saints, whose memory we honor with Polyeleos without All-Night Vigil, that is 11 January – Ven. Theodosius, 17 January – Anthony the Great, 20 January – Euthymius the Great, 25 January – Gregory the Theologian, 27 January – Translation of the relics of Chrysostom, and since the *Triodion* can begin within the limits of 35 days, from 11 January to 14 February, therefore these saints can fall either outside, or in the middle of the *Triodion*: in the middle of the *Triodion*, if the beginning of the *Triodion* falls on one of the days from 11 to 27 January; outside the *Triodion*, if the beginning of the *Triodion* falls on one of the days from 28 January to 14 February. And if they fall outside the *Triodion*, then their services are subject to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos; if they fall in the middle of the *Triodion*, they should have a separate rule, and since church books do not give it, we will give it.

And if they fall outside the *Triodion*, then their services are subject to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos; if they fall in the middle of the *Triodion*, they should have a separate rule, and since church books do not give it, we will give it.

In January fall five saints, whose memory we honor with Polyeleos without All-Night Vigil, that is 11 January – Ven. And if they fall outside the *Triodion*, then their services are subject to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos; if they fall in the middle of the *Triodion*, they should have a separate rule, and since church books do not give it, we will give it.

units.english_cohort_translation: St. Gregory and Chrysostom can fall not only with the Sunday of the Publican and of the Prodigal [Son], but also with the Meatfare, for when the *Triodion* begins on 18 or 20 January, then the Sunday of the Prodigal [Son] will be 25 or 27 January, and when the *Triodion* begins on 11 or 13 January, then 25 or 27 January will be Meatfare Sunday. These saints can fall also on the Saturday of Souls, that is Meatfare, which precedes Meatfare Sunday. If the *Triodion* begins on 12 or 14 January, then 25 or 27 falls on Meatfare Saturday. Chrysostom can fall also on Cheesefare Tuesday, which will be after Meatfare Sunday, for if 25 January falls on Meatfare Sunday, then 27 January will be Cheesefare Tuesday.

units.english_cohort_translation: If one of these saints falls outside the *Triodion*, one should adhere to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos. If he falls in the middle of the *Triodion*, as e. g. St. Theodosius can fall on the Sunday of the Publican, he must be transferred to another day. If one of the four other saints falls on the Sunday of the Publican, of the Prodigal [Son], Meatfare, on Meatfare Saturday or on Cheesefare Tuesday, then one must adhere to the rule of the Three Hierarchs, given in the *Menaion* on 30 January, which we will give immediately, with the exception of the All-Night Vigil, which will not be here, but there will be it at Great Vespers, at the end. Resurrectional Troparion, Glory: of the Saint, Both now: Resurrectional Theotokion according to the tone of the Saint. At Compline, after *“It is truly meet”* – Kontakion of the Saint, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the *Triodion*[^361].

units.english_cohort_translation: Note Our and Russian church rules do not give for this case All-Night Vigil, and consequently neither Small Vespers, but only one Great, without blessing of loaves; afterwards also Compline, at which after *“It is truly meet”* – Kontakion of the Saints. All this according to the rule of the Forerunner on 24 February[^365]. However, since with us even in this case All-Night Vigil is served, although there is no rule for it, we will give the rule of the All-Night Vigil also for this case, similarly to the rule of the Meeting on 2 February, if it falls on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday of Cheesefare week.

units.english_cohort_translation: Note If the Three Hierarchs fall on one of the days of Cheesefare week, then the three-ode canon of Matins we sing at Compline, namely: if the Feast is on Monday, then at Compline on Sunday; if on Tuesday, then on Wednesday; if on Wednesday, then on Thursday; if on Thursday, then on Tuesday; if on Friday, then on Wednesday. Thus give our and Russian typikons for the Feast of the Meeting on these days. Only, if the Feast falls on Monday, let the three-ode canon be sung on Tuesday, for when there is All-Night Vigil – Compline does not happen.

units.english_cohort_translation: Meeting of the Lord Note This feast falls on 2 February and therefore can fall either in the middle, or outside the *Triodion*. And since the first boundary of the *Triodion* is 11 January, and the last – 14 February, therefore it can fall at most 22 days from the beginning of the *Triodion* and 12 days before the beginning of the *Triodion*. When there is the earliest boundary of the *Triodion*, that is 11 January, then the feast reaches Monday of the first week of Lent, the next – immediately after the fourth Sunday of the *Triodion*, that is after Cheesefare Sunday. And if it falls outside the *Triodion*, then its order is celebrated according to the general rule of a feast of the Theotokos, although partly it is of the Lord. It differs from a feast of the Theotokos only by a separate dismissal and at the Liturgy – by a separate entrance verse, and on the Apodosis there will not be the Apostle-Gospel of the Feast and of the day, as for the Theotokos, but only of the day, as for the Lord. And if it falls on a Sunday, its service is combined with the Resurrectional, according to the rule of a feast of the Theotokos. It has one day of Forefeast and seven days of Afterfeast, for it is given up on 9 February.

units.english_cohort_translation: When the Forefeast of the Meeting falls on Meatfare Saturday, then the service of the Forefeast we sing on the previous Friday with Saints Cyrus, John and Tryphon[^367], according to the general rule of two saints on 4 in the Forefeast, only at *“Lord, I have cried”* there will be stichera: of the Forefeast – 3 and to the Holy Unmercenaries – 3, and the stichera of Tryphon are taken in the morning at the Praises on 4; Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast[^368]. After them, at the Aposticha, – stichera of the Forefeast with their refrains. On Meatfare Saturday we sing the general order for the deceased.

units.english_cohort_translation: Everything according to the general rule of a Saint on 4 in the Forefeast, only at the Aposticha of Vespers, and also at Matins, there will not be stichera of the Forefeast, but idiomesa of the *Triodion* of the day twice and to the Martyr with general refrains; also Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast. And at Matins, after the 2nd Kathisma there will not be the Sessional hymn of the Forefeast, but of the *Triodion*. The canon, where the three-ode canon comes, will be of the Forefeast with Heirmos on 4, three troparia of the Saint on 2 and of the *Triodion* on 8[^369]; katavasia at the 3rd, 6th, 8th and 9th – Heirmos of the canon of the Saint. Generally, in those odes where the three-ode canon comes, there will be the Katavasia of the *Triodion*.

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: 95. Відтак всі співають Величання. Коли хор повторює Величання священик, перед яким іде диякон з запаленою свічею, кадить від чотирьох боків ікону свята або святого на тетраподі, св. трапезу, святилище, іконостас, співслужителів, обидва хори, людей і ще раз ікону свята, але тільки спереду. Якщо, однак, звичайне кадження відбувається перед Євангелією, тоді на Величаннях священик кадить лише саму ікону. Хор: „Слава” і знову Величання. Відтак служитель і співслужителі ще раз співають величання.

cohort_provenance.verbatim_source:

1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 4 stichera of the Feast

2. After the Prokimenon of the day – Paremia and Prokimenon of the *Triodion*

3. **Aposticha:** Aposticha of the *Triodion*, Glory, Both now: of the Feast

4. At the end: Troparion to the Fathers, Glory, Both now: of the Feast

units.slavonic_diplomatic:
Початок великодньої утрені
На великодній утрені кадження відбувається з особливою урочистістю.
units.english_cohort_translation: **At the Divine Liturgy** there will be Prokimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn to the Feast and to the Fathers, and in the Forefeast – both of the day, and to the Fathers. Apostle and Gospel both here, and there will be of the day and to the Fathers APODOSIS OF THE FEAST OF THE MEETING

units.english_text: **At the Divine Liturgy** there will be Prokimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn to the Feast and to the Fathers, and in the Forefeast – both of the day, and to the Fathers. Apostle and Gospel both here, and there will be of the day and to the Fathers APODOSIS OF THE FEAST OF THE MEETING

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source:
Початок великодньої утрені
На великодній утрені кадження відбувається з особливою урочистістю. Служителі, одягнувши найкращі ризи, як на Службі Божій, виходять перед престіл звичайним порядком і роблять поклін усі разом. Головний служитель дає 1-му служителеві Євангелію, а 2-му – образ воскресіння Христового, сам бере лівою рукою хрест, а правою (від диякона) – кадильницю· Кадить спочатку престіл, а після – служителів. Потім головний служитель, віддавши дияконові кадильницю, стає на своє місце. Всі вклоняються перед престолом і обертаються на схід, щоб вийти до притвору. Вихід відбувається за звичайним порядком старшинства під гомін дзвонів та зі співом пісні „Воскресіння Твоє, Христе Боже”. А порядок такий: свіченосці, священики, диякони з запаленими свічками, а за ними – головний служитель. Всім також роздають запалені свічки. У притворі стають усі перед зачиненими церковними дверми, як на понижчій схемі:

cohort_provenance.verbatim_source:
**At the Divine Liturgy**

there will be Prokimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn to the Feast and to the Fathers, and in the Forefeast – both of the day, and to the Fathers. Apostle and Gospel both here, and there will be of the day and to the Fathers

APODOSIS OF THE FEAST OF THE MEETING

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: служители одягнувши найкращи ризи як на служби божий
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Служителі, одягнувши найкращі ризи, як на Службі Божій, виходять перед престіл звичайним порядком і роблять поклін усі разом. Головний служитель дає 1-му служителеві Євангелію, а 2-му – образ воскресіння Христового, сам бере лівою рукою хрест, а правою (від диякона) – кадильницю· Кадить спочатку престіл, а після – служителів. Потім головний служитель, віддавши дияконові кадильницю, стає на своє місце. Всі вклоняються перед престолом і обертаються на схід, щоб вийти до притвору. Вихід відбувається за звичайним порядком старшинства під гомін дзвонів та зі співом пісні „Воскресіння Твоє, Христе Боже”.
units.english_cohort_translation: Note This Apodosis can fall either in the middle, or outside the *Triodion*. In the middle of the *Triodion*, if the *Triodion* falls on one of 30 days from 11 January to 9 February inclusive; outside the *Triodion*, if it falls on other five days, from 10 to 14 February. And if it falls outside the *Triodion*, then the Apodosis will be 9 February, according to the general rule of the Apodosis of a feast of the Theotokos; And in this case the Afterfeast has 7 days inclusive with the Apodosis. But if it falls in the middle of the *Triodion*, then the number of days of the Afterfeast from 7 can be reduced to 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0, and the reason for this – various services of the *Triodion*, with which it coincides. However, this reduction does not always take place in the middle of the *Triodion*, but only when the Apodosis of the Feast coincides with certain services of the *Triodion*, which are incompatible with the service of the Feast. Such are: Meatfare Saturday (of Souls), Meatfare Sunday, which is of the Last Judgment, Cheesefare Wednesday and Friday, which have a completely Lenten rule, and Monday of the 1st week of Lent, on which the day of 9 February can fall, and partially also Cheesefare Sunday. Generally one can establish such a rule: if Pascha falls on days from 8 April and earlier, and the *Triodion* – from 28 January and earlier, then the Apodosis of the Meeting will be 9 February, that is on the seventh day after the Feast. When in a given year the Apodosis of the Feast will be at its proper time, and earlier, when there will be no Apodosis at all, the following table, compiled according to the rules of Slavic menaia, will show.

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source:
Початок великодньої утрені
На великодній утрені кадження відбувається з особливою урочистістю. Служителі, одягнувши найкращі ризи, як на Службі Божій, виходять перед престіл звичайним порядком і роблять поклін усі разом. Головний служитель дає 1-му служителеві Євангелію, а 2-му – образ воскресіння Христового, сам бере лівою рукою хрест, а правою (від диякона) – кадильницю· Кадить спочатку престіл, а після – служителів. Потім головний служитель, віддавши дияконові кадильницю, стає на своє місце. Всі вклоняються перед престолом і обертаються на схід, щоб вийти до притвору. Вихід відбувається за звичайним порядком старшинства під гомін дзвонів та зі співом пісні „Воскресіння Твоє, Христе Боже”. А порядок такий: свіченосці, священики, диякони з запаленими свічками, а за ними – головний служитель. Всім також роздають запалені свічки. У притворі стають усі перед зачиненими церковними дверми, як на понижчій схемі:

units.english_cohort_translation: **3.6.4.1 Since the last boundary of the Triodion is 14 February, this feast always falls in the middle of the Triodion. If the Triodion is earlier, then this feast enters all the deeper into the Triodion and coincides with many Triodion services. Even more, this feast can coincide with other services, given in the Triodion from Wednesday of Meatfare Week to Tuesday of the 8th week of the Triodion, that is of the 4th of Great Lent, inclusive. The last boundary of the beginning of the Triodion is 14 February, and after subtracting from 14 February 13 days, which precede the beginning of the Triodion, 11 will remain, dividing which by 7, we will get in the quotient 1, with 4 in the remainder, that is one whole week and one not whole – the first four days; and since the first day of the first week is Sunday (for the Triodion begins on Sunday), then the first day of the second week will be Sunday, the second – Monday, the third – Tuesday, the fourth – Wednesday. And since the first Sunday of the Triodion is the Sunday of the Publican, the second – of the Prodigal [Son], the third – Meatfare, then the Wednesday on which the Finding falls will be Meatfare Wednesday (for in the Lenten Triodion the days of the week are named after the following Sunday), as the earliest boundary of this feast in relation to the Triodion. And that the last boundary of this feast in relation to the Triodion is Tuesday of the 4th week of Great Lent is proven thus. The first boundary of the Triodion is 11 January, from which to 24 February will be 45 days, dividing which by 7, we will get 6 whole weeks with a remainder of 3; but, since the first day of this remainder is Sunday, as is the first day of each of the 6 past weeks, it will be the 7th Sunday of the Triodion, and the second day will be Monday, the third – Tuesday of the 8th week of the Triodion, of the 4th of Great Lent** The Service of this feast – of the type of a Saint with Polyeleos without All-Night Vigil, and since it coincides with services of the *Triodion*, it has 12 following cases FINDING OF THE PRECIOUS HEAD

The Priest, at the end of the readings, having closed the Holy Doors, takes off the phelonion 4. **Aposticha:** Aposticha of the *Triodion*, Glory: to the Forerunner, Both now: his Theotokion 5. **Troparia:** Troparion to the Forerunner, Glory, and now: Resurrectional Theotokion according to the tone of the troparion 6. Litany "Have mercy on us, O God" and Great Dismissal

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Compline** 1. **Canons:** Canons for the deceased of the *Octoechos* and sequential of the *Menaion* 2. If Small Compline is celebrated, as Greek typikons give, then after *“It is truly meet”* will be Kontakion to the Forerunner and Theodore. If – Great, as Slavic Triodia have, then after the 1st Trisagion we say the Troparion of both saints, after the 2nd – usual troparia "Have mercy on us, O Lord", and at the last Trisagion – Kontakion to the Forerunner[^385]

units.english_cohort_translation: 1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* At *“Lord, I have cried”* there will be 10 stichera: 6 of the *Triodion* and 4 to the Forerunner, Glory: to the Forerunner, Both now: 1st Theotokion according to the tone of the Doxastikon Immediately after the readings to the Forerunner – "Let my prayer be set forth" and according to the order Liturgy of the Presanctified. If the Finding falls on Wednesday, then after "Let my prayer be set forth" there will be also Prokimenon, Alleluia and Apostle-Gospel of the Forerunner, Communion Hymn "O taste" ("Vkusite") and of the Forerunner. If the Finding falls on Thursday, then on Wednesday evening there will be no Apostle-Gospel of the Forerunner, but it will be in the morning on Thursday

units.english_cohort_translation: > **Note:** On the Forefeast the typikon prescribes the Service of the Presanctified, as also on Saints with Polyeleos; however, with us the Service of the Presanctified is sung only on Wednesday and Friday, and on other days – of Chrysostom. When the Service of the Presanctified was supposed to be according to the typikon, but is not celebrated, then 3 stichera, which are at the Aposticha, should be transferred to *“Lord, I have cried”*, and after them sing both 3 prosomia stichera of the *Triodion*, and 3 of the Forefeast. On Wednesday evening the stichera from the Aposticha do not need to be transferred to *“Lord, I have cried”*, for they are already given in the *Triodion* at *“Lord, I have cried”*. c) On Wednesday evening, when the Forefeast is on Thursday Everything – according to the general Lenten rule of this day, only: At *“Lord, I have cried”*, after 6 stichera, which will be in the *Triodion*, also 3 of the Forefeast on 4; Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast.

units.english_cohort_translation: > **Note:** If the feast falls on Monday, then on Sunday evening it has two Vespers: one Small, and the second – Great with Matins, with which it comprises the All-Night Vigil; if the feast falls on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday, then on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday evening it has only one Great Vespers together with the Liturgy of the Presanctified, and afterwards – Great Compline with Matins, with which it comprises the All-Night Vigil. And since today with us the Liturgy of the Presanctified is celebrated only on Wednesdays and Fridays of Great Lent, we give for Vespers of this feast three rules: one – for Sunday evening, the second – for Monday, Tuesday and Thursday evening, the third – for Wednesday evening. a) On Sunday evening

units.english_cohort_translation: 1. **Kathisma:** After the 1st Kathisma there will be the Sessional hymn of the *Triodion*, without litany 2. **Canons:** Canon of the Feast, Heirmoi twice, troparia on 12, and where there is a three-ode canon, there will be 2 canons on 14, that is of the Feast with Heirmos on 6, of the three-ode canon on 8 and katavasia – Heirmos of the three-ode canon. At the 9th ode to the Heirmos and to the troparia of the Canon of the Feast we sing separate refrains, and to the troparia of the three-ode canon – "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"; also after the Katavasia we sing the Heirmos of the *Triodion* and of the Feast; the refrain and Heirmos both choirs sing together 3. After the stichera of the Praises – Small Doxology; Aposticha of the *Triodion*; Glory, and now: of the Feast. "It is a good thing" once, and after "Our Father" – Troparion of the Feast and litany "Have mercy on us, O God" with three great prostrations. This Matins ends just as the daily one, that is without dismissal

units.english_cohort_translation: We celebrate small without the canon, but after the "Creed" immediately – *“It is truly meet”* and after the Trisagion – Kontakion of the Feast; also after "God, have mercy on us" we make 15 prostrations, or 16 usual ones with the prayer of St. Ephraim "O Lord and Master"[^404]; and before "Spotless" we recite the concluding Trisagion with "Our Father" and "Lord, have mercy" (12) according to the rule of all Sundays of the Forty Days.
