slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: Тут головний служитель бере від диякона кадильницю і кадить ікони притвору, крилоси і людей. Диякон цілий час попереджує його з запаленою свічею. Відтак головний служитель вертається перед двері і кадить диякона; а тоді останній, взявши кадильницю від головного служителя, кадить його й відразу віддає кадильницю головному служителеві, який тричі кадить двері і тоді виголошує: „Слава святій”. Після „Амінь” головний служитель із співслужителями співає тричі „Христос воскрес” і стихи „Нехай воскресне Бог”, на які люди відповідають піснею „Христос воскрес”. Після останнього „Христос воскрес” головний служитель відчиняє двері (У нас тричі стукає хрестом) та входить у церкву, а за ним усі служителі й люди (див. ч. 71; Літургікон, стор. 141-146).

units.slavonic_text: Після останнього „Христос воскрес” головний служитель відчиняє двері (У нас тричі стукає хрестом) та входить у церкву, а за ним усі служителі й люди (див. ч. 71; Літургікон, стор. 141-146).
units.english_text: The Service of the Archangel is sung on another day or at Compline. The service of the Wednesday of the Veneration of the Cross and of the Feast we sing according to the general Lenten rule, only:

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: Тут головний служитель бере від диякона кадильницю і кадить ікони притвору, крилоси і людей. Диякон цілий час попереджує його з запаленою свічею. Відтак головний служитель вертається перед двері і кадить диякона; а тоді останній, взявши кадильницю від головного служителя, кадить його й відразу віддає кадильницю головному служителеві, який тричі кадить двері і тоді виголошує: „Слава святій”. Після „Амінь” головний служитель із співслужителями співає тричі „Христос воскрес” і стихи „Нехай воскресне Бог”, на які люди відповідають піснею „Христос воскрес”. Після останнього „Христос воскрес” головний служитель відчиняє двері (У нас тричі стукає хрестом) та входить у церкву, а за ним усі служителі й люди (див. ч. 71; Літургікон, стор. 141-146).

units.slavonic_diplomatic:
1. У співслужінні одного диякона
97. Згідно з прадавнім звичаєм Східної Церкви, при тому самому святому престолі можна служити тільки одну св. Літургію. Однак від цього правила можна відійти, якщо для користі вірних Божественну Літургію треба повторити.
units.english_cohort_translation: **At Matins** 1. **Canons:** Canons 2 making 10: of the Feast on 6 and of the Cross on 4, and where there is a three-ode canon, there will be 4 canons on 14, that is of the Feast on 4, of the Cross on 2 and 2 three-ode canons on 8; also Katavasia – heirmos of the three-ode canon[^406]. After the 3rd ode – Kontakion-Ikos of the Feast and Sessional hymn of the Cross, Glory, and now: of the Feast; after the 6th – Kontakion-Ikos of the Cross; at the 9th – "More honorable"; after the 9th – Triadikon Exaposteilarion.

Той самий хліб можна зберігати кілька днів й уживати його на кількох літургіях, за умови, що будуть дотримані всі церемонії проскомидії на ньому чи на його частині, краючи хліб і виймаючи агнця та частині, згідно з приписом.
units.english_cohort_translation: * *After the 3rd Ode:* there is no Resurrectional Kontakion-Ikos, but only the Sessional hymn of the Feast 2. **Praises (Lauds):** At the "Praises", after 4 Resurrectional stichera and 4 stichera of the Feast there will be also the 9th idiomelon of the *Triodion* with its refrain, also Glory: the same, Both now: *“Most Blessed Art Thou”*

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: 98.  Євхаристійний хліб не мусить бути безумовно спечений того дня, в який св. Жертва приноситься. Той самий хліб можна зберігати кілька днів й уживати його на кількох літургіях, за умови, що будуть дотримані всі церемонії проскомидії на ньому чи на його частині, краючи хліб і виймаючи агнця та частині, згідно з приписом. units.english_cohort_translation: > **Note:** Our handwritten typikon, *Tserkovne Oko* and others transfer the service of the Akathist to another time, for example to the 4th Saturday of Lent, or to the Sunday of the 5th week. The new Constantinopolitan Typikon transfers it to Thursday of the 5th week of Lent (of the Great Canon), which it transfers back, to Tuesday. The Pochaiv *Anthologion* and Moscow Typikon combine the service of the Annunciation with the service of the Akathist, and on Matins give a rule similar to the rule of the Annunciation on the Akathist Saturday, only the canon of the Akathist they prescribe on 6 and of the Feast on 8[^409].

units.english_cohort_translation: However, the service of the Annunciation is so great that it does not allow combination with another service, and the service of the Akathist is also great and long, so that it could be sung together with the feast, and therefore, it seems, we have quite serious reasons not to make this combination. Therefore, here too, the Akathist should be transferred to another day, namely, optimally to Monday, Tuesday, or Wednesday of the 5th week, at Compline[^407], and on Thursday we sing the great canon.

units.english_cohort_translation: 1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: 6 of the *Triodion* and 4 of the Feast; Glory: of the *Triodion*, Both now: of the Feast 2. **Entrance:** After the Entrance with the Gospel – 8 readings: 3 of the *Triodion*, the first two with their Prokimena, and 5 of the Feast, and immediately Prokimenon of the day of the *Triodion*; also Apostle, Alleluia and Gospel – of the day 3. At the Aposticha: stichera of the *Triodion*, only Glory: of the Feast 4. At the end, according to the rule of the *Triodion*: Troparion of the Feast, and then Glory, and now: "The noble Joseph"; but since according to the present custom the Bringing Out of the Shroud takes place and the Troparion "The noble Joseph" we sing after placing it in the prepared tomb, therefore one should sing only the Troparion of the Feast, and after the Bringing Out of the Shroud – Troparion "The noble"

units.english_cohort_translation: 1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Troparion "The noble" once and "When Thou didst descend" once, Glory: "Unto the myrrh-bearing women", Both now: of the Feast 2. After the Sessional hymn of the *Triodion*, which is before the canon, we sing the Polyeleos and everything else up to the canon – to the Feast, according to the general rule of a feast of the Theotokos 3. **Canons:** *Distribution:* Canons 2 on 16: of the Feast with Heirmos on 8, Heirmoi – twice; troparia on 6 and of the *Triodion* with Heirmos on 8, Heirmoi – twice.

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Small Vespers** Stichera at *“Lord, I have cried”* and at the Aposticha are taken according to the general rule of a feast of the Theotokos on Sunday. Prokimenon will be great "Who is so great a God as our God". At the Aposticha, after the Doxastikon of the Feast, will be Glory: "It is the Day of Resurrection"; also "Christ is risen" (3), Glory, and now: Troparion of the Feast; "Have mercy on us, O God" and Dismissal.

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Great Vespers** 1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: 4 of the *Triodion* and 6 of the Feast, Glory, and now: of the Feast 2. After the Great Prokimenon – 5 readings of the Feast and, if Sunday evening, then after "And that we may be accounted worthy" the usual Paschal Gospel is read 3. At the Litya: stichera of the Feast, and at the Aposticha: stichera of the *Triodion*, Glory: of the Feast, Both now: "It is the Day of Resurrection" and, after "Christ is risen" (3), Troparion of the Feast three times with the blessing of loaves 4. Instead of "Blessed be the name of the Lord" – "Christ is risen" (3) and Psalm "I will bless the Lord"[^415]

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Matins** 1. At the beginning, after the ending of the verses "Let God arise", we do not say Glory, and now: Troparion "Christ is risen", but Glory: Troparion of the Annunciation, Both now: the same 2. After the litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord" – Polyeleos with "Great Doxology", Post-Polyeleos Sessional hymn, Gradual of Tone 4, 1st antiphon and everything else up to the canon – according to the general rule of a feast of the Theotokos on Sunday, only "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" (3) and Ps. 50 are not taken 3. Paschal Canon with Heirmos on 6 and of the Feast with Heirmos on 8. Katavasia of the Feast. After the 3rd ode – Kontakion-Ikos of the Resurrection and Sessional hymn of the Feast, and other things, as in the previous case on p. 271

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 99 священик що хоче служити таинство повинен насамперед
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 99.  Священик, що хоче служити таїнство, повинен насамперед замиритися з усіма й не мати нічого проти нікого, по змозі зберегти серце від лукавих думок, вже від вечора бути стриманим і дотримувати посту до самого часу відправи та приготовлятись до жертвоприношення молитвами (див. ч. 190).

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: и диякон починае мовити слава тоби боже наш
units.slavonic_diplomatic: І диякон починає мовити: „Слава Тобі, Боже наш”, „Царю небесний”, „Святий Боже” (3), „Слава, і нині”, „Пресвята Тройце”, „Господи, помилуй” (3), „Слава, і нині”, „Отче наш”. Священик: „Бо твоє є царство”. Диякон: „Амінь”.
units.english_cohort_translation: **At Vespers** a) On Sunday evening 1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: 3 of the *Triodion*, 4 of the Feast and 3 of the Archangel, Glory, and now: of the Feast 2. Everything else – according to the Lenten rule of the *Triodion* on Sunday evening, only at the Aposticha – Glory, and now: of the Feast b) On Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday evening We sing without canon and without prostrations because there was All-Night Vigil, only after "More honorable" – 3 great prostrations with the prayer of St. Ephraim, 12 others and again one great with the whole St. Ephraim[^416].
units.slavonic_text: І диякон починає мовити: „Слава Тобі, Боже наш”, „Царю небесний”, „Святий Боже” (3), „Слава, і нині”, „Пресвята Тройце”, „Господи, помилуй” (3), „Слава, і нині”, „Отче наш”. Священик: „Бо твоє є царство”. Диякон: „Амінь”.

**At Vespers**

a) On Sunday evening

1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: 3 of the *Triodion*, 4 of the Feast and 3 of the Archangel, Glory, and now: of the Feast

2. Everything else – according to the Lenten rule of the *Triodion* on Sunday evening, only at the Aposticha – Glory, and now: of the Feast

b) On Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday evening

We sing without canon and without prostrations because there was All-Night Vigil, only after "More honorable" – 3 great prostrations with the prayer of St. Ephraim, 12 others and again one great with the whole St. Ephraim[^416].

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 102 увийшовши у святилище роблят перед святою трапезою
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 102.  Увійшовши у святилище, роблять перед святою трапезою три малі поклони й цілують: священик – св. Євангелію, а диякон – святу трапезу і, якщо існує звичай, обидва – напрестольний хрест.
units.english_cohort_translation: **At Matins** 1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Troparion of the Feast twice, Glory: of the Archangel, Both now: of the Feast 2. After the kathismata: Sessional hymn of the Feast 3. **Canons:** *Distribution:* Canons 2: of the Feast on 8 and of the Archangel on 6.
units.slavonic_text: 102.  Увійшовши у святилище, роблять перед святою трапезою три малі поклони й цілують: священик – св. Євангелію, а диякон – святу трапезу і, якщо існує звичай, обидва – напрестольний хрест.
units.english_text: **At Matins** 1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Troparion of the Feast twice, Glory: of the Archangel, Both now: of the Feast 2. After the kathismata: Sessional hymn of the Feast 3. **Canons:** *Distribution:* Canons 2: of the Feast on 8 and of the Archangel on 6.

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: 102.  Увійшовши у святилище, роблять перед святою трапезою три малі поклони й цілують: священик – св. Євангелію, а диякон – святу трапезу і, якщо існує звичай, обидва – напрестольний хрест. Прийшовши на місце, де знаходяться святі ризи, бере кожний з них до рук свій стихар і робить три малі поклони до сходу, кажучи кожний про себе: „Боже, милостивий будь мені грішному”.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 105 священик у правий частини святилища одягаеться так
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 105. Священик, у правій частині святилища одягається так: взявши стихар в ліву руку, робить до сходу три малі поклони, як про це було сказано і, благословляючи його, мовить: „Благословенний Бог наш”. Тоді одягає його, кажучи: „Нехай радіє душа моя”. Взявши епітрахиль і поблагословивши його, накладає на себе і мовить: „Благословенний Бог, що зливає благодать”. Взявши пояс, підперезує себе, кажучи: „Благословенний Бог, що перепоясує”. Накладаючи нарукавник на праву руку, мовить: „Десниця Твоя”, а на ліву: „Руки твої”. Тоді бере набедреник, якщо його має і, поблагословивши та поцілувавши його, завішує його над правим коліном, кажучи: „Перепояши меч Твій”.
units.english_cohort_translation: **At the Divine Liturgy** 1. **Troparia:** Troparion of the Feast and of the Archangel, Glory: Kontakion of the Archangel, Both now: of the Feast 2. Prokimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn – of the Feast; Apostle-Gospel – of the day and of the Feast; instead of *“It is truly meet”* – Heirmos of the Feast 3. APODOSIS OF THE ANNUNCIATION

units.english_cohort_translation: On Tuesday evening 1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: 6 of the *Triodion* and 4 of the Feast, Glory: of the *Triodion*, Both now: of the Feast 2. **Entrance:** 2 readings of the *Triodion* with their prokimena and the first 2 of the 5 of the Feast that are given at yesterday's Vespers, and also Small Litany with the exclamation of the Trisagion, and from here according to the order the Service of Chrysostom

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: Після цього священик бере лівою рукою просфору, а правою – святе копіє, робить ним тричі знак хреста над печаттю просфори і мовить тричі: „На спомин Господа і Бога”, відразу встромлює копіє у правий бік печаті, крає і мовить: „Немов ягня на заколення”, а в лівий: „І як агнець непорочний”, в горішній бік печаті: „У смиренні його”, в долішній: „А про рід його”. А диякон, спостерігаючи побожно це таїнство, кожного разу говорить: „Господеві помолімся”, тримаючи при цьому правою рукою орар. Потім говорить: „Візьми, владико”. Священик, встромивши св. копіє під спід правого боку просфори, виймає святий хліб і мовить: „Бо візьметься від землі життя його” і, поклавши його навзнак на святий дискос, після заклику диякона: „Жертвуй, владико”, крає його хрестоподібне і мовить: „Жертвується Агнець Божий” і обертає догори другий бік хліба, що має хрест. Диякон каже: „Проколи, владико”. Священик простромлює копієм святий хліб в горішньому правому розі, де витиснені букви „ІС”, кажучи: „Один з воїнів”.

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: Після цього священик бере лівою рукою просфору, а правою – святе копіє, робить ним тричі знак хреста над печаттю просфори і мовить тричі: „На спомин Господа і Бога”, відразу встромлює копіє у правий бік печаті, крає і мовить: „Немов ягня на заколення”, а в лівий: „І як агнець непорочний”, в горішній бік печаті: „У смиренні його”, в долішній: „А про рід його”. А диякон, спостерігаючи побожно це таїнство, кожного разу говорить: „Господеві помолімся”, тримаючи при цьому правою рукою орар. Потім говорить: „Візьми, владико”. Священик, встромивши св. копіє під спід правого боку просфори, виймає святий хліб і мовить: „Бо візьметься від землі життя його” і, поклавши його навзнак на святий дискос, після заклику диякона: „Жертвуй, владико”, крає його хрестоподібне і мовить: „Жертвується Агнець Божий” і обертає догори другий бік хліба, що має хрест. Диякон каже: „Проколи, владико”. Священик простромлює копієм святий хліб в горішньому правому розі, де витиснені букви „ІС”, кажучи: „Один з воїнів”.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 110 тоди священик бере в руки другу просфору
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 110. Тоді священик бере в руки другу просфору, однак якщо ані другої, ані інших просфор немає, закінчує приписані літургійні дії на одній, кажучи: „На честь і пам’ять” і, взявши частицю, кладе її праворуч святого хліба, поблизу від його середини, мовлячи: „Стала Цариця”.
units.english_cohort_translation: The Great Canon is transferred back to Tuesday. And here the service of the feast with the triodion is sung according to the Lenten rule given above, and at Matins the feast takes its apodosis.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 111 тоди взявши третю просфору мовит чесних небесних
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 111. Тоді, взявши третю просфору, мовить: „Чесних, небесних”, бере першу частицю, кладе її ліворуч святого хліба, починаючи перший ряд. Потім каже: „Чесного славного пророка, Предтечі”. Вийняту частицю кладе під першу і мовить: „Святих славних”, а тоді кладе третю частицю під другу, закінчуючи перший ряд. Потім каже: „Святих отців наших”; вийнявши четверту частицю, кладе її поруч з першою, починаючи другий ряд.

units.english_cohort_translation: 1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 4 Resurrectional stichera of the *Octoechos* of the current tone; Glory: to the Saint, Both now: Theotokion of Small Vespers of the *Octoechos*, according to the tone of the Doxastikon 2. Prokimenon Great of the day 3. At the Aposticha: one Resurrectional stichera of the *Octoechos*, also stichera of the Saint of Great Vespers, only Both now: to the Resurrection "It is the Day of Resurrection", "Christ is risen" (3) and immediately the Troparion of the Saint; Glory, Both now: Resurrectional Theotokion according to the tone of the Saint; "Have mercy on us, O God" and dismissal

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Small Vespers** Everything – according to the general rule of a Saint with All-Night Vigil on Sunday. Only at the end, on the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearers, there will be the Troparion to the Saint, Glory, and now: "The noble Joseph". On the Sundays of the Paralytic and of the Samaritan Woman – Resurrectional Troparion, Glory: to the Saint, Both now: Resurrectional Theotokion according to the tone of the Saint.

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Great Matins** 1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* At *“God is the Lord”*, if the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearers, Troparion Resurrectional once, "The noble Joseph" once, Glory: of George, Both now: to the Myrrh-bearing women. In other Sundays: Resurrectional Troparion twice, Glory: to the Saint, Both now: Resurrectional Theotokion according to the tone of the Saint 2. Everything else up to the canon is taken according to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos on Sunday, only "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" – three times 3. **Canons:** *Distribution:* Canons 3 on 14: Resurrectional with Theotokion on 6, that is Resurrectional on 4 and Theotokion on 2, of the Saint on 4 and of the *Triodion* on 4. (Since in the Canon of the *Triodion* there are many troparia, of which the first are – Resurrectional, and some – festal, that is of the Myrrh-bearers or of Arimathea, the penultimate – Triadikon, and the last – Theotokion, one Resurrectional and one of the Feast is taken, then the Triadikon and Theotokion).

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Great Matins** 1. From the beginning to the canon everything – according to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos in the middle of a Feast, only the first two sessional hymns will be of the Feast, and after the Polyeleos all three sessional hymns – of the Saint; after the Gospel – "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" once 2. **Canons:** *Distribution:* Canons 3 on 14: first of the Feast on 6, of the Saint on 4 and second of the Feast on 4.

units.english_cohort_translation: Holy Apostle James the Greater Can fall with services of the *Triodion* from Friday of Bright Week to Thursday after the Sunday of the Blind Man, the 6th after the Resurrection. It is celebrated according to the rules of St. George, here on p. 280, with the exception of the All-Night Vigil, as noted about St. Mark, 25 April. Although St. George does not reach the Sunday of the Blind Man like James, however, the Sunday of the Blind Man has the same rule as the three preceding Sundays, to which St. James reaches. But since on Wednesday after the Sunday of the Blind Man – is the Apodosis of the Resurrection, and on Thursday – Ascension, to which the rules of St. George do not reach, in these two cases one should adhere to the rule of the Theologian on 8 May, which we will give below, with the exception of the All-Night Vigil, which James does not have.

units.english_cohort_translation: **3.9.2 May: Appearance of the Sign of the Precious Cross in the sky in Jerusalem** and of the Holy Martyr Acacius The Service of this day – of small type, without Polyeleos, without Great Doxology and incomplete, for it has only a Troparion and Kontakion, stichera at *“Lord, I have cried”*, a canon at Matins, at the Liturgy – Apostle-Gospel and Communion Hymn to the Cross from 14 September, as our and Russian typikons and the Venetian *Menaion* give, according to others – only Troparion and Kontakion. It coincides with services of the Flowery *Triodion* from Friday before the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearers to Thursday before the Descent of the Holy Spirit.

Resurrectional Troparion and of the Fathers, Glory: of the Apostle, Both now: of the Ascension

At the blessing of loaves: Troparion "Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos" twice and of the Apostle once

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Great Matins** 1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Resurrectional Troparion once and of the Fathers, Glory: of the Apostle, Both now: Resurrectional Theotokion, according to the tone of the Apostle 2. Everything else up to the canon – Resurrectional, as usual, only, instead of "The Blameless", there will be Polyeleos with "Great Doxology" and after the Hypakoe – all three Sessional hymns of the Apostle 3. **Canons:** *Distribution:* Canons 3 on 14: Resurrectional with Heirmos on 4, of the Apostle on 4 and of the Fathers on 6.

units.english_cohort_translation: **At the Divine Liturgy** the Apostle-Gospel is read only of the Saint, and of the day is read on the previous day just as on Feasts of the Lord and of the Theotokos 1. Their service is not celebrated in one day, but in two; however, on the second day their service – is of the daily type and combined with the service of the *Octoechos* and of the sequential saint so, that the *Octoechos* takes the first place, the Forerunner or the Chiefs [of the Apostles] – the second, according to the rule of a Saint on 4, and the sequential saint – the third. units.english_cohort_translation: In relation to the Feast of the Co-suffering, with which these saints can coincide (for the rule has nothing), they are subject to the rule of the Theologian on 8 May, when he falls on the Feast of the Ascension, here on p. 295-296. However, since the Co-suffering does not have All-Night Vigil, at Small Vespers everything is sung only to the Saint, and at Great Matins all sessional hymns will be to the Saint, Glory, and now: of the Feast. Everything else up to the canon – only to the Saints. Canon of the Feast with Heirmos on 6 and to the Saints on 8. If 25 and 30 June, that is the second day of the Feast of these Saints, falls with the Co-suffering of the Most Holy Theotokos, then their service is taken at Compline.

units.english_cohort_translation: **On a Sunday** For the case of Sunday church books do not give a rule. We think that at Vespers, if there be no Polyeleos, at *“Lord, I have cried”* there should be 6 Resurrectional stichera and 4 of the Theotokos[^443]. If there be Polyeleos, then 4 Resurrectional and 6 of the Theotokos, Glory: of the Theotokos, Both now: Dogmatikon of the tone. At the Aposticha – Glory, and now: of the Robe. Troparia at the end of Vespers and at *“God is the Lord”* we end with the Troparion of the Robe, and at the Liturgy – with the Kontakion of the Robe.

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Great Matins** , if there be Polyeleos, from the Gradual to the canon everything only Resurrectional is sung, as usual. Everything else at Matins, at the Hours and at the Liturgy is sung according to the general rule of a feast of the Theotokos on Sunday. If there be no Polyeleos, then Sessional hymns of the Robe, of the Polyeleos and "Great Doxology" we do not sing. Everything else we sing according to the general rule of a feast of the Theotokos.

units.english_cohort_translation: **3.11.4 July: Dormition of St. Anne, mother of the Most Holy Theotokos** and memory of the holy women Olympias and Eupraxia Note Although even in ancient typikons the Service of St. Anne is given of small type with the service of the *Octoechos* and of the holy women[^446], however, with time it was honored with us with Polyeleos, and by the decision and decree of the Synod of Zamość, even with All-Night Vigil[^447] (although with us there is none, but only Polyeleos); and with the Greeks – Great Vespers with stichera at the Litya, and also Great Matins, from the canon and further[^448].

units.english_cohort_translation: Everything – according to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos, whether on Sunday, or on weekdays. units.english_cohort_translation: **3.12.1 August: Procession of the Wood of the Precious Cross** and memory of the Holy Martyrs Maccabees Note The Procession of the Precious Cross, which took place once in Constantinople from the imperial palace to the most beautiful church of Sophia, we depict now by the bringing out of the Precious Cross in the evening first from the sacristy to the Holy Table, and then, on the day of 1 August, from the Holy Table to the tetrapod, at Matins during the Doxology, when the Veneration also takes place, according to the rule of 14 September, on p. 120, except the Exaltation, which happens only on 14 September on the Exaltation of the Precious Cross, and here there will be none. Besides this, in Slavic books on this day also the Lesser Blessing of Water is prescribed either at Matins immediately before the Veneration, or later, at another time of the day. In some places also the blessing of herbs takes place, as on the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos[^454].

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Matins** Canon of the *Octoechos* on 4, of the Cross on 6 and of the Saints on 4. Katavasia after each ode – sequential "The Cross having been traced" (14 September). After the 3rd ode – Kontakion-Ikos and Sessional hymn of the Saints, only Both now: of the Cross; after the 6th – Kontakion-Ikos of the Cross; after the 9th – Exaposteilarion of the *Octoechos*, Glory: of the Saints, Both now: of the Cross 1. **Praises (Lauds):** 6: 3 of the Cross and 3 of the Saints, Glory: of the Saints, Both now: of the Cross 2. During the singing of the Praises the Priest, having vested in all sacred vestments (of violet color)[^455]  and having exclaimed before the steps of the Holy Table: "Glory to Thee, Who Hast shown us the light", and having censed the precious Cross, carries it out around the Holy Table through the northern doors before the Holy Doors, and after the end of the Great Doxology with the Trisagion, exclaims: "Wisdom, attend", goes before the tetrapod and, having placed the precious Cross on it, when the Choir sings the Troparion "Save, O Lord", censes it from four sides and venerates the precious Cross, everything exactly as on 14 September, here on p. 122-127

units.english_cohort_translation: 3. The Blessing of Water, if it be outside Matins, is celebrated whole just as you have in the Trebnik. The Blessing of Herbs, if there be any, usually takes place at the Liturgy after the Prayer behind the Ambo just as on the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos

units.english_cohort_translation: **3.12.1.1.9 On Saturday evening, after the Dismissal of Vespers the Bringing Out of the Precious Cross from the sacristy to the Holy Table takes place, and at Matins, during the Great Doxology, from the Holy Table to the tetrapod, according to the rule of 14 September. However, after the exclamation "Wisdom, attend", instead of the Troparion "Save, O Lord", we sing the Resurrectional Troparion, one of the two usual ones, at which the Priest should cense the Precious Cross from four sides and immediately after this perform the veneration of the Precious Cross, singing the Troparion "Before Thy Cross we bow down", or before the veneration perform also the rite of the Blessing of Water, according to the rule given here for weekdays, no. 5**

units.english_cohort_translation: **At the Divine Liturgy** the entire service is taken first of the Sunday, and then – of the Cross. The Service of the Saints, since it is without Polyeleos, is not taken. If someone would prefer to take it too, then Prokimena, Alleluia and Communion Hymns will be only two: to the Cross and to the Saints, and Apostle-Gospels – three: sequential, of the Cross and of the Saints[^456]

units.english_cohort_translation: Everything – according to the general rule of a Feast of the Lord, only after the Prayer behind the Ambo[^457], as Slavic typikons give, or after the Dismissal of the Liturgy, as the Peremyshl Trebnik gives, the Priest blesses on the tetrapod the first grapes (and since we have no grapes, then the first fruits) with one prayer, given in the *Menaion*, or with three, given in our Trebnik[^458], with censing and sprinkling them with holy water at the end.

units.english_cohort_translation: **3.12.4 August: Image Not-Made-By-Hands** and of the Holy Martyr Diomedes Notes The Service of the Holy Martyr is sung at Compline, and two services remain, that is of the Dormition and of the Image Although the service of the Image, as of the Lord, is greater than of the Theotokos, however, here the Theotokos one takes the first place The Service of the Image, according to the rule of our and Russian menaia, is on 6 and is celebrated according to the general rule of a Saint without Polyeleos on 6, with Praises and Great Doxology. It has also in the canon after each ode the sequential katavasia and, in Slavic books[^460], a separate Great Dismissal Although the Service of the Image – is without Polyeleos, nevertheless, at the Liturgy we do not omit it, as other services of Saints without Polyeleos of feasts of the Lord and of the Theotokos

At the end: Troparion of the Image, Glory, and now: of the Dormition 5. **Dismissal:** Separate Dismissal

units.english_cohort_translation: Everything – according to the rule of 24 June, however, by the decision of the Lviv Synod, must be transferred from a weekday to Sunday with All-Night Vigil. It is usually transferred to the following Sunday, only if the following Sunday falls on 1 September, then the service is transferred to the previous Sunday, so as not to coincide with three other services, that is Resurrectional, of the Indiction and of St. Simeon[^464]. The fast of the Beheading we do not transfer to Sunday, but keep on the very day of the feast[^465].

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Great Matins** 1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Sunday Troparion twice, Glory, Both now: Sunday Theotokion according to its tone 2. Everything else up to the canon is of the Sunday, as usual, only after the 50th Psalm, instead of Glory: "Through the prayers of the holy apostles" and the rest, at all odes of the Sundays of the *Triodion* we sing: Glory: *“Open to me the doors”*, Both now: *“Lead me on the paths of salvation”*, and after the verse "Have mercy on me, O God", the sticheron: *“Thinking upon the multitude”*

units.english_cohort_translation: > **Notes** The Synod of Lviv permits meat during this week, except on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, on the condition of [reciting] 5 "Our Father" and 5 "Virgin Theotokos" for the laity and Psalm 50 for the clergy. On the other three days, we use dairy products The divine services of this week approach the Lenten [order], however, gradually, for Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday have only certain parts in the *Triodion*, while all other parts are filled by the *Octoechos* and *Menaion*. Wednesday and Friday have in the *Triodion* a fuller order of Lenten character with prostrations[^472]. Saturday and Sunday, although they have a full service in the *Triodion*, nevertheless are not of Lenten form, as are all Saturdays and Sundays of Great Lent. The parts that Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday have in the *Triodion* are as follows: 1. Aposticha at Vespers and at Matins. 2. 2nd Sessional Hymn at Matins before the Canon. 3. Canon of the *Triodion*, usually double, that is, with two heirmoi The Odes of the *Triodion* triodion [three-ode canon] in the first five days of this week, as of all weeks of Great Lent, follow this sequence:

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Matins** 1. Instead of the 2nd Sessional Hymn of the *Octoechos*, it will be – of the *Triodion* 2. **Canons:** Canons: where there is no triodion [three-ode canon], there will be two of the *Octoechos* and one of the saint, as usual; but where there is a triodion, both canons of the *Octoechos* are omitted and the canon of the saint is sung alone or two together (if there are two) with heirmos on 6[^475] and both canons of the triodion on 8[^476]. The Katavasia will be after Odes 3, 6, 8, and 9, and also where there is a triodion, always the heirmos of the last canon 3. **Aposticha:** Aposticha of the *Triodion* with the usual verses of the *Horologion*

units.english_cohort_translation: Note In view of the Lenten form of the church services of these days, violet vestments should be used, since at Matins, instead of *“God is the Lord”*, "Alleluia" is sung on these days, as on the days of Great Lent; therefore, the Typikon prescribes three prostrations (small) at the beginning of Vespers at the Trisagion and at "O come, let us worship", and also after the pre-introductory psalm at "Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia, glory to Thee, O God"[^477], as well as after each of the three antiphons of the Kathisma (although now we read only the beginning of the Kathisma), after "Vouchsafe, O Lord", and after the Trisagion following "Now letteest Thou Thy servant depart". In addition to this, the Aposticha will be of the *Triodion*.

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Vespers** 1. From the beginning to the troparia after "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart", everything – according to the general rubric for a saint without Polyeleos on weekdays, however, with prostrations 2. After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart" with the Trisagion – 3 troparia, that is, "Virgin Theotokos", Glory: To the Baptist, Both now: "Intercede", each with a prostration at the end, and "Beneath Thy tender mercy", without a prostration 3. From "Lord, have mercy" (40) to the end, everything – as in the *Horologion*; however, at the last Trisagion and at "Blessed be the name of the Lord", which must be said before the psalm "I will bless the Lord", there will be three prostrations (small); and at the prayer of St. Ephrem – 16 prostrations[^479], that is, 3 great, 12 small, and again one great, as at the daily Midnight Office after "Thou Who at all times"[^480]. Dismissal with the usual commemorations of the service of the day and the saint > **Notes** on Prostrations 4. The prostrations we make at the three first troparia, according to the Typikon – are not great, but small, although due to ignorance of the rubric, or due to excessive piety, great ones are made among us. For here this prostration is called simply metanoia, and with the addition megale [great] it is given only at the prayer of St. Ephrem and never at the end of Vespers, after the litany "Have mercy on us, O God". Likewise at the Great Canon the rubric does not prescribe great prostrations, but simply metanoias 5. Neither Greek nor Slavonic rubrics give the form of the great or small prostration. However, according to custom it will be thus: he who makes a great prostration falls on his knees and touches the ground with his forehead; he who makes a small prostration does not fall on his knees, nor touches the ground with his forehead, but only crossing himself reaches the ground with his right hand, or only to the knees as the Synod of Lviv prescribes in Title V "On the Holy Liturgy", in the prayers before the iconostasis before the Proskomedia[^481]. We reach the ground with the right hand when we bow to the Holy Mysteries; only to the knees when we bow to holy icons, or at various supplications. However, our people in these parts do not have the custom, when bowing, to extend hands to the ground, or to the knees, but only crossing themselves to bow low before the Holy Mysteries, and higher – in other circumstances. We suppose, however, that at small Lenten prostrations we should reach the knees with the hand, for throughout the whole year at the Trisagion and at "O come, let us worship" we make prostrations, not reaching the knees with the hand[^482]

units.english_cohort_translation: AT Great Compline > **Note ** on Prostrations We make three small prostrations: 1. At each Trisagion (which will be five times), except the Trisagion after the supplicatory verses "O All-holy Lady", for immediately after them, before the Trisagion, follows "O God, absolve", at which there were already three prostrations. 2. At each of the three "O come, let us worship"[^483]. 3. At "Alleluia" after the first and second Trisagion. 4. At "O God, absolve" after the supplicatory verses to the Most Holy Theotokos. 5. units.english_cohort_translation: 1. From the beginning to the end of the litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord", everything – as usual for every day 2. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Instead of *“God is the Lord”* we sing Alleluia in the current tone of the *Octoechos* and the Trinity Hymns of the tone 3. Two Kathismata with the usual prostrations at "Glory"; after the 1st Kathisma – Sessional Hymn of the *Octoechos*; after the 2nd – Sessional Hymn of the *Triodion*, then Psalm 50 and immediately – Canon 4. **Canons:** *Distribution:* Canons 3 on 14: first of the *Octoechos* (the second of the *Octoechos* is not taken) with heirmos on 6, of the *Menaion* of the saint on 4, and of the *Triodion* on 4. In those odes where the triodion [three-ode canon] occurs, we sing the canon of the *Triodion* on 6 and both canons of the triodion together on 8, and one more separate troparion with the refrain "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", and instead of the * *Katavasia:* Katavasia it will be the heirmos of the second canon of the triodion. In the odes in which there is no triodion, we suppose that the * *Katavasia:* Katavasia will be the heirmos of the last canon, that is, of the *Triodion*, after each ode, as given in the *Triodion* on Cheesefare Friday, for these two days have a common rubric, although for Wednesday it is given imprecisely. The Canon of the *Octoechos* and *Menaion* in these odes, according to the rubric of the Greek Triodia, is omitted[^492]. The rubrics of the Slavs, for Whom the Greek length is not enough, prescribe transferring the odes of the *Menaion* canon to the preceding ones, in which the triodion has no place, and they sing on Wednesday the 1st ode of the *Octoechos* with heirmos on 4, the 1st and 3rd odes of the *Menaion* (without Theotokia) on 6 and the *Triodion* on 4. On Friday – the 4th ode of the *Octoechos* on 4, the 4th and 5th odes of the *Menaion* on 6 and the *Triodion* on 4. Similarly, the 6th ode of the *Octoechos* on 4, the 6th and 8th of the *Menaion* on 6 and the *Triodion* on 4. Also the 6th ode of the *Octoechos* on 4, the 7th and 9th of the *Menaion* on 6 and the *Triodion* on 4. The Biblical Odes in the Psalter we do not sing[^493]. To the troparia of the canon we chant the usual refrains (on [pp. 29-30](#refrains-to-the-odes-of-the-canon)).

units.english_cohort_translation: 1. Three small prostrations: at "O come, let us worship", at the Trisagions, at Alleluia after the three psalms, at "How shall we call Thee"; and at the prayer of St. Ephrem – 16 usual ones 2. After the conclusion of the three psalms with Alleluia, the troparion is sung, called also the Prokimenon, with two verses in the tone of the Prokimenon. "The appointed reader (or priest) sings in the middle of the church the Troparion 'In the morning' (at the 1st Hour, and at the others – the specific one), and we sing loudly the same and bend our knees to the ground. Exactly so at the other two verses and again the same troparion"[^496]. This bending of the knees is done three times: once – after the singing of the troparion before the verse, once – after the singing of the troparion after the 1st verse, and once – after the singing of the troparion after the 2nd verse[^497]. After singing the troparion with its verses, we say Glory, Both now: Theotokion and make three prostrations. (At the 6th Hour, immediately after the Theotokion, there will be the Troparion of the Prophecy and one reading of the Prophecy between two Prokimena in the *Triodion*)

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 117 писля видпусту проскомидии священик иде перед святу
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 117.  Після відпусту проскомидії священик іде перед святу трапезу, а диякон кадить проскомидійник тричі, потім святу трапезу від чотирьох боків, мовлячи потиху: „У гробі” і 50(51) псалом, після чого кадить запрестольну ікону. Виходить зі святилища північними дверми, приходить перед святі двері і, вклонившись перед ними, кадить ікони південної частини іконостасу, починаючи від ікони Спасителя, потім – ікони північної частини, починаючи від ікони Богородиці, а потім – хори, правий і лівий. Вірних кадить або з солеї, або, якщо існує звичай, ідучи через церкву до самого притвору.
units.english_cohort_translation: **At Vespers** > **Notes** 1. Since the five first weekdays of each week of Great Lent, that is Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday have a service of Lenten form, beginning from Sunday evening, we use sacred vestments of Lenten colors, according to the previous rubric – purple, according to the Synod of Lviv – violet 2. We do not make prostrations at Vespers of these Sundays from the beginning of Vespers, but from "Vouchsafe, O Lord". We make, therefore, three small prostrations after "Vouchsafe, O Lord" and at the Trisagion following "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart"; and 3 great prostrations – at the troparia, at "Virgin Theotokos" and at the prayer of St. Ephrem, without the 12 small ones 3. No Kathisma 4. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: 4 Penitential of the *Octoechos* of the current tone, 2 given at the Aposticha of Vespers and 2 at the Aposticha of Matins (which are taken from the *Octoechos* and given at the end of the *Triodion*), 3 of the *Triodion* and 3 of the *Menaion* of the saint; Glory: of the saint, Both now: Usual Theotokion in the tone of the Doxastikon; if none, then Glory, Both now: Theotokion from the *Menaion* - If two saints fall, we sing to one in the evening 3 stichera, and to the other the Stichera of the Praises on 4[^506].
units.slavonic_text: 117.  Після відпусту проскомидії священик іде перед святу трапезу, а диякон кадить проскомидійник тричі, потім святу трапезу від чотирьох боків, мовлячи потиху: „У гробі” і 50(51) псалом, після чого кадить запрестольну ікону. Виходить зі святилища північними дверми, приходить перед святі двері і, вклонившись перед ними, кадить ікони південної частини іконостасу, починаючи від ікони Спасителя, потім – ікони північної частини, починаючи від ікони Богородиці, а потім – хори, правий і лівий. Вірних кадить або з солеї, або, якщо існує звичай, ідучи через церкву до самого притвору.
units.english_text: **At Vespers** > **Notes** 1. Since the five first weekdays of each week of Great Lent, that is Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday have a service of Lenten form, beginning from Sunday evening, we use sacred vestments of Lenten colors, according to the previous rubric – purple, according to the Synod of Lviv – violet 2. We do not make prostrations at Vespers of these Sundays from the beginning of Vespers, but from "Vouchsafe, O Lord". We make, therefore, three small prostrations after "Vouchsafe, O Lord" and at the Trisagion following "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart"; and 3 great prostrations – at the troparia, at "Virgin Theotokos" and at the prayer of St. Ephrem, without the 12 small ones 3. No Kathisma 4. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: 4 Penitential of the *Octoechos* of the current tone, 2 given at the Aposticha of Vespers and 2 at the Aposticha of Matins (which are taken from the *Octoechos* and given at the end of the *Triodion*), 3 of the *Triodion* and 3 of the *Menaion* of the saint; Glory: of the saint, Both now: Usual Theotokion in the tone of the Doxastikon; if none, then Glory, Both now: Theotokion from the *Menaion* - If two saints fall, we sing to one in the evening 3 stichera, and to the other the Stichera of the Praises on 4[^506].

units.english_cohort_translation: On the first day of Great Lent we do not make prostrations at the Midnight Office, except three great ones at the prayer of St. Ephrem, and on other Lenten days we make 3 small prostrations: 1. At each of the three Trisagions. 2. At both "O come, let us worship". 3. At each Glory: "The Blameless"; also 16 usual ones at the prayer of St. Ephrem, that is 4 great and 12 small[^511].

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Matins** > **Note:** We begin prostrations from the Kathismata and make: 1. At "Alleluia" of each "Glory" of the Kathismata – 3 prostrations[^512]. 2. At "More honorable" of each of the 6 verses of the Song of the Theotokos – 1 prostration. 3. At *“It is truly meet”* – 1 prostration. 4. At "Glory to God in the highest" – 3 prostrations. 5. At the final Trisagion – 3 prostrations. 6. At the prayer of St. Ephrem – 16 prostrations, that is 12 small and 4 great.

units.english_cohort_translation: 1. From the beginning to the end of the litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord", everything, just as on every day 2. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Instead of *“God is the Lord”* we sing Alleluia in the sequential tone of the *Octoechos* 3. We sing three Trinity Hymns of the current tone, given in the *Horologion*, three for each tone. They are all sung three times with the refrain "Glory" to the second, and "Both now" – to the third. At each first one we make a commemoration of the weekday service, at the second – a commemoration of all saints, at the third – a commemoration of the Theotokos. However, since the weekday service of the week changes daily, and the troparia are sung the same each day of the week (except Saturdays and Sundays, on which, because they are not Lenten, the Trinity Hymns are not sung), at the end of each first Trinity Hymn a colon is given, which signifies that the troparion must be completed with the commemoration of the weekday service, the form of which is indicated at the end of the 3rd troparion of Tone 1

units.english_cohort_translation: Note These three commemorations we make also at the Exaposteilaria following the canon. But the Lenten Exaposteilarion has only one troparion in each tone, which is sung three times, therefore, when it is sung the first time, the commemoration of the weekday service is added to it, when – the second time, with the refrain "Glory", then – the commemoration of all saints, and when the third time, with the refrain "Both now", then – the commemoration of the Theotokos. These commemorations are added where the colon is given, that is before "And save me".

units.english_cohort_translation: 4. Three Kathismata with their Sessional Hymns, the Sessional Hymns of which, sung after the 1st Kathisma, are of the *Octoechos* of the current tone, given also at the end of the *Triodion*. The Sessional Hymns sung after the 2nd and 3rd Kathismata are of the *Triodion* 5. Psalm 50 and the first petition of the Great Litany "Save, O God", and after the exclamation "Through the mercy and compassion" immediately – the Canon 6. Odes and Canons. The Biblical Odes, given at the end of the Psalter, are intertwined with the odes of the canon, as given: before the ode of the canon the corresponding ode of the Psalter is recited, leaving its last verses for refrains to the troparia of the canon, in such quantity as there will be troparia in the ode of the canon, including the heirmos, except two, for to the penultimate troparion we refrain "Glory", and to the last – "Both now". The 2nd Ode is recited in full before the ode of the canon, and to the troparia of its canon we refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee". According to our ancient custom, the Odes of the Psalter are recited only in those odes in which the triodion occurs, and in the other odes we refrain the usual refrains to the troparia of the canon. The Greek Typikon prescribes singing the Odes of the Psalter in the tone of the *Menaion* canon, but now we do not even know what their melody was The Canons will be only of the *Menaion* and *Triodion*, for the *Octoechos*, according to the Greek rubric, during Great Lent is not sung, with the exception of Sundays. In some odes there will be 3 canons on 14, that is of the Saint of the *Menaion* with heirmos on 6 and both canons of the *Triodion* on 8: one on 4 and the second on 4. In some odes there will be only one canon of the saint on 4, and in the second ode there will be only two canons of the *Triodion* on 8, with heirmos on 9. This difference regarding the number of canons and their troparia in the odes arises because the *Triodion* canons do not occur daily in all odes, but in general only in three odes in the following sequence:

According to our ancient custom, the Odes of the Psalter are recited only in those odes in which the triodion occurs, and in the other odes we refrain the usual refrains

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 121.  Потім диякон, повернувшись знову на звичайне місце, співає: „Ще і ще”, а священик проказує потиху молитву третього антифону „Ти, що дарував нам”. Виголос: „Бо Ти благий”. Хор: „Амінь”.
units.english_cohort_translation: The Katavasia will be always the heirmos of the last canon either of the triodion, or of the *Menaion*: of the triodion where there will be a triodion, and where there will be only the *Menaion*, then the Katavasia of the *Menaion* will be only after Odes 3 and 6, for at the 8th and 9th there will always be a triodion and therefore there will always be the Katavasia of the triodion.

units.english_cohort_translation: A more precise example of the combination of the Odes of the Psalter with the Odes of the Canon is given at the 1st Ode in the Moscow Typikon, and is presented as follows: "After this we begin: 'Let us sing to the Lord' in the tone of the canon of the *Menaion* of the saint of the day and the verses of the odes are recited hurriedly, each Choir – its verse, until they reach 'The waters became thick' and from this they begin verses on 14, and we sing the *Menaion* with heirmos on 6. And we sing thus: the first Choir reads the verse 'The waters became thick' and sings the heirmos. The second Choir reads the second verse 'The enemy said' and, after it, – the troparion of the canon, and in sequence verses by choirs up to 'Then hastened'. From the verse 'Then hastened' we begin the triodion of Kyr Joseph on 4. And at 'The Lord reigning' we sing the 2nd triodion of Kyr Theodore the Studite, and one choir sings the troparion, and the second choir – the 2nd verse and the troparion. After this both choirs, having united, sing: Glory: Trinity Hymn, in a higher voice, Both now: Theotokion. Then we sing in the highest voice: 'Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee', and we sing the other troparion of Theodore, because the ode has 5 troparia. At the end we sing the Katavasia – heirmos of the second canon"[^515].

units.english_cohort_translation: Regarding the refrains to the troparia of the canon, know that in order to find the number of refrains as quickly as possible, the last four, six, and eight verses of the Biblical Odes (except the 2nd, for it is read in full before the heirmos) from the bottom up are marked in the middle of the song, or on the side, with the inscription: "on 4, on 6, on 8". But on 14 they are not counted off, since 6 verses from 8 upwards are easily counted. However, the counting of 14 verses in current Psalters does not coincide exactly with the counting in previous Psalters, for where the rubrics place the 14th verse at "The waters became thick", current Psalters place the 14th verse at "The enemy said", and "The waters became thick" moves to the 15th verse. The 6th Ode has only 12 verses, so do not forget to divide these two verses of it on 4. The 9th Ode, one, of the Theotokos, is sung whole before the heirmos with "More honorable", and the other, of Zachariah, is sung whole in the refrains, and in those editions where there are only 13 verses, one verse must be divided into 2.

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: 122.  Співається третій антифон або Блаженні, якщо неділя. Коли співці дійдуть до „Слава” священик і диякон, що стоять перед святою трапезою, роблять три малі поклони. Тоді священик бере святу Євангелію, дає її дияконові й опускає вниз фелон. Обидва обходять з правого боку святу трапезу і, вийшовши північними дверми, попереджувані свіченосцями, роблять малий вхід. Прийшовши перед святі двері, свіченосці стають по протилежних боках: один – біля ікони Богородиці, а другий – Спасителя, священик – посередині, а диякон – трохи попереду нього, праворуч. Обидва схиляють голови і диякон тихим голосом каже: „Господеві помолімся”, а священик проказує потиху молитву входу „Владико, Господи Боже наш”.

units.slavonic_incipit: По закінченні молитви диякон тихим голосом
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: закинченни молитви диякон тихим голосом каже до
units.slavonic_diplomatic: По закінченні молитви диякон тихим голосом каже до священика, тримаючи трьома пальцями орар і вказуючи на схід: „Благослови, владико, святий вхід”. Священик благословляє до сходу і мовить: „Благословенний вхід”. Тоді диякон подає священикові святу Євангелію для цілування. Коли закінчиться останній стих антифону чи Блаженних, диякон виходить на середину, стає перед священиком, підносить трохи руки і, показуючи святу Євангелію , виголошує: „Премудрість, прості”. Потім входять у святилище і диякон кладе св. Євангелію на престіл, а свіченосці, вклонившись разом перед св. дверми, вертаються на свої місця. Хор співає: „Прийдіте, поклонімся”, „Спаси нас... у святих дивний Ти...”, а якщо неділя: „Спаси нас... що воскрес із мертвих...”.
units.english_cohort_translation: 4. Selected verses from the Holy Scripture of the Old Testament, that is: at the 1st Hour – "Direct my steps", at the 3rd – "Blessed is the Lord God", at the 6th Hour – "Let Thy compassions come quickly", at the 9th – "Forsake us not". At the 1st Hour "Direct my steps" is divided into 4 verses, of which we sing the first 3 twice, and the 4th – three times. At the 6th Hour between the Theotokion and the Old Testament verses we sing the Troparion of the Prophecy of the *Triodion* and one prophecy between two Prokimena there 5. After the Trisagion, instead of the Kontakion, we read three Lenten troparia, according to the order of the Hours in the *Horologion*, adding to the 2nd "Glory", and to the 3rd – "Both now"

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 124 потим диякон каже до священика повели владико
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 124. Потім диякон каже до священика: „Повели, владико” і відходить на горне місце. Священик, ідучи, мовить: „Благословенний, хто йде”. Диякон: „Благослови, владико”, а священик: „Благословенний Ти на престолі” і благословляє горне місце.
units.english_cohort_translation: 2. The last prayer of the 9th Hour "O Master Lord Jesus Christ" is transferred to the Typika, to the place of the prayer "O All-holy Trinity", and the prayer "O All-holy Trinity" with the psalm following it is transferred, according to the rubric of our Pochaiv Triodion, to the end of Vespers[^519]. And on Wednesday and Friday, since Vespers will be with the Presanctified, "O All-holy Trinity" cannot be transferred to the end of Vespers, for it ends with the Liturgy and therefore remains in its place at the Typika, exactly so the prayer "O Master Lord Jesus Christ" remains in its place at the 9th Hour.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 125 по закинченни трисвятого диякон пидходит до св
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 125.  По закінченні трисвятого диякон підходить до св. дверей і, тримаючи трьома пальцями піднесеної правої руки орар, мовить: „Будьмо уважні”, а священик благословляє людей і виголошує: „Мир всім”. Тоді знову диякон: „Премудрість, будьмо уважні” і вертається до священика. Хор співає прокімен, псалом Давида.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 126.  Під час співання „алилуя” диякон, взявши кадильницю і насипавши до неї ладану, підходить до священика і каже: „Благослови, владико, кадило”. Прийнявши від священика, який каже: „Благословенний Бог”, благословення, кадить навкруги св. трапезу, ціле святилище, священика, ікони святилища, ікони іконостасу, обидва хори і людей (див. чч. 33 і 75).

units.slavonic_incipit: Диякон, віддавши кадильницю, підходить до священика
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: диякон виддавши кадильницю пидходит до священика и схиливши
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Диякон, віддавши кадильницю, підходить до священика і, схиливши перед ним голову та тримаючи пальцями орар, вказує на св. Євангелію і мовить голосно: „Благослови, владико, благовістите ля святого апостола”. Священик благословляючи його, виголошує: „Бог, молитвами” та передає йому св. Євангелію, а диякон відповідає: „Амінь” і, вклонившись святій Євангелії, бере її, виходить святими дверми, попереджуваний свіченосцями, що виходять бічними дверми, стає на амвоні або неподалік від св. дверей на означеному місці, там кладе св. Євангелію на аналой та читає її, обернений до народу.

units.slavonic_incipit: Священик стоїть перед престолом і, дивлячись
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: священик стоит перед престолом и дивлячис на захид
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Священик стоїть перед престолом і, дивлячись на захід, виголошує: „Премудрість, прості, вислухаймо святого Євангелія”. Потім благословляє: „Мир всім”. units.english_cohort_translation: On Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday of the first week of Great Lent, after "O come, let us worship", we recite Psalm 69 "O God, come to my assistance", given in the order of Great Compline after the 3rd "O come, let us worship", after the prayer "O Master God the Father"; then one fourth part of each ode of the Great Canon (Matins on Thursday before the 5th Sunday of Lent)[^524]. Refrain to the troparia of the canon – "Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me"[^525], to the troparion of St. Mary of Egypt – "Venerable Mother Mary, pray to God for us", and to the troparion of St. Andrew – "Venerable Father Andrew, pray to God for us". According to the rubric, 3 small prostrations should be made at each troparion of the canon, however, among us this is not done, since there are no people in church at that time The rubric for Great Compline we have partly here on page 327, and partly – in the *Horologion*.

Refrain to the troparia of the canon – "Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me"[^525], to the troparion of St. Mary of Egypt – "Venerable Mother Mary, pray to God for us", and to the troparion of St. Andrew – "Venerable Father Andrew, pray to God for us". According to the rubric, 3 small prostrations should be made at each troparion of the canon, however, among us this is not done, since there are no people in church at that time

The rubric for Great Compline we have partly here on page 327, and partly – in the *Horologion*.

units.english_cohort_translation: On Wednesday we make 3 small prostrations: at the Trisagion at the beginning, at "O come, let us worship", at "Alleluia" after the pre-introductory psalm and after each antiphon of the Kathisma and at "Let my prayer be set forth". Great prostrations, according to local custom, we make at "Light of Christ", when the Priest blesses the people crosswise with the triple-candle; at the conclusion of the singing "Let my prayer be set forth" and after "Now the Powers of Heaven", when the consecrated Lamb is taken from the artophorion and placed on the diskos[^526]. And on Fridays at Vespers and at Compline we do not make prostrations, only the prescribed ones at the Presanctified, that is: after "Let my prayer be set forth" – 3 prostrations[^527], after the Entrance of the Holy Gifts – 3 prostrations and at "Let my prayer be set forth" – 3 prostrations, and among us also at "Light of Christ" – 3 prostrations.

units.english_cohort_translation: At "O Gladsome Light" – Prokimenon of the *Triodion*, one reading of the *Triodion* and the second Prokimenon of the *Triodion*[^529]; then the Priest, having taken the triple-candle with the censer and exclaiming "Wisdom, Aright", begins "The Light of Christ", blessing with the triple-candle crosswise to the east, then, blessing to the west, says: "Illumines all"[^530]; all make three prostrations to the ground, and the Reader sings: "The Reading from Proverbs" and, when the Priest or Deacon exclaims: "Let us attend", reads the second reading of the *Triodion* 7. "Let my prayer be set forth". Has after it three verses and is sung six times, that is: twice – before the first verse, once – after each verse and again once at the end. And among us the first time "Let my prayer be set forth" is sung by the Priest, the second time – by the Choir, all three verses – by the Priest, after each the Choir – "Let my prayer be set forth", the last time in a higher voice up to the half – the Priest, and from the half – the Choir. Where there are two choirs, they sing "Let my prayer be set forth" alternately: the first begins after the Priest, and the second half is sung by both choirs together. When the Priest sings, he himself stands, and the Choir and people kneel; when the Choir sings, the Choir stands together with the people, and the Priest kneels. If there are two choirs, the one singing stands, and the other kneels; people who are on the side of the right choir kneel, stand and sing with the right choir, and those on the left – with the left[^531].

units.english_cohort_translation: The Priest sings "Let my prayer be set forth" first in front of the altar, then the 1st verse – on the south, the 2nd – on the west, the 3rd – on the north side, and at the end the first half – again in front of the holy table[^532]. He censes each side of the altar twice, that is before the beginning of his singing and at the end of the Choir's singing, that is at "The lifting up of my hands", for then, having censed, he moves to the next side of the altar, in order to cense there also, so that the Choir is ready to sing its verse[^533].

units.english_cohort_translation: Immediately after the end of the singing of "Let my prayer be set forth" is exclaimed "Let us all say" and according to the order – Liturgy of the Presanctified > **Notes** If there is no Liturgy of the Presanctified, then we sing Vespers according to the rubric of Monday, Tuesday and Thursday evening, that is from the 10 stichera on *“Lord, I have cried”* we transfer the first 3 to the Aposticha, and the other 6 we sing on *“Lord, I have cried”*[^534]; and there will be on Wednesday stichera of the *Triodion* – 3 and of the *Menaion* – 3, and on Friday Martyria of the *Octoechos* – 3 and of the *Menaion* – 3. On Friday evening, after "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart", there will be no Lenten troparia with prostrations, but the Troparion of the Saint, Glory, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones, in the tone of the Troparion of the Saint and, after the litany "Have mercy on us, O God", – 3 great prostrations[^535] and the Great Dismissal, as usual If on this day falls a saint with Polyeleos, namely the Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner and the 40 Martyrs, and also on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of Passion Week[^536], then immediately after "Let my prayer be set forth" there will be censing and on the two previously named feasts their Epistle and Gospel are read, the Gospel – beginning from "Wisdom, Aright". On the three days of Passion Week only the Gospel is read, beginning from "And that we may be accounted worthy", since there is no Epistle By the decision of the Synod of Lviv, the pastor must celebrate the Liturgy of the Presanctified on every Wednesday and every Friday of Great Lent and on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of Passion Week > **Note ** on the number of prostrations per day. The number of prostrations made in church reached once 300 per day, excluding the Midnight Office: "Three hundred during the day and night, without the Midnight Office". (Greek *Triodion*, our Manuscript Typikon and *Tserkovne Oko* on the 1st Monday of Lent).

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 129. Під час співання херувимської пісні диякон, взявши кадильницю й насипавши до неї ладану, підходить до священика, кажучи: „Благослови, владико, кадило” і, прийнявши благословення: „Благословенний Бог”, проказує 50(51) псалом і кадить навкруги св. трапезу, запрестольну ікону, ікони іконостасу, обидва хори і людей.
units.english_cohort_translation: **At Compline** Note Compline on all Fridays of Great Lent, according to the Greek rubric, is Small, and according to the Pochaiv *Triodion*, *Tserkovne Oko* and the Moscow Typikon – Great. However, in our times, when abbreviations prevail, we should adhere to the Greek rubric, the more so because even in our Horologia, in the order of Great Compline, troparia are given only for 4 days of the week, that is for Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. We do not make prostrations, as was already said on page 349.

units.slavonic_incipit: Після кадження диякон стає праворуч священика,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: писля кадження диякон стае праворуч священика тримаючи кадильницю
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Після кадження диякон стає праворуч священика, тримаючи кадильницю на перстеневому пальці лівої руки. Священик разом з дияконом, піднісши вгору руки, проказують херувимську пісню тричі, щоразу роблячи малий поклін.
units.english_cohort_translation: **At Compline** we sing the Canon for the Dead, which is in the *Octoechos* for the current tone, and the Canons of the *Menaion* to the saints of the nearest Saturday and Sunday we sing, if the Ecclesiarch prefers, one – at Compline on Friday with the Canon for the Dead, and the other – on Sunday at Compline[^540]. The Greek *Triodion* adds: "we do so on all Friday evenings of holy and Great Lent". Before the Canon for the Dead we should sing also the usual Theotokion Canon of the *Octoechos*, for the rubric does not exclude it[^541]

we sing the Canon for the Dead, which is in the *Octoechos* for the current tone, and the Canons of the *Menaion* to the saints of the nearest Saturday and Sunday we sing, if the Ecclesiarch prefers, one – at Compline on Friday with the Canon for the Dead, and the other – on Sunday at Compline[^540]. The Greek *Triodion* adds: "we do so on all Friday evenings of holy and Great Lent". Before the Canon for the Dead we should sing also the usual Theotokion Canon of the *Octoechos*, for the rubric does not exclude it[^541]

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: диякон мовит до священика визьми владико а священик
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Диякон мовить до священика: „Візьми, владико”, а священик бере великий покровець, що називається воздухом, і кладе його на ліве рамено дияконові, кажучи: „Піднесіть руки ваші”. Тоді бере святий дискос, огорнений малим покровцем, та ставить його з уважністю та побожністю на голову дияконові , а диякон, тримаючи кінець ораря лівою рукою, тримає дискос обома руками на голові. Сам священик бере в руки чашу, покриту малим покровцем, і тримає її перед собою. Обидва виходять північними дверми, попереджувані свіченосцями. Ці останні приходять до самих св. дверей і стають по обох їхніх боках.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 130 священик увийшовши св дверми ставит святу чашу
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 130.  Священик, увійшовши св. дверми, ставить святу чашу на престіл; бере також від диякона  святий дискос і ставить його на престіл, ліворуч чаші. Скинувши малі покровці з дискоса і чаші, кладе їх на престіл, а великим покровцем, тобто  воздухом, що його  бере  з рамена диякона і над кадильницею кадить, покриває святі дари, мовлячи: „Благообразний Йосиф”. Потім, взявши кадильницю з рук диякона, кадить святі дари хрестоподібне, кажучи: „Ущаслив, Господи” (див чч. 9, 20, 149).
units.english_cohort_translation: Note The service of this Saturday, as also the services of the 3rd and 4th Saturdays of Great Lent, differ from the services of Meatfare Saturday and the Saturday before the Sunday of Pentecost in that it does not exclude fully either the service of the *Menaion*, or the service of the day of the *Octoechos*, that is to all saints and the dead. The services of Meatfare Saturday and the Saturday before the Sunday of Pentecost exclude generally the service of the *Menaion*, and from the service of the *Octoechos* little is taken, but have their own order in the *Triodion* exclusively for the dead. Therefore, we suppose that the two litanies for the dead: "In peace let us pray to the Lord" and "Have mercy on us, O God", which according to our later rubric are given at Vespers and at Matins, and the litany for the dead "Again and again", which is said between the odes of the canon, should be taken only on these two Saturdays which are exclusively for the dead, and on the other three – usual litanies.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 131 виддавши кадильницю священик опускае фелон и схиливши
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 131.  Віддавши кадильницю, священик опускає фелон і, схиливши голову, мовить до диякона: „Пом’яни мене, брате і співслужителю”, а диякон відповідає йому: „Нехай пом’яне Господь Бог священство твоє”. Священик на це: „Помолися за мене, співслужителю мій”. Диякон, схиливши голову, тримаючи орар трьома пальцями правої руки, мовить до священика: „Дух Святий найде на тебе”. Священик: „Той же Дух”. Тоді диякон йому: „Пом’яни мене, владико святий”.
units.english_cohort_translation: 1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: Idiomelon of the *Triodion* of the day twice, 4 Martyria of the *Octoechos* and 4 of the *Menaion* of the saint, Glory: of the saint, if there be, but if not, then Glory: Sticheron for the Dead of the tone, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the departing tone 2. Instead of the Prokimenon of the day of the *Horologion* there will be Prokimenon of the *Triodion* and reading, second Prokimenon and second reading of the *Triodion*, then "Let my prayer be set forth" and the rest of the Presanctified > **Notes** 3. After the end of the Presanctified, in other services of this day (except the Panakhida for the dead) vestments of red color should rather be used, than black, for red ones are – predominantly for martyrs 4. If there be no Presanctified, then we sing Vespers according to the rubric given here, on page 347

units.slavonic_incipit: Священик обертається до народу і благословляє:
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: священик обертаеться до народу и благословляе мир всим
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Священик обертається до народу і благословляє: „Мир всім”. Хор: „І духові твоєму”. Диякон: „Возлюбім один одного”, а священик вклоняється тричі, потиху мовлячи: „Возлюблю Тебе, Господи” та цілує святі дари так, як вони покриті: спочатку – св. дискос, потім – св. чашу, а на кінці – край св. трапези перед собою. Диякон, зробивши три малі поклони на своєму місці та поцілувавши свій орар там, де на ньому знак хреста, виголошує: „Двері, двері” (див. ч. 200).
units.english_cohort_translation: 3. **Kathisma:** After the 1st Kathisma – Small Litany and Sessional Hymn of the *Octoechos* of the current tone 4. 17th Kathisma ("The Blameless"), in two stations, with refrains and troparia 5. **Canons:** *Distribution:* Canons 3 on 14: of the Temple of the Lord or Theotokos with heirmos on 6, of the Saint of the *Menaion* on 4 and of the *Octoechos* of the current tone the second[^547] on 4. If the Temple is of a Saint, then – Canon of the Saint with heirmos on 6, Temple on 4 and Octoechos on 4. From the 6th Ode, leaving the Canons of the Temple and Octoechos, we sing the Canon of the Saint of the *Menaion* on 6 and both canons of the tetraodion on 8. Refrain to the troparia of the tetraodion – "Holy Martyrs, pray to God for us". At the end of the eight troparia of each ode of the tetraodion we add two more troparia: one Martyric with the Martyric refrain, and the second – for the dead with the refrain for the dead. From the two Martyric refrains "Wondrous is God" and "To the saints that are in His earth" and from the two refrains for the dead "Their souls" and "Blessed are they Whom Thou Hast chosen", the first we refrain to the Martyric and for the dead of the 6th and 8th Odes, and the second – to the Martyric and for the dead of the 7th and 9th Odes.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 133 диякон станьмо гидно хор милист миру диякон
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 133.  Диякон: „Станьмо гідно”. Хор: „Милість миру”. Диякон, зробивши малий поклін, входить південними дверми у святилище, стає праворуч священика і, якщо треба, бере рипіду і повіває нею побожно над святими дарами. Якщо рипіди не буде – робить це малим (складеним) покровцем.
units.english_cohort_translation: After the 3rd Ode – Sessional Hymn of the Saint[^548], after the 6th – Kontakion and Ikos for the Dead, after the 9th – Exaposteilarion of the *Octoechos* (to all saints, Glory: to the dead).

Знову священик і диякон вклоняються низько, одночасно роблячи на собі знак св. хреста. 135. units.english_cohort_translation: 1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: 6 Sunday of the *Octoechos* and 4 of the *Triodion*; Glory: *Triodion*, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the tone 2. Sunday Aposticha; Glory, Both now: *Triodion* 3. At the end: Sunday Troparion, Glory: of the Cross, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones, in the tone of the Cross 4. **Dismissal:** "Christ our true God, Who rose from the dead, through the prayers of His most pure Mother, by the power of the precious and life-giving Cross, which we venerate today, through the intercessions of the holy, glorious and all-laudable apostles, of our venerable and God-bearing fathers and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for He is good and loves mankind"

units.english_cohort_translation: After the dismissal of the Liturgy, and also after the end of every service celebrated in church, from this day until the end of the 6th Hour of the following Friday, veneration of the Precious Cross takes place: the Priest, having come before the tetrapod, sings together with the people "Before Thy Cross we bow down" (3). If there be a sufficient number of people, the Choir sings the stichera of veneration until all have venerated, according to the rubric given on page 127, in the note[^549].

units.english_cohort_translation: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday of the fourth week of Great Lent Everything – according to the general Lenten rubric of the previous weeks, except the veneration of the Precious Cross, according to the previously stated. Only Wednesday and Friday differ from the other three days in that at Matins, instead of the Canon of the *Menaion*, they have the Cross Canon of the *Triodion*. Also at Vespers on Tuesday for Wednesday all 6 stichera on *“Lord, I have cried”* will be of the Cross; and the Canon of the *Menaion* on these two days we take at Compline.

units.english_cohort_translation: Note The service of St. John of the Ladder, which some later [typika] prescribed to sing on this Sunday, is usually not taken among us. And if someone, namely in monasteries, wishes to sing it, let him sing it instead of the service of the regular saint of the *Menaion*, according to the rubric for a saint without Polyeleos on 4, and let him take the service of the regular saint at Compline. According to this Typikon, the service of St. Mary of Egypt is sung on the fifth[^550] Sunday of Lent, but if someone wishes, he may sing it instead of the service of the regular saint.

units.english_cohort_translation: > **Notes** 1. The stichera, not only the two first, but also all others, we sing in the tone of the Idiomela, for of the three types of Prosomoia given in the *Triodion* at the other stichera, two in our Heirmologia we do not find; and the one which is given at the stichera of St. Andrew of Crete, although it is given also in the Heirmologia, nevertheless, today we do not use. The stichera of St. Andrew of Crete, in the Greek text are given according to the order and in the sequence of the 24 letters of the Greek alphabet 2. If there be no Presanctified, then the Idiomelon and Martyricon stichera on *“Lord, I have cried”* are not taken, but are transferred with their two refrains to the Aposticha 3. It is not good to neglect prostrations at the stichera of St. Andrew 4. At the entire divine service of this day we use sacred vestments of Lenten colors, as usual

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Matins** 1. From the beginning to the end of the Sessional Hymns of the *Octoechos*, given at the end of the *Triodion*, at the 1st Kathisma, we sing everything according to the general Lenten rubric, then Psalm 50 and immediately, having omitted the litany "Save, O God", the Great Canon[^551]. At the time of the singing of the canon the holy doors are opened and candles are lit on the holy table. Before the holy doors in cathedral churches a rug is spread, on which first the Bishop, if he be present, and then the other sacred ministers two by two, according to the rank of their dignity, at each ode make one great prostration, after the singing of each troparion of the ode of the canon. In our seminary, the seminarians make prostrations before the holy doors, and in the sanctuary, before the steps of the altar, all eight superiors make prostrations according to the rank of their dignity, one at one ode, by turn, and at the 9th Ode – all eight together, in epitrachelia 2. **Canons:** Canons two: one – the Great [Canon] of St. Andrew, of nine odes, the second – triodion, contains the 4th, 8th and 9th Odes, which also in these odes takes the first place. The odes of the nine-ode canon do not have an equal number of troparia and each of them has at the end two troparia to St. Mary of Egypt and one to St. Andrew of Crete. The triodion we sing on 10 troparia with the first heirmos, for the 2nd heirmos is not sung. Refrains to the troparia of the Great Canon are these: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", then "Venerable Father Andrew, pray to God for us", then "Venerable Mother Mary, pray to God for us". To the troparia of the triodion the refrain will be – "Holy Apostles, pray to God for us"[^552], because according to content they belong to the service of Thursday. At each troparion of the Canon of St. Andrew the rubrics prescribe three prostrations, but we make only one, however, great, and in cathedral temples the clergy makes prostrations only by turn and adapted to the nine odes of the canon. The choirs sing the canon in the middle of the church, each at a separate analogion, making at the troparia of the canon a small prostration. As Katavasia at all odes we take the heirmos of the last canon[^553]

The choirs sing the canon in the middle of the church, each at a separate analogion, making at the troparia of the canon a small prostration. As Katavasia at all odes we take the heirmos of the last canon[^553]
