units.english_cohort_translation: Note The service of this feast is of the small type; it has only the Katavasia at Matins after each ode and the Great Doxology and is combined with the usual service of Lenten Saturday and with the Temple Canon at Matins. The peculiarity of this feast lies in that at its Matins the whole order of the Akathist to the Most Pure Virgin Mary is sung, the 12 ikos-Kontakia of which are divided into four quarters, the first of which is sung instead of the Sessional Hymn after the first Kathisma, the second – instead of the Sessional Hymn – after the second Kathisma, the third – after the 3rd, and the fourth – after the 6th Ode of the Canon; the initial Kontakion is sung at the beginning and at the end of each quarter, and before the last singing of it – once more the first Ikos[^556]. This Matins, according to the rubric, is sung at the 4th hour of the night, but we sing it at the usual time[^557]. The service of the regular saint, according to the rubric of the Greek *Triodion*, is sung at Compline.

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Matins** 1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Troparion of the feast twice; Glory, Both now: once more 2. **Kathisma:** After the 1st Kathisma – Small Litany and the initial Kontakion "To the Directress" is sung by the Choir. The Priest, dressed in all sacred vestments of light color, opens the holy doors and censes everything as usual; then, having come to the altar, sings the first quarter of the ikos-Kontakia and, after its conclusion, the same choir sings once more the initial Kontakion "To the Directress". All rubrics at this singing prescribe standing; (and therefore this is called Akathist, that is non-sitting). The Choir sings the Kontakion in the middle of the church majestically and solemnly 3. **Kathisma:** After the 2nd Kathisma and after the 3rd and 6th Odes of the Canon, immediately after the Small Litany, the Priest sings the other three quarters of the ikos-Kontakia, and the Choir – the Kontakion "To the Directress" at the beginning and at the end of each quarter. At the beginning of each quarter the Priest censes everything just as at the beginning of the first quarter This Akathist order is celebrated usually at the altar. In the cathedral temple it is sung at the altar of the Mother of God, which is located in its right nave; and then the Priest censes the altar and everything else, as usual, and immediately, having left the holy doors open, goes out through them to the altar of the Most Holy Theotokos and sings there the Akathist order, censing from the altar at the beginning of each quarter the icon of the Mother of God, the sacred ministers, the choirs and the people. After singing the 4th quarter of the ikos-Kontakia the Priest returns to the sanctuary, closes the holy doors and goes to the sacristy, where he takes off the sacred vestments and, having put on the epitrachelion, continues the service of Matins.

units.english_cohort_translation: 4. **Canons:** Canons 2 on 12: Temple of the Saint with heirmos on 6 and of the feast on 6. Katavasia "I shall open my mouth" up to the 6th Ode. From the 6th Ode we do not take the Canon of the Temple, but we sing 3 canons on 14, that is of the feast on 6 and both canons of the triodion on 8 with the addition of two troparia, that is one Martyric with the refrain "Wondrous is God", and the second – for the dead, with the refrain "Their souls", and the Katavasia of the *Triodion*. Refrain to the troparia of the Canon of the Theotokos – the general "Most Holy Theotokos, save us", however, among us they like to refrain the acrostic of the canon "Container of Joy, to Thee alone it is fitting to rejoice". In Greek: "Vessel of joy, to Thee alone it is fitting to rejoice". Both the troparia and this refrain we sing to the melody given in the new *Heirmologion* on the Akathist Saturday

At the 9th Ode we sing "More honorable" and after the 9th – Exaposteilarion of the feast.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Священик молиться потиху: „Дякуємо Тобі”. Виголос: „Благодаттю і щедротами”. Хор: „Амінь”. І відразу священик читає потиху молитву „Зглянься, Господа”, а диякон, ставши перед св. дверми, опоясує себе орарем навхрест, якщо цього не зробив на молитві „Отче наш”.
units.english_cohort_translation: On Friday, which we mark as a solemn feast, let the Hours be celebrated in the morning in church, called Royal, and about noon – Vespers with the bringing out of the Shroud[^559], which, when it is brought out, is placed before the iconostasis in the so-called tomb, and there let it remain for constant veneration by the people until Resurrection Matins It would be very desirable that the pastors on the same day, after the placing of the Shroud, preach to the people at a convenient time a word on the passion and death of Christ It is also entrusted to the same pastors to celebrate on this Friday, after sunset, Tomb Matins in church, in view of the divine service of this day and in view of the solemn rites celebrated at its end

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 138 диякон робит малий поклин и входит пивденними
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 138. Диякон робить малий поклін і входить південними дверми у святилище та, ставши праворуч священика, робить ще раз малий поклін і каже: „Роздроби, владико, святий хліб”, а священик розламує його уважно і побожно на чотири частини в такий спосіб: насамперед поділяє його на дві частини і ту частину, яку тримає у правій руці, тобто ту, що має написи „ХС” і „КА”, кладе на дискос, потім ламає впоперек поміж буквами „ІС” і „НІ” частину, яку тримає у лівій руці і кладе частицю „ІС” вгорі дискоса, а частицю „НІ” – на лівий; взявши потім другу половину, ламає її посередині між буквами „ХС” і „КА” і частицю „ХС” кладе внизу дискоса, а частицю „КА” на правий край дискоса, щоб утворили частиці знак хреста на дискосі. Під час цього мовить: „Роздроблюється і розділюється”.
units.english_cohort_translation: On the first three days of Bright Week it is fitting daily to sing Matins, Liturgy and Vespers in church The Synod forbids all priests read liturgies throughout the whole Passion Week, and on the first three days of this week prescribes only the Liturgy of the Presanctified; on Great Thursday and Saturday – only the sung Liturgy, that is of St. Basil the Great with Vespers (Title IV, Chapter I. 3. 5). On Great Friday, with the exception of the feast of the Annunciation, the Liturgy should not be celebrated Note From this Saturday to the Sunday of Ap. Thomas inclusive only the *Triodion* is sung, and the *Menaion* – only if the Annunciation falls, and from Bright Monday to the Sunday of Ap. Thomas inclusive, if a saint with Vigil or Polyeleos falls. The Canons of saints without Polyeleos of these 16 days are prescribed for Compline, beginning from Monday of the 2nd week of Great Lent, as was noted above, on page 357.

Диякон робить малий поклін і входить південними дверми у святилище та, ставши праворуч священика, робить ще раз малий поклін і каже: „Роздроби, владико, святий хліб”, а священик розламує його уважно і побожно на чотири частини в такий спосіб: насамперед поділяє його на дві частини і ту частину, яку тримає у правій руці, тобто ту, що має написи „ХС” і „КА”, кладе на дискос, потім ламає впоперек поміж буквами „ІС” і „НІ” частину, яку тримає у лівій руці і кладе частицю „ІС” вгорі дискоса, а частицю „НІ” – на лівий; взявши потім другу половину, ламає її посередині між буквами „ХС” і „КА” і частицю „ХС” кладе внизу дискоса, а частицю „КА” на правий край дискоса, щоб утворили частиці знак хреста на дискосі. Під час цього мовить: „Роздроблюється і розділюється”.

The Synod forbids all priests read liturgies throughout the whole Passion Week, and on the first three days of this week prescribes only the Liturgy of the Presanctified; on Great Thursday and Saturday – only the sung Liturgy, that is of St. Basil the Great with Vespers (Title IV, Chapter I. 3. 5). On Great Friday, with the exception of the feast of the Annunciation, the Liturgy should not be celebrated

Thomas inclusive, if a saint with Vigil or Polyeleos falls. units.slavonic_diplomatic: 141. Опісля священик, нахилившись, бере у праву руку чашу, а в ліву малий рушничок, тримаючи його під підборіддям, і причащається з чаші Кров’ю, кажучи: „Чесної і святої крові Господа і Бога”. І обтирає свої уста, як також і край св. чаші, малим рушничком, кажучи: „Оце діткнулося уст моїх”.

units.slavonic_incipit: Диякон, піднісши св. дискос над св.
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: диякон пиднисши св дискос над св чашею уважно
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Диякон, піднісши св. дискос над св. чашею, уважно обтирає його губкою, якщо є звичай її вживати, так, щоб жодної окрушинки не залишилось на дискосі. Тоді, якщо нема вірних до причастя, покриває св. чашу рушничком і малим покровцем, а на св. дискос кладе складену звізду і складені покровці. І відчиняються св. двері.
units.english_cohort_translation: [^562]Everything – according to the general rubric of a feast of the Lord with All-Night Vigil without Litiya. It has everything proper to itself, and at the Liturgy – Antiphons and Entrance Hymn. However, before the Troparion of Flowery [Sunday] we sing yesterday's Troparion of Lazarus; only after the Great Doxology we sing the Troparion of Lazarus alone.

units.slavonic_incipit: Якщо будуть вірні до причастя, диякон,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: якщо будут вирни до причастя диякон поклавши до
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Якщо будуть вірні до причастя, диякон, поклавши до чаші ложечку, накриває її рушничком або її покровцем, або обома і, зробивши малий поклін, приймає її з побожністю від священика, підходить до святих дверей і, підносячи святу чашу, показує її людям, кажучи: „Зі страхом Божим і вірою приступіть”. Хор: „Благословенний, хто йде”. Священик іде за дияконом, бере від нього святу чашу і проказує молитву „Вірую, Господи”. Одночасно диякон бере з престолу дискос. По закінченні молитви священик відкриває святу чашу, покровець і рушничок тримає лівою рукою і причащає ложечкою, кажучи „Чесного, пресвятого”. Диякон підкладає дискос під підборіддя причасника.
units.english_cohort_translation: 2. The blessing and distribution of branches takes place, according to the rubric, immediately after the 50th Psalm, during the kissing of the Gospel. According to our custom, the blessing takes place after the 50th Psalm, and the distribution – during the anointing with oil (myrovanie), that is during the canon. And it takes place thus: When the Priest has sung the Gospel, he places it on the analogion near the tetrapod, between two candles lit on candlesticks. On the tetrapod are placed branches and prepared censers and sprinklers. The Priest approaches the tetrapod and at the time when the Choir reads the 50th Psalm, having put incense in and blessed the censer, censes the branches from the four sides of the tetrapod and, after the conclusion of the 50th Psalm, when the Deacon exclaims (if there be none, then the Priest himself) "Let us pray to the Lord", reads aloud (from the *Sluzhebnik* (lit. "Sluzhebnik") or from the *Triodion*[^563] ) the first prayer "O Lord our God", and the Choir responds: "Amen". Priest: "Peace be to all"; deacon: "Bow your heads unto the Lord"; and, after "To Thee, O Lord", the Priest reads the second prayer "O Lord God Almighty... unto ages of ages"[^564]; choir: "Amen"; the Priest sprinkles the branches with holy water, saying: "These branches are blessed and sanctified" and the rest; and, after singing the litany "Save, O God", with His right hand anoints the people, and with His left hand distributes to all the branches, which the Deacon solemnly hands to him, and if there be no deacon, then one of the church servers[^565]

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: Можна ще й так робити: диякон покриває св. чашу рушничком або її покровцем і, зробивши малий поклін, приймає побожно чашу від священика, підходить до св. дверей і, підносячи чашу, показує її людям, кажучи: „Зі страхом Божим і вірою приступіть”. Хор: „Благословенний, хто йде”. Диякон вертається до св. трапези, де ставить чашу, з якої скидає малий покровець. Священик бере св. чашу з ложечкою і рушничком, а диякон – дискос і виходять зі святилища; підходять ті, що бажають причащатися. Після молитви „Вірую, Господи”, що її проводить священик, вірні, з усякою побожністю і страхом, склавши на грудях руки навхрест, роблять малий поклін і один за одним підходять до причастя, або приймають його в інший спосіб, згідно з місцевим звичаєм. Священик, причащаючи, мовить до кожного причасника: „Чесного, пресвятого”.

units.slavonic_text: Хор: „Благословенний, хто йде”.
units.english_text: On Monday, Wednesday and Friday the Synod of Lviv prescribes a strict fast. On Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday it permits also dairy products (Title XI, part 4).

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: Можна ще й так робити: диякон покриває св. чашу рушничком або її покровцем і, зробивши малий поклін, приймає побожно чашу від священика, підходить до св. дверей і, підносячи чашу, показує її людям, кажучи: „Зі страхом Божим і вірою приступіть”. Хор: „Благословенний, хто йде”. Диякон вертається до св. трапези, де ставить чашу, з якої скидає малий покровець. Священик бере св. чашу з ложечкою і рушничком, а диякон – дискос і виходять зі святилища; підходять ті, що бажають причащатися. Після молитви „Вірую, Господи”, що її проводить священик, вірні, з усякою побожністю і страхом, склавши на грудях руки навхрест, роблять малий поклін і один за одним підходять до причастя, або приймають його в інший спосіб, згідно з місцевим звичаєм. Священик, причащаючи, мовить до кожного причасника: „Чесного, пресвятого”.

units.slavonic_text: По закінченні причастя вірних священик залишає ложечку в чаші й прикриває її рушничком.
units.english_text: **At Vespers** WITH PRESANCTIFIED

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: По закінченні причастя вірних священик залишає ложечку в чаші й прикриває її рушничком. Потім, повернувшись з дияконом у святилище, ставить святі Дари на св. трапезу, а диякон прикриває св. чашу її покровцем. Священик бере ще раз св. чашу і від святих дверей благословляє нею людей, виголошуючи: „Спаси, Боже, людей Твоїх”. Хор: „Ми бачили світло істинне”. І вертаються обидва до св. трапези.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 143 священик ставит св чашу на престил и
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 143. Священик ставить св. чашу на престіл і кадить її тричі, молячись потиху: „Вознесися на небеса, Боже”. Потім віддає дияконові кадильницю і, взявши св. дискос, ставить його дияконові на голову, а диякон, тримаючи його з побожністю спереду і дивлячись в бік святих дверей, нічого не кажучи, йде просто між св. трапезою та святими дверми до проскомидійника і ставить на нього св. дискос. Після цього на тому самому місці очікує священика. А священик, зробивши малий поклін і взявши св. чашу, обернений до святих дверей, дивиться на людей і каже потиху: „Благословенний Бог наш”, а потім виголошує: „завжди, нині і повсякчас”. Хор: „Амінь. Нехай сповняться уста наші”. Священик відходить до проскомидійного стола, після чого диякон кадить святі Дари і священика. Священик, поставивши святі Дари і зробивши малий поклін, вертається до св. трапези.
units.english_cohort_translation: > **Note:** If there be no Presanctified, then on *“Lord, I have cried”* we sing stichera on 6, and the three last we transfer to the Aposticha with the usual verses, singing the first twice. We make the Entrance with the Gospel and, after the second reading of the *Triodion*, we sing the Gospel, as above, and everything else with prostrations, according to the Lenten custom.

units.slavonic_incipit: На заамвонній молитві диякон стоїть праворуч
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: на заамвонний молитви диякон стоит праворуч и вказуе
units.slavonic_diplomatic: На заамвонній молитві диякон стоїть праворуч і вказує своїм орарем на ікону Спасителя. По закінченні молитви священик входить у святі двері і, відразу вертаючись до проскомидійного стола, проказує молитву на споживання святих Дарів „Сповнення закону”.
units.english_cohort_translation: 3. **Canons:** Canon only one: triodion on Monday and Wednesday, or diodion [two-ode canon] on Tuesday. Troparia – on 12, heirmoi – twice. We do not recite the [Biblical] Odes, but only the refrain to the troparia of the canon "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"[^572], then the Katavasia, heirmos of the canon once both choirs together. Before the Kontakion-Ikos the Priest sings the Small Litany; at the 9th Ode we do not sing "More honorable", nor *“It is truly meet”* after the canon, but immediately after the Katavasia – Small Litany and Exaposteilarion "Thy bridal chamber" twice, Glory, Both now: three times the same 4. **Praises (Lauds):** 4: of the *Triodion*, Glory, Both now: *Triodion*, Small Doxology and, after "Let us complete", – Aposticha of the *Triodion* and everything else with prostrations, as on the Lenten days of Great Lent
units.slavonic_text: На заамвонній молитві диякон стоїть праворуч і вказує своїм орарем на ікону Спасителя. По закінченні молитви священик входить у святі двері і, відразу вертаючись до проскомидійного стола, проказує молитву на споживання святих Дарів „Сповнення закону”.
units.english_text: 3. **Canons:** Canon only one: triodion on Monday and Wednesday, or diodion [two-ode canon] on Tuesday. Troparia – on 12, heirmoi – twice. We do not recite the [Biblical] Odes, but only the refrain to the troparia of the canon "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"[^572], then the Katavasia, heirmos of the canon once both choirs together. Before the Kontakion-Ikos the Priest sings the Small Litany; at the 9th Ode we do not sing "More honorable", nor *“It is truly meet”* after the canon, but immediately after the Katavasia – Small Litany and Exaposteilarion "Thy bridal chamber" twice, Glory, Both now: three times the same 4. **Praises (Lauds):** 4: of the *Triodion*, Glory, Both now: *Triodion*, Small Doxology and, after "Let us complete", – Aposticha of the *Triodion* and everything else with prostrations, as on the Lenten days of Great Lent

units.english_cohort_translation: 1. At the 1st and 9th Hours there will be no Kathisma, but it will be only at the 3rd and 6th 2. Immediately after the Theotokion "O Theotokos, Thou Art the vine" at the 3rd Hour and, after the corresponding Theotokia, at the other two Hours, the rubrics prescribe the reading of the Four Gospels, which today among us is read only in cathedral, or conciliar, churches[^573]. At the 6th Hour we read the Gospel not immediately after the Theotokion, but after the conclusion of the Troparion of the Prophecy and the Paremia with its Prokimena. The reading of the Four Gospels covers all the Evangelists, that is Matthew, Mark and Luke in full, and John – only up to the "Passion of Christ", that is up to "Now is the Son of man glorified", Section 46, verse 13.32. All the Evangelists, taken together, are divided into 9 readings, according to the number of the three Hours (3, 6, 9) and three days (Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday). Matthew is divided into 2 readings, Mark – into 2, John – into 2, and Luke – into 3. The first reading covers the first half of Matthew, the second – the second half of Matthew, the third – the first half of Mark, the fourth – the second half of Mark, the fifth – the first part of Luke, the sixth – the second part of Luke, the seventh – the third part of Luke, the eighth – the first half of John, the ninth – the second half of John. The rubric does not indicate where the first half of the three Evangelists and the first and second parts of Luke end. But since Matthew has 28 chapters, its half ends with the 14th chapter, Mark – 16 chapters, so its half ends with the 8th chapter, Luke – 24 chapters, so its first part ends with the 8th chapter, and the second – with the 16th. John, up to "Now is [the Son of man] glorified", has 12 chapters and part of the 13th chapter, therefore its half ends with the 6th chapter and part of the 7th The Priest, at the beginning of each reading, dressed in a phelonion of Lenten color, opens the holy doors and censes everything as usual, then, having come out through the holy doors to the analogion placed before the holy doors facing the people, on which stand two candlesticks with lit candles, reads from there the Gospel, beginning from "And that we may be accounted worthy". After the conclusion of each reading, having kissed the beginning of the reading and leaving the Gospel on the analogion until the end of the 3rd reading, he returns to the sanctuary and, having closed the holy doors, takes off the phelonion[^574].

units.english_cohort_translation: 4. Only one Kontakion of the *Triodion* 5. In Slavonic rubrics and the Greek Typikon of Sabbas, on Great Wednesday, instead of the dismissal the prayer "O Master most merciful" is given, which is at Vespers with All-Night Vigil, and in Slavonic ones – also the prayer of forgiveness for sins committed in Great Lent, and commemorations. However, these superfluous additions of the Greco-Slavs are unknown to the Greeks. The prayer "O Master most merciful" and the forgiveness may be retained perhaps only in monasteries. The commemorations, which are superfluous here, will be taken later, at the end of Compline and the Midnight Office, which have nothing in common with forgiveness for the sins of the Forty Days

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 145 по закинченни псалма и роздачи антидора священик
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 145. По закінченні псалма і роздачі антидора священик стає у святих дверях і, благословляючи людей, виголошує:  „Благословення Господнє на вас”. Хор: „Амінь”. Священик, обернений до сходу, мовить: „Слава Тобі, Христе Боже”.
units.english_cohort_translation: **At Compline** AND AT THE Midnight Office Everything – according to the rubric of Monday and Tuesday, here on [pp. 379-380](#great-monday-and-great-tuesday), only on Wednesday, after the dismissal of the Liturgy of the Presanctified, the prostrations in church cease, and in the cells are made until the ringing for Matins of the bright Resurrection of Christ[^575]. We, however, until the Resurrection of Christ make three great prostrations in church, at the end of the Divine Service, singing the verse "Though Thou didst suffer", and during the veneration of the Shroud, singing "The noble Joseph".

We, however, until the Resurrection of Christ make three great prostrations in church, at the end of the Divine Service, singing the verse "Though Thou didst suffer", and during the veneration of the Shroud, singing "The noble Joseph".

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 148 у видповидний час священик входит до церкви
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 148.  У відповідний час священик входить до церкви і, разом з обома дияконами, робить перед святими дверми три малі поклони до сходу. Потім роблять все так, як на Літургії у співслужінні одного диякона, і обидва відповідають священикові. units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 149 по видпусти проскомидии кадят диякони принесення трьома
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 149. По відпусті проскомидії кадять диякони принесення трьома вимахами, а потім ідуть разом зі священиком перед св. трапезу, мовлячи тихо: „У гробі плоттю” та інше, разом кадять її спереду, потім 1-й диякон –правий бік св. трапези, а 2-й диякон – лівий, і знову обидва разом – від сходу, потім – запрестольну ікону та інші ікони святилища, як також 1-й диякон – хрест, а 2-й диякон – ікону Богородиці, якщо вони будуть за престолом (див. ч. 33). Потім виходять зі святилища: 1-й диякон –південними, а 2-й – північними дверми. Прийшовши перед святі двері, кадять ікони іконостасу: 1-й диякон починає від ікони Спасителя, а 2-й – від ікони Богородиці, після цього 1-й диякон – правий, а 2-й – лівий хори.
units.english_cohort_translation: Note "It is fitting for the Priest on Great Thursday at the Liturgy to consecrate two Lambs, in order to consume one at Communion, and to place the other in the artophorion and keep in the tabernacle in the usual place until today (Friday)". Thus in our *Sluzhebnik*[^584]. Regarding the Lamb itself, which is to be kept in the tabernacle until the day of exposition, the Synod of Lviv orders that "it before consecration be fitted to its vessel, the so-called Melchizedek, into which it is well inserted and carefully wiped, so that afterwards crumbs do not fall from it; so that placed in such a way in the Melchizedek, it be consecrated at the Liturgy of one of the preceding days and kept in the tabernacle until the exposition itself". When the Priest prepares the Lamb at the Proskomedia, wishing to use it for exposition, he does not say over it the words "In remembrance of the Lord" etc., nor does He perform over it the sacred actions which are usually performed over the Lamb that is to be consumed at the same Divine Service, for it is considered only communicative; it is enough only to cut it, so that it would be convenient to break and consume it on another day.

По відпусті проскомидії кадять диякони принесення трьома вимахами, а потім ідуть разом зі священиком перед св. трапезу, мовлячи тихо: „У гробі плоттю” та інше, разом кадять її спереду, потім 1-й диякон –правий бік св. трапези, а 2-й диякон – лівий, і знову обидва разом – від сходу, потім – запрестольну ікону та інші ікони святилища, як також 1-й диякон – хрест, а 2-й диякон – ікону Богородиці, якщо вони будуть за престолом (див. ч. 33). Потім виходять зі святилища: 1-й диякон –південними, а 2-й – північними дверми. Прийшовши перед святі двері, кадять ікони іконостасу: 1-й диякон починає від ікони Спасителя, а 2-й – від ікони Богородиці, після цього 1-й диякон – правий, а 2-й – лівий хори. Вірних кадять один з правого, а другий з лівого боку чи з солеї, або, якщо існує звичай, – у самому храмі, йдучи до самого притвору, після чого входять у святилище: 1-й диякон – південними, а 2-й – північними дверми і кадять ще раз престіл спереду трьома вимахами і так само священика.

units.english_cohort_translation: From the usual beginning to the end of the troparion after "Alleluia" and from the Canon to the end of Matins everything – according to the rubric of Matins of Great Thursday, here on [pp. 383-384](#great-thursday---matins). Between the troparion and the canon there will be five Sessional Hymns, each of which has before it three antiphons of the Passion troparia, without Kathismata and small litanies, then the Beatitudes, Prokimenon and Psalm 50. Besides this we read 12 Passion Gospels: the first – after the troparion, the five following – after each of the five Sessional Hymns, the seventh – after the Beatitudes, the eighth – after the 50th Psalm, the ninth – after the Exaposteilarion, the tenth – after the Praises, the eleventh – after "Let us complete", the twelfth – after the Aposticha. After the singing of each Gospel we ring all the church bells and, after the twelfth Gospel, we do not ring until the Resurrection itself, but instead of bells we use wooden clappers. But it is better already at Passion Matins not to ring, but to strike clappers or boards, for Passion Matins is a time of sorrow, to which the joyful sounds of bells do not correspond. Also in Rome already at Passion Matins clappers are used.
units.english_text: From the usual beginning to the end of the troparion after "Alleluia" and from the Canon to the end of Matins everything – according to the rubric of Matins of Great Thursday, here on [pp. 383-384](#great-thursday---matins). Between the troparion and the canon there will be five Sessional Hymns, each of which has before it three antiphons of the Passion troparia, without Kathismata and small litanies, then the Beatitudes, Prokimenon and Psalm 50. Besides this we read 12 Passion Gospels: the first – after the troparion, the five following – after each of the five Sessional Hymns, the seventh – after the Beatitudes, the eighth – after the 50th Psalm, the ninth – after the Exaposteilarion, the tenth – after the Praises, the eleventh – after "Let us complete", the twelfth – after the Aposticha. After the singing of each Gospel we ring all the church bells and, after the twelfth Gospel, we do not ring until the Resurrection itself, but instead of bells we use wooden clappers. But it is better already at Passion Matins not to ring, but to strike clappers or boards, for Passion Matins is a time of sorrow, to which the joyful sounds of bells do not correspond. Also in Rome already at Passion Matins clappers are used.

units.english_cohort_translation: 3. From the usual beginning to the end of the litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord" everything – as at Matins daily 4. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Instead of *“God is the Lord”* we sing Alleluia in the tone of the following troparion 5. **Troparia:** Troparion "When the glorious disciples" twice, Glory, Both now: once more the same 6. When the troparion is sung the third time, the Priest vests in a violet phelonion, goes before the steps of the altar, bows to the Holy Mysteries and, having opened the holy doors, recites the prayer of the censer, after which, having blessed the censer: "Blessed is our God", censes around the holy table, then, having stood before the steps of the altar and bowed low, goes out through the holy doors before the iconostasis and censes the local icons, the choirs and the people and, having returned through the holy doors to the sanctuary, gives up the censer and, having again bowed low, sings the Small Litany without exclamation, then goes out through the holy doors to the analogion and exclaims: "And that we may be accounted worthy", "Peace be to all", "Wisdom, Aright" and the rest. The Choir, instead of "Glory to Thee, O Lord", sings "Glory to Thy Passion, O Lord"[^586]. Priest: "Let us attend" and reads the first Gospel. After the conclusion of the reading the Choir, instead of "Glory to Thee, O Lord", sings: "Glory to Thy long-suffering, O Lord"[^587]. The Priest, having kissed the beginning of the reading, returns to the sanctuary and, having closed the holy doors and bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, goes to the sacristy, takes off the phelonion and goes to his place All this – exactly so at the readings of the other Gospels, with the exception of the litany and censing, which according to the rubric of our Triodia and the Typikon of the Lviv University, will be only at the 1st Gospel and at the five Sessional Hymns, and the censing – only of the holy table. They give thus: "We do not sit at these Sessional Hymns, since the Priest censes the holy table, but we sing them standing"[^588]. Finally we consider that it is fitting to cense not only at the Sessional Hymns, but also at all other Gospels, for the censing takes place not for the sake of the Sessional Hymns, but for the sake of the Gospels, however, only the holy table (around), as our Triodia have, which mention the censing only of the holy table. Everything should be censed only twice, that is at the 1st Gospel and at the Canon, at the heirmos of the 9th Ode.

units.english_cohort_translation: If there be deacons, they remain from the beginning of Matins, dressed in dalmatic with orarion of violet color, in the sanctuary, at their places, until they begin to sing the third time the troparion "When the glorious disciples"; then they come out together with the Priest who will sing the Gospel, dressed in a violet phelonion, before the steps of the altar and, having bowed together with him to the Holy Mysteries, open the holy doors, cense everything as usual, as at the beginning of the Liturgy, return before the steps of the altar and, having given up the censers and bowed both together to the Holy Mysteries, go out, each through his door, before the holy doors and, again having bowed to the Holy Mysteries, stand there until the second deacon after the singing of the troparion sings the Small Litany; then, having bowed to the Holy Mysteries and having exchanged their places, they proceed to the analogion so that, when the Priest approaches the analogion, the first Deacon is on the right, and the second – on the left of him. When the Priest, having bowed to the Holy Mysteries, comes out through the holy doors to the analogion, the first Deacon exclaims: "And that we may be accounted worthy". Priest: "Peace be to all". Second deacon: "Wisdom, Aright. Let us listen". Priest: "The Reading from (Name)". First deacon: "Let us attend". Priest – reading. After the conclusion of the reading, the Priest kisses the beginning of the reading first himself, afterwards the Deacon who is on the right kisses [it], and after him the one who is on the left. All three return to the sanctuary: the Priest – through the central, and the deacons – through the side doors, stand together with the Priest before the steps of the altar and, having closed the holy doors and bowed all together to the Holy Mysteries, go to their places. At the other Gospels, since there will be no Small Litany, the deacons, having come out before the holy doors, bow and, having exchanged places, proceed to the analogion and, when the Priest stands between them, exclaim: "And that we may be accounted worthy" and the rest, as above.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 152 коли спивци що спивают третий антифон або
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 152. Коли співці, що співають третій антифон або Блаженні, дійдуть до „Слава” або до останніх стихів Блаженних, священик і диякони роблять три малі поклони. Тоді священик передає св. Євангелію 1-му дияконові, а сам розпускає фелон (див. ч. 34). Священик з 1-им дияконом обходять з правого боку св. трапезу, під час чого 2-й диякон бере кадильницю, і виходять всі північними дверми, попереджувані свіченосцями: першим іде, кадячи, 2-й диякон, потім – 1-й диякон, несучи св. Євангелію, а за ними –  священик. units.slavonic_incipit: До малого входу Перший диякон каже:
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: до малого входу перший диякон каже господеви помолимся
units.slavonic_diplomatic:
До малого входу
Перший диякон каже: „Господеві помолімся”, а священик проказує потиху молитву входу. По закінченні молитви 1-й диякон, вказуючи правою рукою на схід, каже до священика: „Благослови, владико, святий вхід”. Священик благословляє і 1-й диякон дає священикові св. Євангелію для цілування. По закінченні останнього стиха антифону чи Блаженних, 2-й диякон виходить на середину, а 1-й диякон, ставши за ним, виголошує: „Премудрість, прості”. Після цього всі входять у святилище, 2-й диякон віддає кадильницю, а 1-й диякон кладе св. Євангелію на св. трапезу .
units.english_cohort_translation: 9. Psalm 50 and the eighth Gospel 10. **Canons:** Canon – triodion, heirmoi – twice, troparia – on 12, Katavasia after each ode – its heirmos, both choirs together. After the 5th Ode – Small Litany and Kontakion-Ikos; at the 9th Ode we do not sing "More honorable", but only the heirmos "More honorable"[^593]; after the 9th we do not sing *“It is truly meet”*, but we sing the Katavasia[^594]; then – Small Litany and three times the Exaposteilarion with the refrain "Glory, Both now", as usual, then – the ninth Gospel 11. **Praises (Lauds):** Stichera of the Praises on 4, Glory: one sticheron, Both now: another, then – the tenth Gospel 10. "To Thee belongs glory"[^595], "Glory to Thee Who Hast shown us the light".

units.english_cohort_translation: On Friday morning, before the beginning of the Royal Hours, the Shroud and the most beautiful Book of the Holy Gospels is placed on the holy table. Before the holy doors is placed the Tomb of God, at which, according to the custom of the northern and western Latin churches[^598], the Holy Mysteries are exposed until the Resurrection of Christ itself. Our Sluzhebnyky prescribe placing on this Tomb the Artophorion with the Holy Mysteries. According to the custom of our archcathedral temple, the Holy Mysteries are exposed in a monstrance on the main altar. And the Tomb of God should be erected so that above it rises a cross without the Crucified One, with a cloth hung on its crossbar and with the instruments of Christ's passion, it should be decorated with costly carpets, surrounded by many candlesticks and lamps and vessels with small trees and flowers. The front board of the sarcophagus is covered with red damask, to which a cloth is attached, and to it afterwards the Shroud will be attached. The board itself should not lie horizontally, but slanted so that the Shroud attached to it would be visible and accessible for veneration.

units.english_cohort_translation: In the archcathedral church they are sung at 10 o'clock in the morning, together with the Typika and with Vespers[^599]. We sing everything according to the rubric of the Royal Hours of the Eve of the Nativity of Christ. However, since the Tomb of God is placed before the holy doors, the analogion of the Gospel is placed a little further from it, the analogia of other readings – further from it. And everything that on the Eve of the Nativity of Christ the sacred ministers recite before the holy doors, they now recite before the Tomb, but they do not cense the Tomb, since there is nothing in it yet.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: 155. Під час співання „алилуя” диякони, взявши кадильниці й насипавши ладану, підходять до священика і кажуть: „Благослови, владико, кадило” і, прийнявши благословення, кадять св. трапезу спочатку спереду, потім 1-й диякон – з правого боку, а 2-й – з лівого і знову обидва разом – від сходу, потім – запрестольну ікону та інші ікони святилища, 2-й диякон також – приношення, й обидва – все інше, за звичаєм.

units.english_cohort_translation: **At Vespers** > **Notes** 1. At this Vespers there will be an Entrance with the Gospel and, at its end, at the last sticheron of the Aposticha, – the procession with the Shroud and the placing of it in the Tomb 2. All actions that the sacred ministers at usual Vespers perform before the iconostasis, at this Vespers they perform before the Tomb of God 3. From the usual beginning to *“Lord, I have cried”* everything – as at Daily Vespers, without Kathisma 4. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* stichera on 6, Glory: one sticheron, Both now: another. Entrance with the Gospel 5. Instead of the Prokimenon of the day there will be Prokimenon of the *Triodion*, Paremia and third Paremia; then – third Prokimenon of the Apostle, Apostle, "Alleluia" and Gospel. At "Alleluia" there will be censing. "Let us attend. Peace be to all. Wisdom, let us attend" we exclaim only at the 1st and 3rd Prokimena. We begin the Gospel from "Wisdom, Aright". Instead of "Glory to Thee, O Lord" before the Gospel will be "Glory to Thy Passion, O Lord", and after the Gospel – "Glory to Thy long-suffering, O Lord", exactly so as at Matins 4. "Let us all say", "Vouchsafe", "Let us complete" and Aposticha of the *Triodion*.

units.english_cohort_translation: 5. At the last sticheron of the Aposticha, that is at "Thee, Who Art clothed with light", takes place the procession with the Shroud and the placing of it on the Tomb The sacred ministers, the Bishop and the four most worthy canons, who will carry the Shroud, vest in all sacred vestments of their rank, and the other canons and priests – only in epitrachelia and phelonia, some – only in epitrachelia, and two deacons – in all diaconal [vestments]. Lit candles are distributed to the canons and other priests in the sanctuary, and to the brotherhood – in the church. The sacred ministers approach the steps of the altar and bow low. The Bishop ascends to the altar, takes the Shroud, spread on the altar, and gives it to the four canons so that each holds it by one corner. Then the Deacon who is on the right ascends to the altar and, having bowed low, unlocks the artophorion, takes from there the pyx with the Holy Mysteries, places [it] on the (folded) antimension, takes from there the Lamb with the stand into which it is inserted, not touching it with his fingers, but holding by the stand, places [it] into the monstrance and locks it well. Having locked the pyx, he places [it] into the artophorion and, having bowed, locks it also; and places the monstrance on the antimension so that it faces the people, steps aside until the Bishop, kneeling, censes the Holy Mysteries three times, each time – with a prostration at the end, and, having taken upon himself the omophorion (aer), approaches the altar. Then the Deacon, having bowed to the Holy Mysteries, takes with both hands the monstrance and hands it to the Bishop, who before that makes a prostration. The Bishop turns to the right to the people, and when the singers begin to sing "Thee, Who Art clothed with light", goes out behind the clergy through the holy doors on the northern side of the Tomb into the church and, having entered under the canopy, surrounded by candle-bearers and preceded by two deacons who cense unceasingly, proceeds behind all to the church doors. In front goes the cross-bearer, then the banner-bearers, four girls icon-bearers, after them – the church brotherhood, the seminarians, the seminary choir, then, from the holy doors, – priests, canons, four sacred dignitaries who carry the Shroud, turned with feet to the people, and at the end – the Bishop with deacons who cense, and candle-bearers. The procession goes out of the church and turns to the right, that is to its northern side and, having gone around the church three times (or, as now they do there, – once), returns to the church. Those who carry the Shroud, and the other priests stand before the Tomb, and the Bishop with the deacons returns by the southern side of the Tomb, through the holy doors, to the sanctuary. The right deacon receives from his hands the Holy Mysteries and places [them] on the altar. The Bishop kneels and, having put aside the omophorion (Velum), censes the Holy Mysteries three times, each time bowing his head; the Deacon, having bowed, exposes the Holy Mysteries at the top of the tabernacle. Having bowed before the steps of the altar, all three depart: the Bishop through the central, the deacons – through the side doors before the Tomb. The Bishop receives the Shroud from the canons who hold it, and places [it] on the Tomb, and they fasten it to the Tomb. When the singers have finished singing "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart", the Trisagion and the rest with "Our Father", the Bishop exclaims: "For Thine is the Kingdom" and begins to sing with the servers the troparion "The noble Joseph"; at the end he makes with the servers a low bow, and all the people – a great prostration to the ground. Then the second time the same troparion – the second choir, and all – a prostration, as before. And where there will be only one choir, the first time the troparion is sung by the sacred ministers, the second time – by the Choir, the third time the half – by the sacred ministers, and from "wrapped [it]" and further – by the Choir[^601]. After the singing of the troparion and after the prostrations all kiss the Shroud, according to the order, having made before the kissing one prostration: first the Bishop, and after him – all other sacred ministers, according to the rank of their dignity. After this there will be the Great Dismissal, specific to this Saturday, after which the sacred ministers return to the sanctuary, leaving the holy doors open until the end of Bright Week, take off the sacred vestments and go out, and the people kiss the Shroud[^602].

units.slavonic_incipit: Тоді диякони, поклавши кадильниці на їхні
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: тоди диякони поклавши кадильници на ихни мисця пидходят
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Тоді диякони, поклавши кадильниці на їхні місця, підходять до священика і 1-й диякон виголошує: „Благослови, владико, благовістителя святого апостола”. Священик: „Бог, молитвами” і передає йому св. Євангелію, а 1-й диякон виходить св. дверми, стає на амвоні або на невеликій відстані перед святими дверми на означеному місці і там кладе на аналой св. Євангелію, що її буде читати, обернений до народу, а 2-й диякон виголошує зі святилища: „Премудрість, прості, вислухаймо святого Євангелія”.
units.english_cohort_translation: The icon of the Shroud is transferred on Holy and Great Friday from the sanctuary at the end of Vespers, while the Dismissal Troparia "The noble Joseph", etc. are sung, and is placed on a prepared table in the middle of the presbytery, where there are already and remain lit candles with vessels of flowers throughout the whole day until the hour of Matins of Great Saturday (which is celebrated on the evening of Great Friday).

units.english_text: Small Compline This Compline, as also the Midnight Office, we read in private. At Compline – the Canon on the Crucifixion of the Lord and on the Lamentation of the Most Holy Theotokos.

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: Тоді диякони, поклавши кадильниці на їхні місця, підходять до священика і 1-й диякон виголошує: „Благослови, владико, благовістителя святого апостола”. Священик: „Бог, молитвами” і передає йому св. Євангелію, а 1-й диякон виходить св. дверми, стає на амвоні або на невеликій відстані перед святими дверми на означеному місці і там кладе на аналой св. Євангелію, що її буде читати, обернений до народу, а 2-й диякон виголошує зі святилища: „Премудрість, прості, вислухаймо святого Євангелія”. Священик: „Мир всім”. 1-й диякон: „Від (ім’я) святого Євангелія читання”, 2-й диякон: „Будьмо уважні”. По прочитанні Євангелії каже священик 1-му дияконові: „Мир тобі, що благовістуєш” і 1-й диякон, наблизившись до самих святих дверей, віддає згорнену Євангелію священикові. І зачиняються святі двері (див. ч. 126).

units.english_text: **4.2.6 Matins of Great Saturday**

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: 156. Потім диякони виходять своїми дверми і стають на означеному місці, а 1-й диякон починає: „Промовмо всі”. Потім 2-й диякон: „Помоліться, оглашенні”. 1-й диякон: „Всі оглашенні, вийдіть”. 2-й диякон: „Оглашенні, вийдіть” і знову 1-й диякон: „Всі оглашенні, вийдіть. Щоб ніхто з оглашенних не залишився, тільки вірні. Хор: „Господи, помилуй”. 1-й диякон: „Заступи, спаси, помилуй”, „Премудрість”. 2-й диякон: „Ще і ще”, „Заступи, спаси, помилуй”, „Премудрість”. Після цього входять обидва до святилища. І відчиняються святі двері .

units.english_cohort_translation: > **Notes** This Matins we sing usually on Friday evening, after sunset, although the rubrics prescribe it at the 7th hour of the night The sacred ministers remain during Matins before the Tomb of God, where seats and a table with candlesticks and books are prepared for them. Sitting, they sing Matins from there: the priests – in epitrachelia and phelonia, and the deacons – in dalmatics of violet color From "Blessed is our God" to "O come, let us worship" exclusively everything – as usual at Matins; then after "Lord, have mercy" (12), without "O come, let us worship" the Priest immediately: "Glory to the Holy" and the Six Psalms up to *“God is the Lord”*, as usual 9. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Troparion "The noble Joseph" (2), Glory: "When Thou didst descend", Both now: "The angel stood by the tomb"[^604]

units.slavonic_incipit: По кадженні стають диякони по боках
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: кадженни стают диякони по боках священика тримаючи
units.slavonic_diplomatic: По кадженні стають диякони по боках священика, тримаючи кадильниці на перстеневому пальці лівої руки і разом зі священиком, піднісши вгору руки, проказують всі разом тричі херувимську пісню, після кожного разу роблячи малий поклін (див. ч. 129).
units.english_cohort_translation: Regarding the censing, we suppose that it is sufficient to cense only the Shroud (together with the Holy Mysteries, if they be exposed on the tomb), the choirs and the people[^605].

units.slavonic_incipit: Потім, якщо існує звичай, цілує священик
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: тим якщо иснуе звичай цилуе священик св трапезу
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Потім, якщо існує звичай, цілує священик св. трапезу і напрестольний хрест, а диякони – край св. трапези і, безпосередньо, попереду – диякони, йдуть до проскомидійника. Там священик, взявши кадильницю від 1-го диякона кадить святі дари.
units.english_cohort_translation: About the Encomia (Praises), in Greek Triodia called Engkomia (praise), let it be known that before each of them one verse of the Kathisma is sung, until all are finished; only the first troparion of each station (in the editions of Pochaiv Triodia also the second troparion of the second station) is sung without a verse both at the beginning and at the end of each station, with the exception of the third, after which the first troparion is not sung and the Small Litany is not recited, but immediately – "The Choir of angels" and, after the singing of it, – Small Litany.

units.english_cohort_translation: 11. **After the Great Doxology:** At the Great Doxology we make the Entrance with the Gospel and, instead of the one troparion after the Doxology, there will be one Sticheron of the Praises (Shroud [Epitaphios]), two troparia and three readings, that is one – of the Prophecy, one – of the Apostle and one – of the Gospel The Entrance takes place thus: During the singing of the Stichera of the Praises the Priest and deacons, if there be any, having bowed low before the Shroud, and simultaneously also before the Holy Mysteries, go to the sacristy and vest in all sacred vestments of their rank. During the singing of the Doxastikon also the other sacred ministers, who are before the Tomb of God, dressed in phelonia, having bowed low, depart to the sanctuary and, when the Priest with the deacons comes before the steps of the altar, stand together with him on both sides and bow all together to the Holy Mysteries. After singing the Praises [Stichera] the Priest exclaims: "Glory to Thee Who Hast shown us the light", then puts incense in for the left deacon and, when the Doxology ends, approaches the altar, takes from it the Gospel, gives it to the right deacon and, preceded by candle-bearers and the Deacon with the censer, they make the Entrance just as at the Liturgy. Having stood before the Tomb of God: the right deacon – on the right, and the left – on the left of the Priest, closer to the Tomb, the other sacred ministers – on two wings, a little at a distance, await the conclusion of the Trisagion and the sticheron "Come, let us bless". After the conclusion of the singing of the sticheron the first deacon, raising the orarion in the direction of the people, exclaims: "Let us attend", the Priest, blessing the people: "Peace be to all", the second deacon, raising the orarion: "Wisdom, let us attend" and we sing the Troparion "The noble Joseph" once. The first deacon places the Gospel on the analogion facing the people, the second gives up the censer and the Troparion of the Prophecy once[^607].

units.slavonic_incipit: Диякони, увійшовши через святі двері у
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: диякони увийшовши через святи двери у святилище стают
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Диякони, увійшовши через святі двері у святилище, стають неподалік від них по протилежних боках: 2-й – ліворуч, а 1-й – праворуч. Після слів „Всіх вас” входить священик у святилище і, підійшовши наперед з дияконами, ставить святу чашу на престіл, також бере від 1-го диякона св. дискос і ставить його на престіл ліворуч чаші; великим покровцем, що його бере від 2-го диякона і над кадильницею кадить, покриває св. дари, відтак бере з рук 2-го диякона кадильницю і кадить нею св. дари (див. ч. 130).
units.english_cohort_translation: Then again: "Let us attend. Peace be to all. Wisdom, let us attend", Prokimenon, Reading of the Prophecy, Second Prokimenon, Reading of the Apostle and "Alleluia", during which the deacons cense the Tomb of God, the present sacred ministers and the people. After this the first deacon: "Wisdom, Aright! Let us listen"; Priest: "The Reading from the Holy Gospel according to Matthew". Choir: "Glory to Thy Passion, O Lord". Second deacon: "Let us attend"; the Priest sings the Gospel, facing the people. After its conclusion the Choir: "Glory to Thy long-suffering, O Lord". Then the Priest, having kissed and closed the Gospel, leaves it on the analogion, and the first deacon sings the litany "Let us all say", and the second – "Let us complete our prayer" in full, as usual.

units.english_cohort_translation: 1. According to the custom of the archcathedral church, this Vespers begins at 9 o'clock in the day 2. On this day there will be only one Vespers, that is Great with the Liturgy of St. Basil and without All-Night Vigil, and after the Prayer behind the Ambo, or (as the rubrics prescribe) after the dismissal of the Liturgy, there will be the Blessing of Loaves, as usual at the All-Night Vigil 3. The form and rubric of this Vespers is the same as the Vespers on the Eve of the Nativity, here on [pp. 169-171](#24-december--royal-hours-and-vespers-of-the-eve-of-nativity), without *“Blessed is the man”*; only here, after "O Gladsome Light", there will be no Prokimenon, but immediately 15 readings, between which there will be no troparia, and at the 6th reading all verses of the Song of Moses are read with the refrain "For gloriously has He been glorified", and at the 15th reading the verses of the Song of the Three Youths are read with the refrain "Praise the Lord and exalt Him above all for ever". Instead of "Alleluia" we sing the last verse of the 81st Psalm with its other verses, in the form of a Prokimenon[^609]. Dismissal of Matins of Saturday 4. Although the service of the feast usually begins at Vespers of the preceding day and therefore the whole Resurrection service should be celebrated in bright vestments, nevertheless, since the Liturgy, with which Vespers is sung, is still of the Saturday day, in the part of the verses on *“Lord, I have cried”* we sing about the descent of the Savior's soul into hell and therefore from the beginning of Vespers we use violet vestments, and afterwards change them after the conclusion of the Apostle, at the verses instead of "Alleluia", in order to read the Gospel already in bright vestments 5. Throughout the whole Bright Week, beginning from the Vespers of this day, the Resurrection service is sung and, besides the stichera of the *Triodion*, are sung also the Resurrection stichera of the *Octoechos*, each day – in a different tone, that is on Sunday – in Tone 1, on Monday – in Tone 2, on Tuesday – in Tone 3, on Wednesday – in Tone 4, on Thursday – in Tone 5, on Friday – in Tone 6, on Saturday – in Tone 8, omitting Tone 7

units.english_cohort_translation: 5. At the end: "The noble Joseph" (3) with prostrations, as at Matins of Great Saturday, but the Shroud is kissed only by the sacred ministers, according to rank, and the Bishop, taking the Shroud from the Tomb, hands it to four canons and thus all the sacred ministers return to the sanctuary and four canons hang the Shroud behind the holy table over the High Place[^613]. Then they depart to the sacristy, take off the violet vestments and vest in all bright sacred vestments of their rank, and at this time in the church all candles are lit > **Note ** on the Shroud Regarding the time and place of the placing of the Shroud we do not find an ancient rubric, for this rite is later and different in different regions. According to the custom of our archcathedral church the Shroud remains hung behind the holy table, over the High Place, from Resurrection Matins to the Apodosis of the Resurrection inclusive, that is until Wednesday before the Ascension. According to the custom of our other churches, the Shroud, taken from the Tomb before Resurrection Matins, is placed on the holy table, where it remains during the whole Bright Week, and from the Sunday of Ap. Thomas to the Apodosis of the Resurrection – behind the holy table. According to others – it remains on the altar, the antimension with the Gospel is placed on it and the Liturgy is celebrated on it. However, it is better to place the Shroud behind the holy table, for lying on the altar, it is often significantly damaged by candles, from which wax drips on it.

units.english_cohort_translation: After the Shroud is taken from the Tomb of God and transferred to the sanctuary, the sacred ministers, having dressed in all the brightest sacred vestments of their rank, go out before the steps of the altar and, having bowed all together low to the Holy Mysteries, bend their knees and receive lit candles; so also the brotherhood in the church. The Deacon, who is on the right (or the Priest himself, if there be no deacons) approaches the middle of the altar and, having bowed low, places the Gospel on its right side, then, having taken the Holy Mysteries from the tabernacle and placed them on the antimension, steps aside a little, and the Bishop (or main priest), having censed the Holy Mysteries three times, as usual, and having taken upon himself the omophorion, rises, ascends the steps and, having bowed, receives the Holy Mysteries, after which turns to the people and begins to sing the sticheron "Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior". Under the joyful sound of all bells the procession around the church takes place, with everything, as was given on Great Friday at Vespers, here on page 394, except the Shroud, which now, by the decision of bl. m. Cardinal Sembratovych, should not be carried, for this does not correspond to the joy of the Resurrection; rather it is fitting to carry the icon of the Resurrection, as it is in the *Triodion*, at the beginning of Resurrection Matins, during the procession to the church doors. Therefore, when the main sacred minister begins to sing the sticheron "Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior", the choirs and people take up the singing and sing it, repeating, all the time, until the procession ends, namely the circuit of the church either three times, or at least once. When the circuit ends, all enter the church; in order, however, to avoid confusion during the second procession, those carrying banners and icons remain before the church doors, and in the church prepare for the procession the cross-bearer with two candle-bearers, the brotherhood, choirs and clergy. When the sacred ministers enter the sanctuary, the main priest ascends to the altar and, having turned to the people, blesses them with the Holy Mysteries, quietly saying: "Save, O God, Thy people and bless Thine inheritance", places the Holy Mysteries on the altar, descends before the steps, bends the knees and, having taken off the omophorion, censes the Holy Mysteries three times, as usual; the Deacon, having approached the Holy Mysteries, bows low, takes them with the stand from the monstrance and places into the artophorion, and places the artophorion into the tabernacle and, having bowed, locks it. And where there will be no monstrance, the Holy Mysteries are placed in the artophorion and with it are locked in the tabernacle.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: писля слив священика тому то й ми споминаючи яки
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Після слів священика „Тому-то й ми, споминаючи”, які він мовить потиху, 1-й диякон бере у праву руку св. дискос, а 2-й диякон, також правою рукою, – св. чашу, так що права рука 1-го диякона спочиває на правиці 2-го диякона. Після цього диякони трохи підносять Святе, накреслюючи знак хреста над ілитоном, а священик виголошує: „Твоє від Твоїх”. Поставивши дискос і чашу, священик і диякони роблять знову малий поклін.
units.english_cohort_translation: > **Note:** This procession with the Holy Mysteries before Resurrection Matins – is a later addition of our churches, borrowed not from the Greeks and not from the Romans, but only from the Latin churches of these parts, superfluous to the majesty of our Resurrection Matins and is not given in our rubrics.

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: Після слів священика „Тому-то й ми, споминаючи”, які він мовить потиху, 1-й диякон бере у праву руку св. дискос, а 2-й диякон, також правою рукою, – св. чашу, так що права рука 1-го диякона спочиває на правиці 2-го диякона. Після цього диякони трохи підносять Святе, накреслюючи знак хреста над ілитоном, а священик виголошує: „Твоє від Твоїх”. Поставивши дискос і чашу, священик і диякони роблять знову малий поклін. Після цього священик проказує потиху молитву „Ще приносимо”, під час чого 1-й диякон повіває над святими Дарами, якщо треба.

units.english_cohort_translation: PROCESSION BEFORE THE CHURCH DOORS. All people go out of the church, and after them go out also the sacred ministers. And the procession takes place thus: All sacred ministers, in all their sacred bright vestments, stand before the steps of the altar. The main sacred minister takes the cross, the Deacon – the censer, all together bow low to the Holy Mysteries and turn to the west. The main one begins to sing the sticheron "Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior", all take up the singing of the sticheron and go out from the sanctuary to the church: the Priest – through the holy [doors], and all other sacred ministers – through the Deacon's doors; at this time all bells ring, and all go to the great church doors and, having gone out of the church, stand according to rank before the church doors, which are immediately closed[^615]. In the middle of the church is placed on the holy table first of all the icon of the Resurrection of Christ, usually on the Artos, also other holy icons, reliquaries and the book of the Holy Gospels in the most precious binding or something else of the sacred things, all this – according to the number of priests who will give them to be kissed by the people at the end of Matins. Outside, before the church doors, Matins begins in the following way BEGINNING OF MATINS. Immediately after the church doors are closed, the main priest, holding with his left hand the cross, and with his right – the censer and censing the church doors[^617], exclaims loudly: "Glory to the Holy" and the rest. The Choir responds: "Amen"; the Priest gives up the censer and sings loudly the troparion "Christ is risen", also all – the same, then the Priest the second time – the same and all – the same, and the third time the Priest – the same and all – the same, then the Priest in a high voice exclaims the verses, and all after each verse sing this troparion once[^618]. At the end the Priest, having sung in a higher voice the same troparion only up to "trampling down death by death" inclusive, opens the doors, and all finish: "and upon those in the tombs bestowing life" and again all bells ring, all enter the church[^619]. The Matins prayers at Resurrection Matins throughout the whole Bright Week are not recited, for they are connected with the Six Psalms, and since there will be no Six Psalms here, there will be no prayers. If it were necessary to recite the prayers, it should be indicated in the rubric where they should be recited, for during the verses "Let God arise", which take the place of the Six Psalms, it is not possible to recite them, for at this time the rubric orders the Priest to sing verses, and not to add prayers as well ENTRANCE INTO THE CHURCH. The entrance of the procession into the church takes place in the reverse order to the exit from the church, that is first enters the main priest, after him – other priests and sacred ministers, all the clergy, then singers, brotherhood, banner- and icon-bearers, the cross-bearer and all people. The priests enter the sanctuary and approach the holy table. The Bishop, if there be one, departs to his throne. The Deacon stands in his place before the holy doors and sings from there the litany

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: закинченни молитви 1 й диякон видкладае набик рипиду
units.slavonic_diplomatic: По закінченні молитви 1-й диякон відкладає набік рипіду чи покровець й обидва диякони наближаються до священика, який разом з ними робить три малі поклони. Потім 1-й диякон, вказуючи орарем на святий хліб: „Благослови, владико, святий хліб”.
units.english_cohort_translation: After the entrance into the church the first deacon sings the Great Litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord", standing in the usual place, and immediately we sing the Canon 6. **Canons:** Canon of the Resurrection: heirmoi – 4 times (in Greek ones – twice), troparia – on 12. (Today heirmoi – once, troparia with heirmos – on 4). Katavasia after each ode – heirmos of the canon, both choirs together – once. The Priest sings the heirmoi, and the choirs – the troparia and Katavasia. Refrain to the troparia of the canon – "Christ is risen from the dead", at the penultimate – "Glory", and at the last – "Both now", as usual

units.english_cohort_translation: If there be only one priest, he stands in the holy doors and from there gives the cross to be kissed by the people, greeting everyone: "Christ is risen", and the one Who kisses answers: "Truly He is risen". If there be several priests, then first the main one goes out from the holy doors and stands before the iconostasis, on the right side, that is opposite the icon of the Savior, looking to the north. After Him the second priest comes out from the holy doors with the Gospel, approaches the main one, and he gives him the cross to kiss, saying: "Christ is risen", having kissed, in His turn, gives Him the Gospel to kiss, answering: "Truly He is risen" and stands on His left. Then comes out the third priest with the icon of the Resurrection of Christ, approaches the first and He gives Him the cross to kiss, saying: "Christ is risen", and having kissed gives Him the icon of the Resurrection to kiss, answering: "Truly He is risen", and approaches the second priest, who gives him the Gospel to kiss, saying: "Christ is risen", and He, having kissed the Gospel, gives the second to kiss the icon of the Resurrection, answering: "Truly He is risen", and stands on the left of the second. The fourth priest comes out with the icon of the Theotokos, approaches the first, also the second and the third, of whom each gives him his object to kiss, saying: "Christ is risen", and having kissed gives each of them the icon of the Theotokos to kiss, answering: "Truly He is risen". So do also all other priests, as many as there be. In cathedral churches the Bishop, sitting on his throne opposite the icon of the Savior, gives the cross to be kissed, also each of the canons gives His insignia to be kissed, sitting on the seat. And when the kissing between the priests ends, then other sacred ministers and all the people approach one by one each Priest in turn, starting from the first, and kiss his insignia, answering: "Truly He is risen"[^622]. After the kissing once was read the "Homily" of Chrysostom, which is in the Flower *Triodion*.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Перший диякон вказує орарем на св. Дари і каже: „Благослови, владико, обидві” і, після благословення диякони кажуть: „Амінь, амінь, амінь”. Схиливши голови перед священиком, обидва диякони вертаються на місце, де стояли раніше, а 1-й бере рипіду і повіває нею над святими Дарами, як зазначалось вище, якщо треба.

units.english_cohort_translation: At "Blessed is the Kingdom" we sing "Christ is risen" three times, that is once – the Priest and both choirs – once each (although in our *Triodion* is given: "priest – three times and choirs the same – three times"), and where there is only one choir, then the Priest – once and the Choir – once, then half – the Priest and half (from "and upon those in the tombs") – the Choir.

units.english_cohort_translation: Also at "With the fear of God", instead of "Blessed is He that comes" and instead of "We have seen the true light", we sing "Christ is risen" once. Instead of "Let our mouths be filled" and "Blessed be the name of the Lord" – "Christ is risen" (3)[^626]. Among us usually "Christ is risen" is recited also instead of "Be exalted, O God, above the heavens", however, this violates the memory of the mystery of Christ's Ascension, which is mentioned in this place of the Liturgy from the beginning. Our priests say "Christ is risen" (only these two words) also after "With the fear of God", after "Save, O God" and after "Always, now and ever", however, in no rubric do we find this.

units.english_cohort_translation: 4. **Readings:** During the reading of the Gospel, at each verse, all bells are rung Our Sluzhebnyky: "If served conciliarly, then this Gospel is read by all priests and deacons by verses as the Superior decides". About this you have a detailed rubric in our and Russian Triodia. However, the custom that one and the same Gospel be read by all priests and deacons – is a superfluous invention of the Greco-Slavs, which today takes place among us only when the Gospel is read in different languages, as happens in our cathedral temples, in which the Bishop reads it in Greek from the holy doors, then the Deacon – in Slavonic from the ambo, and at the end canons and priests, placed throughout the whole church, in different liturgical languages. In Russia the Bishop reads the Gospel in Slavonic, and other priests – in Hebrew, in Greek and in Latin, in those languages in which the inscription on the Cross was written, then in other new languages (Muralt. 14. Brief. S. 142). The Greeks also read the Gospel, according to the new custom, in different languages, however, not at the Liturgy, but at Vespers (the Gospel read at Vespers of this day), as happens in the Patriarchate of Constantinople[^628].

units.english_cohort_translation: 5. Instead of *“It is truly meet”*, according to the new rubric, we sing the heirmos "Shine, shine" with the refrain "The angel cried" as in the *Triodion* and in the Constantinopolitan Typikon, but without the troparia of the 9th Ode of the Canon, as in our Sluzhebnyky, for these troparia are not about the Most Holy Theotokos, but about Christ's Resurrection 6. Before the dismissal, instead of "More honorable", we sing "Shine, shine" and instead of "Glory, Both now" – "Christ is risen" once. Dismissal with the cross and the rest, which is after the dismissal with the raising of the cross exactly as was indicated for Resurrection Matins 7. BLESSING OF THE ARTOS. After the Prayer behind the Ambo[^629] takes place the blessing of the Artos, for which you have the prayer in the *Sluzhebnik* after the Liturgy of the Resurrection; after the prayer the Artos is sprinkled with holy water. And this Artos with the feast, that is the icon of the Resurrection, after the dismissal of the Liturgy, is carried from the altar, on which it was blessed, to the tetrapod, where it remains until Bright Saturday and the faithful entering the church kiss it. units.english_cohort_translation: **At Vespers** > **Notes** 1. The sacred ministers, dressed in all sacred vestments of their rank during the whole Vespers stand in the sanctuary at the altar, coming out only for the Entrance (and deacons – also for the litanies) before the holy doors and for the final kissing of the sacred insignia, if there be several priests – as was given for Matins 2. Censing is done three times, that is at the usual beginning, only before the holy table, then at *“Lord, I have cried”* and at "O Gladsome Light", as usual 3. **Entrance:** Entrance takes place with the Gospel, for it is to be read 4. The Priest and deacons, if there be any, dressed in all sacred vestments of their rank, come before the steps of the altar and bow low, as usual. The Priest receives the censer with the usual prayer of blessing the censer, censes before the holy table, exclaiming: "Blessed is our God"[^632]; then, having given up the censer, ascends with the deacons the steps and sings "Christ is risen" once and both choirs – once each. After this the Priest recites clearly "Let God arise" and other verses with "Glory, Both now". The choirs, at each verse, sing "Christ is risen" once or three times exactly as was indicated for the beginning of Matins. Afterwards the Priest: "Christ is risen" up to "trampling down death by death", and the choirs: "and upon those in the tombs" and the rest 2. "In peace let us pray to the Lord" the Priest sings at the altar, and if a Deacon – then before the iconostasis.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 162 писля кадження священик виддае 2 му дияконови кадильницю
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 162.  Після кадження священик віддає 2-му дияконові кадильницю, а св. дискос зі складеною звіздою і складеними покровцями кладе йому на голову (див. ч. 129). 2-й диякон, тримаючи це все на голові і дивлячись в бік дверей та нічого не кажучи, йде між престолом і святими дверми просто до проскомидійного стола, на який ставить дискос, і там очікує священика. А священик, зробивши малий поклін і взявши святу чашу, відходить, за звичаєм, до проскомидійного стола, після чого 2-й диякон кадить святі речі і священика, а по молитві священика „Сповнення закону” зі страхом і усякою обережністю споживає св. Дари, що залишились після святого причастя, потім розв’язує свій орар.
units.english_cohort_translation: 4. **Entrance:** Entrance with the Gospel and usual censing at "O Gladsome Light"; and, after the Great Prokimenon, the Deacon, and if there is none, the Priest exclaims: "Wisdom!", and the reading from Genesis begins, and other readings 5. "Let us all say", "Vouchsafe" and "Let us complete".

units.english_cohort_translation: Note According to the previous rubric the Priest, at Vespers of Bright Week, from Monday onwards, should not use all sacred vestments, but from the beginning – only the epitrachelion, from the Entrance to the end – also the phelonion[^633]. Among us the custom is observed to use all sacred vestments on the first three days of Bright Week, that is on Sunday, Monday and Tuesday evening, since our people mark all these three days by abstention from work and presence at divine service. On other days of this week it is sufficient to use only the epitrachelion and phelonion.

Схиляючи голову перед святими дверми, проказує молитву входу „Владико Господи Боже наш”, благословляє правою рукою вхід, цілує Євангелію і, показуючи її, виголошує: „Премудрість, прості”. units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 169 коли хор закинчит спивати трисвяту писню священик
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 169. Коли хор закінчить співати трисвяту пісню, священик виголошує: „Будьмо уважні” і благословляє: „Мир всім. Премудрість, будьмо уважні”. Хор співає прокімен. Священик: „Премудрість”. Читець виголошує заголовок апостола. Священик: „Будьмо уважні”. По прочитанні апостола каже читцеві: „Мир тобі” і відразу після цього: „Премудрість, будьмо уважні”. Хор: „алилуя” зі стихами.
units.english_cohort_translation: On Sunday evening for Monday there will be no Entrance, as happens on the Sundays of Lent (for here there is no Great Prokimenon, and the Triodia give the litany "Have mercy on us, O God" at the end of Vespers), except the Sunday of Ap. Thomas, which, as a feast of the Lord, has also a Great Prokimenon. Finally, in the provinces the Great Entrance is made every Sunday evening, regardless of whether there is a feast or not

units.slavonic_incipit: Тоді священик благословляє кадило, бере кадильницю,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: тоди священик благословляе кадило бере кадильницю кадит престил
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Тоді священик благословляє кадило, бере кадильницю, кадить престіл навкруги, ціле святилище і з солеї – іконостас, обидва хори і людей. Вже під час цього або й пізніше проказує тихо молитву перед Євангелією „Засвіти в серцях наших”. По закінченні „алилуя” зі стихами, виголошує: „Премудрість, прості, вислухаймо святого Євангелія” і, благословляючи нарід, каже: „Мир всім”. Хор: „І духові твоєму”. Священик: „Від (ім’я) святого Євангелія читання”. Бере після цього книгу Євангелій, кладе її на аналой дещо поза святими дверми і читає Євангелію, обернений до народу. По прочитанні цілує згорнуту книгу й кладе її на середину престолу або на його правий бік (див. ч. 126, прим.).
units.english_cohort_translation: **At Compline** From today we begin to sing the Canons of the Theotokos. After *“It is truly meet”* throughout the whole week, we recite the Kontakion of the Sunday; only during the eight days of the feast of Mid-Pentecost we read the Kontakion of Mid-Pentecost 1. We sing the Midnight Office as usual, only after the 1st Trisagion on the feast of Mid-Pentecost we take the Troparion of Mid-Pentecost, and on the Apodosis of the Resurrection – the Resurrection Troparion of the Sunday with its Theotokion; and after the 2nd Trisagion in the middle of Mid-Pentecost we take the Kontakion of Mid-Pentecost, and outside Mid-Pentecost – Kontakion of the Resurrection. The prayer "Remember, O Lord" will not be 2. We begin Matins from "Glory to the Holy" and immediately "Christ is risen" (3), then "Glory to God in the highest" and the rest; before the 50th Psalm we recite "The Resurrection of Christ": on Sundays – three times, and on weekdays – once[^639]

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 170 проказавши молитву херувимськои писни благословляе священик кадило
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 170.  Проказавши молитву херувимської пісні, благословляє  священик  кадило,  після  чого  потім  кадить навкруги св. трапезу, запрестольну ікону, принесення і з солеї – іконостас, обидва хори і людей. Повернувшись до престолу і тримаючи кадильницю на перстеневому пальці лівої руки, проказує, піднісши руки, тричі херувимську пісню.
units.english_cohort_translation: **At the Hours** after "Blessed is our God" we recite "Christ is risen" (3), and after the dismissal – "Christ is risen" (3) and add: "and to us He has granted life eternal" and further > **Note:** Since we do not exclaim "Blessed is our God" when the Hour is combined with Matins or with the preceding one, also since we do not impart the dismissal when the Hour is combined with the following one, then we do not read "Christ is risen" then.

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: 170.  Проказавши молитву херувимської пісні, благословляє  священик  кадило,  після  чого  потім  кадить навкруги св. трапезу, запрестольну ікону, принесення і з солеї – іконостас, обидва хори і людей. Повернувшись до престолу і тримаючи кадильницю на перстеневому пальці лівої руки, проказує, піднісши руки, тричі херувимську пісню. Потім підходить до принесення, трьома вимахами кадить святі дари, кажучи потиху: „Боже, милостивий будь мені грішному”. Тоді бере великий покровець і кладе його собі на ліве рамено, кажучи: „Піднесіть руки ваші”, бере св. дискос – лівою, а чашу – правою рукою і виходить північними дверми, виголошуючи: „Святішого вселенського” (див. ч. 129). Увійшовши святими дверми, кладе святі дари на престіл, як належить, великий покровець кадить над кадильницею, що її подає прислуга, кажучи: „Благообразний Йосиф”. Потім, взявши кадильницю з рук прислуги, кадить святі дари трьома вимахами, кажучи: „Ущаслив, Господи”.

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: 170.  Проказавши молитву херувимської пісні, благословляє  священик  кадило,  після  чого  потім  кадить навкруги св. трапезу, запрестольну ікону, принесення і з солеї – іконостас, обидва хори і людей. Повернувшись до престолу і тримаючи кадильницю на перстеневому пальці лівої руки, проказує, піднісши руки, тричі херувимську пісню. Потім підходить до принесення, трьома вимахами кадить святі дари, кажучи потиху: „Боже, милостивий будь мені грішному”. Тоді бере великий покровець і кладе його собі на ліве рамено, кажучи: „Піднесіть руки ваші”, бере св. дискос – лівою, а чашу – правою рукою і виходить північними дверми, виголошуючи: „Святішого вселенського” (див. ч. 129). Увійшовши святими дверми, кладе святі дари на престіл, як належить, великий покровець кадить над кадильницею, що її подає прислуга, кажучи: „Благообразний Йосиф”. Потім, взявши кадильницю з рук прислуги, кадить святі дари трьома вимахами, кажучи: „Ущаслив, Господи”.
