units.english_cohort_translation: [127] Moscow Typikon, chapter 4, and Peremyshl, page 85. -- Mark in chapters 78 and 79 prescribes after the 3rd Ode the Sessional Hymn of the saint, Glory, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the tone, that is Sunday, after the 6th -- Kontakion of the saint. New Constantinopolitan Typikon after the 3rd Ode: Κοντακιον το αναστασιμον χύμα, είτα ψαλλεται το Κάθισμα του Αγιου, και το θεοτοκιον; μετά δε την εκτην ωδην Κοντακιον και Οίκος του εορταζομενου Αγιου /Kontakion of the resurrection spoken, then is sung the Kathisma of the saint, and the Theotokion; after the 6th Ode Kontakion and Ikos of the celebrated Saint/. Greek Typikon in chapter 2, after the 3rd Ode -- Κάθισμα του Μηναίου /Kathisma of the *Menaion*/, after the 6th -- Κοντακιον του Αγιου /Kontakion of the Saint/, after the 9th -- Εξαποστιλαριον το αναστασιμον και του Αγιου ει εορτάζεται, και το θεοτοκιον /Exaposteilarion of the resurrection and of the Saint if he is celebrated, and the Theotokion/, but does not indicate, which Theotokion; however, Slavonic typikons rightly prescribe the Theotokion of the Sunday Exaposteilarion, for it corresponds to the Sunday Gospel.

units.english_cohort_translation: [279] We find the Service of St. Catherine as having Polyeleos only in our Pochaiv *Menaion* and in the new Greek-Venetian one; but in others -- without Polyeleos. In later Greek typikons we find it given on 25 November with the Apodosis of the Feast of the Entry into the Temple of the Most Holy Theotokos, and in earlier ones -- on the 24th, as it is today among Greek-Slavs. Thus the Greek-Venetian *Menaion* of 1615 gives: Σημειωσαι ουν, ότι ευρομεν εν τισι Τυπικοις των νεωτέρων, ότι εν τιοα των πόλεων ψαλλεται η ακολουθία της αγίας μάρτυρος Αικατερίνης εν τη κε του μηνός, εν η και αποδιδοται η εορτή. Εν ετεροις δε Τυπικοις παλαιοτεροις ευρομεν αυτήν εορτάζεσαι εν τη κδ του αυτού μηνός: εν δε τη κε ψαλλομεν την ακολουθίαν του εν αγιοις Κλημεντος Παπα Ρώμης, και Πέτρου Αλεξανδρείας, εν η και αποδιδοται η εορτή των Εισοδιων /Note, therefore, that we found in some newer typikons, that in some places the service of the holy martyr Catherine is sung on the 25th day of this month, on which the feast is also given up. In other older typikons we found that her memory is celebrated on the 24th of this month, and on the 25th we sing the service of Saints Clement Pope of Rome and Peter of Alexandria, and on this day also the feast of the Entry is given up/. This transfer from the 24th to the 25th day, in the opinion of the Greeks, as explained by the new Greek-Venetian *Menaion* (24 November, p. 158), was done at the wish of the monks of Mount Sinai, so that it would not coincide with the Apodosis of the feast and, so that in this way the memory of the saint would be honored more solemnly. For we know that the body of the holy great martyr was transferred by angelic power to Mount Sinai and buried there.

units.english_cohort_translation: [264] Ancient Greek typikons mention nothing about a deacon, neither at the bringing out, nor at the exaltation, nor at the laying of the precious Cross, but only about one priest. The Greek typikon, similarly to the Slavic ones, prescribes for the priest to vest in all priestly vestments: αλασσει ο Ιερεύς πασαν την ιερατικην στολην /the priest vests in all priestly vestments/. The Greek *Triodion* (Sunday of the Veneration of the Cross) and the new Constantinopolitan Typikon, similarly to Slavic typikons, prescribes for the priest to enter with the cross from the sanctuary to the temple through the northern doors: εκ του αριστερού Βήματος /from the left side of the sanctuary/. Greek typikons, with the exception of the new Constantinopolitan, and the Slavic of the Lviv University, prescribe for the priest, having exited from the sanctuary to the temple, to head to the entrance doors that lead from the temple to the narthex, which are sometimes called royal, and there await the end of the Doxology and from there exclaim "Wisdom, attend", and then head to the tetrapod, which is before the iconostasis. Although these doors are called royal, βασιλικαι /royal/, one must understand that they were called so in the past. Today we call royal the middle doors of the iconostasis, which according to ancient custom are called holy: αγιαι ΰυραι /holy doors/ (chapter 96, Greek Typikon).

units.english_cohort_translation: [754] Ed. note. In ancient times, "Royal Doors" referred to those doors that led from the narthex to the temple, for at them the Patriarch met the Emperor. Later this name was applied with improper meaning to the middle doors of the iconostasis. In the rubrics of modern Greek liturgical books, "holy doors" are given (see Akolouthia tou Esperinou kai tou Orthrou, Roma 1950, p. 16), therefore we also consistently correct "Royal Doors" to "Holy Doors" everywhere in this Typikon.

units.english_cohort_translation: 97. According to the ancient custom of the Eastern Church, only one Holy Liturgy may be celebrated at the same holy table. However, one may depart from this rule if the Divine Liturgy must be repeated for the benefit of the faithful. If there is one or several secondary churches in the parish, then the more solemn Liturgy is celebrated in the main sanctuary, and other liturgies should be celebrated rather in the side sanctuaries.

units.english_cohort_translation: Regarding the troparion "Holy is the Lord our God," neither the ancient Greek Typikons nor the Euchologia prescribe to take it three times, nor do they adduce its verses. However, the Slavonic rubrics and the new Constantinopolitan Typikon prescribe to take it three times; regarding the verses -- they do not agree. Our Sluzhebnik and the new Constantinopolitan Typikon present only one verse; ours: "Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy" (5th verse of the 98th psalm, from the last verse of which this troparion is taken). Constantinopolitan: Υψουτε Κυριον τον θεον ημών /Exalt ye the Lord our God/. The Tserkovne Oko and following it the Moscow Typikons present two verses, namely: 1. "For holy is the Lord our God"; 2. "Over all people is our God." In our opinion, if the troparion must be taken three times, then one verse is not sufficient; therefore it is possible to divide the verse "Exalt ye" into two parts, of which the second would begin from: "And worship at His footstool" etc.

units.english_cohort_translation: [277] Some consider, according to the edition of the Peremyshl Typikon of 1870, p. 271, that neither on St. Michael, nor on St. Prophet Elias, should *“Blessed is the man”* be sung and, that then not a single kathisma is taken, for this kathisma, as the publisher writes about it, is found only in the Pochaiv *Anthologion*, and in the most ancient menaia and Anthologia they are not mentioned; the reason for this is considered to be that "Elias did not die, and St. Michael, as bodiless, is not subject to death". However, this is not enough. For regarding the rule, not only the Pochaiv *Anthologion* (*Anthologion*) of 1777 and the Pochaiv *Menaion* of the same year, but also the Lviv *Anthologion* (*Anthologion*) of 1643 and the Great Typikon, under the title *Tserkovne Oko*, printed in Moscow in 1615, that is more than a century and a half before the Pochaiv *Anthologion*, and the manuscript *Anthologion* of 1736, which we have, and the Typikon of the All-Russian Church, printed in Moscow in 1859, by the decision of its Governing Synod, give also on these two feasts the kathisma *“Blessed is the man”*. Although some rules, like the Moscow *Menaion* of 1782, the Greek-Venetian of 1884 do not give *“Blessed is the man”*, it does not follow from this that no kathisma is needed, for even on Saints without Polyeleos in the *Menaion* a kathisma is not given, but the sequential one is meant; so here one can understand the sequential one, which three ancient handwritten Slavic typikons give: one -- of the Lviv University, the second -- of St. Onuphrius in Lviv, and the third -- of the library of the Chapter of St. George; also *Tserkovne Oko* (which gives two rules: one with *“Blessed is the man”*, and the second with the sequential kathisma). The reason that these rules give for these two feasts a sequential kathisma, may lie in the fact that their service initially had neither All-Night Vigil nor Polyeleos, but gradually, with time, grew into All-Night Vigil. About St. Elias it is written in the Pochaiv *Menaion*: "Let it be known that in printed Greek menaia, in handwritten typikons, and also in Slavic handwritten and printed typikons, the service of the Prophet Elias is given on 6, with *Octoechos*". And regarding St. Michael, the above-mentioned Slavic typikons give him a service only of the Polyeleos type, but incomplete, for they partially combine his service with the service of the *Octoechos*, as for a Saint without Polyeleos.

units.english_cohort_translation: [77] When two kathismata should be read, and when three, we noted in the note to the Order of Daily Matins on page 41. Regarding small litanies which are read between kathismata and sessional hymns, the Lviv Synod, our Horologions and our Sluzhebniks (at the end) give them also at Small Matins, and they are used also by the Greek-Melkites (according to the testimony of their patriarch bl. m. Clement Bahous). Conversely, in the Russian Typikon, approved by their Governing Synod (Moscow edition of 1859), in the Order of Daily Matins it is written that the priest says them only at the Vigil and when the memory of saints having a Polyeleos and Doxology is celebrated; similarly also in the new Wallachian-Bucharest Typikon, in which in the Order of Daily Matins is given: "We take sessional hymns from the *Octoechos* without litanies" (untranslatable); and adds: "In monasteries, usually, between kathismata litanies are taken only on Sunday and when more special saints occur". From the Greek Typikon no conclusion can be made, for in it small litanies are not mentioned neither at Small Matins, nor at Great, nor before the Canon, nor after the Canon. It is assumed in the Typikon that this is known to everyone. From the rubrics of the Greek *Triodion*, given at Matins on Meatfare Saturday, one can conclude that these litanies should be said also at Small Matins. For it gives: η συνηιϊης στιχολογια. Εν δε ταις συναπταις πασαις της στιχολογιας και του Κανόνος, μνημονεύονται πάντες οι προαπελΰοντες Πατέρες και αδελφοί ημων /Ordinary Stichology. In all small litanies of the Stichology and of the Canon, all our fathers and brethren who have passed away before us are commemorated/. Let everyone observe the rubric and custom of his Church. Finally, in our opinion, later typikons reject litanies here only for the sake of greater shortening of the divine service; if the single difference between Small and Great Matins were the rejection or use of litanies, then this difference should have been indicated in some place of ancient liturgical books; however, this is not encountered. What the exclamation of the third litany should be is not indicated in any of the church books. Therefore we are forced to borrow it from Great Matins. At Great Matins in Slavonic books two exclamations are given which are used at the third litany, that is one -- for Sunday "For blessed is" and the second -- for Polyeleos feasts "For holy Art Thou". For the sake of distinguishing the Sunday day from the ordinary day, at Small Matins it is appropriate to use the second "For holy Art Thou", although it would not be bad to use also the first "For blessed is" (Οτι ευλογητοα), for in Greek books we find only this one exclamation, without distinction of day. Regarding Sessional Hymns, they are taken two or three after each stichology, depending on the edition, except the Theotokion. In Lviv editions of the *Octoechos* and in the Greek-Venetian one, only to the Theotokion is sung "Glory, Both now". In the Pochaiv and Moscow ones a separate refrain is also given to every second, or even to the third sessional hymn. This refrain, corresponding to the content of the sessional hymn: on Monday and Tuesday -- Penitential "O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger"; on Wednesday and Friday -- of the Cross, and on Thursday -- of the Apostles; to the third sessional hymn, that is the Martyron -- also the Martyron refrain: "Wondrous is God in His saints".

Clement Bahous). Conversely, in the Russian Typikon, approved by their Governing Synod (Moscow edition of 1859), in the Order of Daily Matins it is written that the priest says them only at the Vigil and when the memory of saints having a Polyeleos and Doxology is celebrated; similarly also in the new Wallachian-Bucharest Typikon, in which in the Order of Daily Matins is given: "We take sessional hymns from the *Octoechos* without litanies" (untranslatable); and adds: "In monasteries, usually, between kathismata litanies are taken only on Sunday and when more special saints occur". From the Greek Typikon no conclusion can be made, for in it small litanies are not mentioned neither at Small Matins, nor at Great, nor before the Canon, nor after the Canon. It is assumed in the Typikon that this is known to everyone. From the rubrics of the Greek *Triodion*, given at Matins on Meatfare Saturday, one can conclude that these litanies should be said also at Small Matins. For it gives: η συνηιϊης στιχολογια. Εν δε ταις συναπταις πασαις της στιχολογιας και του Κανόνος, μνημονεύονται πάντες οι προαπελΰοντες Πατέρες και αδελφοί ημων /Ordinary Stichology. In all small litanies of the Stichology and of the Canon, all our fathers and brethren who have passed away before us are commemorated/. Let everyone observe the rubric and custom of his Church. Finally, in our opinion, later typikons reject litanies here only for the sake of greater shortening of the divine service; if the single difference between Small and Great Matins were the rejection or use of litanies, then this difference should have been indicated in some place of ancient liturgical books; however, this is not encountered. What the exclamation of the third litany should be is not indicated in any of the church books. Therefore we are forced to borrow it from Great Matins. At Great Matins in Slavonic books two exclamations are given which are used at the third litany, that is one -- for Sunday "For blessed is" and the second -- for Polyeleos feasts "For holy Art Thou". For the sake of distinguishing the Sunday day from the ordinary day, at Small Matins it is appropriate to use the second "For holy Art Thou", although it would not be bad to use also the first "For blessed is" (Οτι ευλογητοα), for in Greek books we find only this one exclamation, without distinction of day. Regarding Sessional Hymns, they are taken two or three after each stichology, depending on the edition, except the Theotokion. In Lviv editions of the *Octoechos* and in the Greek-Venetian one, only to the Theotokion is sung "Glory, Both now". In the Pochaiv and Moscow ones a separate refrain is also given to every second, or even to the third sessional hymn. This refrain, corresponding to the content of the sessional hymn: on Monday and Tuesday -- Penitential "O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger"; on Wednesday and Friday -- of the Cross, and on Thursday -- of the Apostles; to the third sessional hymn, that is the Martyron -- also the Martyron refrain: "Wondrous is God in His saints".

units.english_cohort_translation: ^[508] Regarding the litany, we do not find unity in the rubrics. For some rubrics are silent about it, others prescribe it, and some exclude it. Those that are silent about it are the manuscript Vatican Typika... Those that prescribe the litany: The Greek Bologna *Triodion* 1724, Kyivan-Pechersk 1640, Lviv 1753 and some manuscripts. Those that exclude it: The Moscow Typikon 1859... *Tserkovne Oko* and the ancient manuscript Typikon... We suppose that the rubrics which do not prescribe the litany are more logical, for at all other Lenten Vespers and Matins this litany is not present...

units.english_cohort_translation: [311] Typikons of some Russian monasteries, given by the *Tserkovne Oko*, prescribe for the deacon at each Hour to sing three litanies, that is "In peace let us pray to the Lord" at the end of the tripalm, the Small Litany before the Prokeimenon and "Let us complete" after the singing of the Gospel. This is not enough for Greek length and with unnecessary additions the Greeks distort the form of the Hours, handed down to us from the beginnings; also ancient Lviv typikons add litanies.

units.slavonic_incipit: Тоді священик скидає воздух і, згорнувши
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: тоди священик скидае воздух и згорнувши його кладе
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Тоді священик скидає воздух і, згорнувши його, кладе окремо, як також і звізду. Диякон входить південними дверми у святилище, стає праворуч священика й, зробивши малий поклін, мовить: „Роздроби, владико, святий хліб”, а священик розламує його і чотири частини розміщує на дискосі так, як це відбувається на Літургії Золотоустого, а частицю з написом „ІС” кладе до святої чаші, не кажучи нічого. Диякон вливає до чаші трохи теплоти, якщо існує звичай, не кажучи нічого і стає дещо на боці. Хор співає кіноник „Спожийте і збагніть”, а також другий, якщо читались апостол і євангелія якогось святого чи святого храмового.
units.english_cohort_translation: [202] Moscow Typikon and *Menaion* November 21, September 8 and 15 and February 2. (Moscow Typikon, fol. 176, on the verso) and Mark Καιφ. ξε /chapter 65/ prescribe, according to the ancient typikon, also of the day, and to the saint, if he has; if -- not, then only of the day, and to the saint -- nothing. Mark, chapter 8, in *Tserkovne Oko*: if -- not, then sequential and of the Theotokos.

units.english_cohort_translation: 7. If there be several Prokeimena, Alleluias, Apostle-Gospels and Communion Hymns, then one must know how to take them. Know first, that in church typikons more than two are not given, with the exception of Apostle-Gospels, of which only in Slavonic typikons three are given, for the Slavs are richer in supplications than the Greeks. For where three readings coincide, the Greek typikons do not give the sequential one, but the Slavonic ones take it under the refrain of the first reading, as if one with it . When this is impossible, on the occasion of some great feast, then they order to take it on the day before under the refrain with the sequential one . However, this rule has been preserved among us perhaps only in cathedral churches, for in others usually only one Apostle-Gospel is taken, as also one service either of the day, or of the saint, or one for need. If, therefore, there be two Prokeimena and two Alleluias, then both are taken under one heading, that is both Prokeimena – before the refrain of the first reading, both Alleluias – after the completion of the second reading. However, the first Prokeimenon is taken twice, namely: once – before and once – after the verse, the second – only once and without a verse, for in this case the Typikon does not give a verse. Similarly also "Alleluia": both of its verses are taken only of the first service, and of the second – only one first verse . The Heading, that is from whom: from Paul, from Matthew or from another, is taken only of the first reading, and the others usually are not taken, although it would be better to announce the headings of other readings as well, for it is not indifferent to the listeners to know the reading of which holy author is being proclaimed; and for this reason only would the rubric make certain sense, which orders to take the sequential reading under the refrain, for taking one reading under the refrain of another means merging it with the previous one because its heading is not announced. If the heading of the following third reading, which is not taken under the refrain, is not named, then it should have been said that this third reading is also taken under the refrain. "Let us be attentive" is announced only at the beginning of the first reading. If there be two Communion Hymns, then "Alleluia" is repeated only upon the completion of the second .

slavonic_provenance.verbatim_source: Диякон обтирає святу чашу, нічого не кажучи і, зробивши три малі поклони, після того, як відсунено завісу іконостасу, відчиняє святі двері. Прийнявши від священика чашу, підходить до святих дверей і, піднісши її, показує людям, кажучи: „Приступіть”. Хор: „Благословлю Господа повсякчасно. Алилуя”. Причастя вірних відбувається так, як на Літургії Золотоустого, а священик, подаючи святий хліб, мовить слова цієї Літургії „Чесного і пресвятого”. Перенесення св. дискоса відбувається так, як на Літургії Золотоустого. Священик робить малий поклін, бере святу чашу, обертається до св. дверей, дивлячись на людей, каже тихо: „Благословенний Бог”, а потім виголошує: „завжди, нині і повсякчас”.

Священик робить малий поклін, бере святу чашу, обертається до св. дверей, дивлячись на людей, каже тихо: „Благословенний Бог”, а потім виголошує: „завжди, нині і повсякчас”.

2.У співслужінні двох дияконів
248. По закінченні часів і по відпусті на кінці зображальних зачиняються святі двері, священик і диякони роблять перед св. трапезою по три малі поклони, кажучи: „Боже, милостивий будь мені грішному” і цілують св. Євангелію, край св. трапези і напрестольний хрест, за звичаєм. Після цього 1-й диякон, віддавши шану священикові, виходить північними дверми і, ставши на своєму місці перед св. дверми, робить три малі поклони, нічого не кажучи, після чого виголошує: „Благослови, владико”. Священик: „Благословенне царство”. Хор: „Амінь” і читець читає початковий псалом.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 250 кадження на псалми господи взиваю я и
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 250. Кадження на псалмі „Господи, взиваю я” і вхід відбуваються так, як на вечірні у співслужінні двох дияконів (див. ч.  39). Повернувшись у святилище,  1-й диякон виголошує від святих дверей: „Будьмо уважні”. Священик, обернувшись до народу: „Мир всім”. 2-й диякон: „Премудрість, будьмо уважні”. Хор співає прокімен першої паремії. 1-й диякон: „Премудрість”. Читець: „З книги Буття читання”. 2-й диякон: „Будьмо уважні”. Читець читає першу паремію, після якої хор співає другий прокімен.
units.english_cohort_translation: ^[615] According to the ancient rubric of community life the procession goes from the temple into the narthex through the northern doors of this narthex and there, before its central doors leading into the temple, the beginning of Matins is sung. Carried are: Gospel -- by the priest and censer -- by the deacon, preceded by candle-bearers, brethren with lit candles, as you have in the Greek *Pentecostarion*. To this the Pochaiv *Triodion* adds the icon of the Resurrection of Christ, and *Tserkovne Oko* -- also the icon of the Most Holy Theotokos and other holy icons, carried by priests and deacons, so that in such a way the procession would be more majestic, than only with candles. According to the custom of the surroundings of Greece, independent of the Patriarch of Constantinople, before this procession the bishop or priest, standing in the holy doors with a lit candlestick in hand, exclaims in a loud voice: "Come ye, take light from the unwaning light, and glorify Christ, who is risen from the dead", that is "Come, receive light from the unwaning light and kiss Christ, risen from the dead". And so all approach one by one, to light their candles from him, forming after this the procession (The Holy Passions. Athens. 1892)

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 253 якщо випаде пам ят якогос святого або храмовий
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 253.  Якщо випаде пам’ять якогось святого або храмовий празник, 2-й диякон виголошує: „Будьмо уважні”. По прокімені апостола 1-й диякон: „Премудрість”. По прочитанні читцем заголовка апостола 2-й диякон: „Будьмо уважні”.
units.english_cohort_translation: [342] Thus have later editions, namely ours Pochaiv and the Russian, and the most ancient Greek, namely Ευχολογιον /*Euchologion*/ of Benedict, and of the Slavic ones -- Ostromir Gospel, *Tserkovne Oko* and the manuscript give the Prokeimenon only to the Saint, and the Apostle-Gospel -- only to the Circumcision, for the Prokeimenon of the Feast and the Apostle-Gospel to the Saint -- is a later addition of the Slavs. However, now comes the time not of adding new, but of shortening ancient prayers. The ancient typikon has this: "Let the Gospel be taken at Matins to the saint, and at the Liturgy -- to the Circumcision".

units.slavonic_incipit: Кадження перед Євангелією відбувається так, як
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: кадження перед евангелиею видбуваеться так як на литургии
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Кадження перед Євангелією відбувається так, як на Літургії Золотоустого у співслужінні двох дияконів (див. ч. 155). Потім 1-й диякон: „Благослови, владико, благовістителя”. Священик: „Бог, молитвами” і передає йому Євангелію. 2-й диякон: „Премудрість, прості, вислухаймо святого Євангелія”. Священик: „Мир всім”. 1-й диякон, ставши на амвоні або дещо перед святими дверми: „Від (ім’я) святого Євангелія читання”. 2-й диякон: „Будьмо уважні” та все інше, за звичаєм.

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Від середи четвертого тижня Посту співають так, як подається далі. 1-й диякон: „Всі оглашенні”. 2-й диякон: „Оглашенні, вийдіть”. Знову 1-й диякон: „Всі, що до просвічення, приступіть. Помоліться ті, що до просвічення”. Хор: „Господи, помилуй”, а 1-й диякон: „Вірні, за братів, що до святого просвічення готуються”.
units.english_cohort_translation: ^[600] The magnificent rite of the Shroud in ancient *Triodia* and Typika is not given, for it was introduced later; however, today it is used among all followers of the Greek rite, and among us -- also with the exposition of the Holy Mysteries, according to the custom of the Latins of the Austrian State and various German dioceses (Nilles, Calend. T. 2, p. 312). It is described in our Sluzhebniks, published in Pochaiv back under Stanislaus Augustus in 1767, then in Russian Typika and in the new Typikon of the Patriarchate of Constantinople. However, in our Sluzhebniks the procession with the Shroud is given only at Vespers, in Russian rubrics -- only at Saturday Matins, after the Great Doxology, and in the Constantinopolitan Typikon the bringing out into the temple to the tomb is prescribed at Vespers, the procession around the temple -- at Matins.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 255 пид час спивання писни нини сили небесни
units.slavonic_diplomatic:
255.  Під час співання пісні „Нині сили небесні” відчиняються святі двері і диякони, взявши кадильниці, кадять трьома вимахами (тричі) тільки спереду св. трапезу, потім
–  проскомидійний стіл і священика. Після цього стають праворуч і ліворуч священика, тримаючи кадильниці на одному з пальців лівої руки, і проказують зі священиком тричі пісню „Нині сили небесні”.
units.english_cohort_translation: [45] According to the ancient rubric, a saint "on 4" could be of two types: that is, either with a troparion or without a troparion; and when the saint has no troparion, then at Matins, instead of "God is the Lord," "Alleluia" was sung and the divine service had a separate rubric. But in our current Horologia, troparia are given for every day of the month, and therefore at Matins we always sing "God is the Lord," and we limit the "Alleluia" service to Great Lent, as do the Greeks.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 256 писля того як св дискос и святу
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 256.  Після того, як св. дискос і святу чашу поставлять на св. трапезі, диякони виходять своїми дверми і стають на звичайних місцях. 1-й диякон виголошує: „Сповнім”. На „Отче наш” диякони перепоясують себе орарями навхрест. 2-й диякон: „Голови наші перед Господом схилім”. Після трьох малих поклонів 1-й диякон виголошує „Будьмо уважні” і після виголосу священика „Напередосвячене святеє святим” вертаються обидва диякони своїми дверми у святилище.
units.english_cohort_translation: [168] E.g. *Menaion* September 15 and August 9 (according to the most ancient typikons, which prescribe to celebrate the memory of the Holy Apostles on 6, without Polyeleos) and November 20, which has the sign of a saint on 6; also the Typikon, given for Thomas Sunday for the whole Pentecost.

units.english_cohort_translation: Regarding the time and place of the placing of the Shroud we do not find an ancient rubric, for this rite is later and different in different regions. According to the custom of our archcathedral church the Shroud remains hung behind the holy table, over the High Place, from Resurrection Matins to the Apodosis of the Resurrection inclusive, that is until Wednesday before the Ascension. According to the custom of our other churches, the Shroud, taken from the Tomb before Resurrection Matins, is placed on the holy table, where it remains during the whole Bright Week, and from the Sunday of Ap. Thomas to the Apodosis of the Resurrection – behind the holy table. According to others – it remains on the altar, the antimension with the Gospel is placed on it and the Liturgy is celebrated on it. However, it is better to place the Shroud behind the holy table, for lying on the altar, it is often significantly damaged by candles, from which wax drips on it.

units.english_cohort_translation: ^[626] So about "Christ is risen" in our Sluzhebniks, except "We have seen", and in its place they have "Christ is risen", however, such is our custom and so in the Pochaiv *Triodion* of 1786... and in the Moscow Typikon of 1859... Ancient Greek rubrics prescribe "Christ is risen" only instead of "Blessed be the name" and instead of the psalm "I will bless the Lord", as in the Slavonic Typikon of the Lviv University. A later custom of the Greeks -- to sing "Christ is risen" after "Blessed is the Kingdom" three times and, instead of "We have seen the true light" and instead of "Blessed be the name of the Lord", -- three times. However, some of them, after "Blessed is the Kingdom" sing "Christ is risen" with its verses, as is given at the beginning of Resurrection Matins. The Moscow Typikon follows them, but the new Constantinopolitan Typikon does not go. What we said about the custom of the Greeks, we took from a description which we have from the island of Corfu, in which is written the following: "After 'Blessed is the kingdom' the priest 'Christ is risen', and successively repeat it, first the right followed by the left choir; and this happens on all the days of Pascha until the Ascension. But on the great Sunday, and on those of the New Week we follow to sing it after its verses unchanged; as was said previously at Matins... Is sung successively 'Christ is risen' – as much on the great Sunday as on the remaining days of Pascha at 'With fear' instead of 'We have seen the light', and before the Dismissal three times flowingly instead of 'Blessed be the name', and at the end, at the Dismissal instead of 'Through the prayers' /After 'Blessed is the Kingdom' the priest: 'Christ is risen', successively again repeat it: first -- the right, then -- and the left choir. And so it will be on all days from the Resurrection to the Ascension. But on the Great Sunday and on the days of Bright Week we continue to sing invariable this with its verses, as is taken at Matins ... Successively is sung 'Christ is risen' on the Great Sunday as much as on the rest of the days of the Resurrection: at 'With fear', instead of 'We have seen the light' and before the dismissal three times flowingly, instead of 'Blessed be the name' and at the end, at the dismissal, instead of 'Through the prayers of our holy fathers'/.

units.english_cohort_translation: [160] According to the ancient typikon, on Sunday, in view of the All-Night Vigil, everything was taken on Small Vespers only of the Sunday, as usual. But on Great Vespers at the Lytia: one sticheron of the temple, and also stichera of the Forefeast from the Aposticha of Matins. At the Blessing of Loaves: Troparion "O Virgin Theotokos" twice and of the Forefeast once (*Menaion* September 7), and Mark: "O Virgin Theotokos" thrice without the Afterfeast (Καιφ. ξε /chapter 65/).

units.english_cohort_translation: [65] Peremyshl Typikon, page 81. -- According to the ancient typikon there was to be a Sunday troparion at all hours, also "Glory" at the 1st and 6th -- Goes also to the first saint, at the 3rd and 9th -- to the second; Kontakia -- alternating: at the 1st and 6th -- to the first, at the 3rd and 9th -- to the second saint (compare John the Theologian on the Sunday of the Holy Fathers). When the Kontakion is only for one saint, then it alone is taken at all [hours]; and when for neither, nor for the feast, then the Hypakoe of the tone is taken; for general Greek editions do not have Sunday Kontakia. Regarding the Hypakoe, you have the rubric in Greek Horologions at the 1st Hour, it and at the other hours must be observed.

units.english_cohort_translation: [201] According to the most general and most ancient typikons in the Afterfeast and on the Apodosis the Trisagion should be taken, and not "As many as have been baptized into Christ" or "Before Thy Cross", for they are taken on the very day of the feast, with the exception of "As many as have been baptized into Christ", which is taken not only on the very day of the Resurrection, but also throughout the whole Bright Week, since throughout the whole Bright Week the divine service takes place as on the very day of the Resurrection. On other days, until the Apodosis of the Resurrection, the Trisagion is taken. So have the general Greek and Slavonic typikons and the most ancient Typikon of the Monastery of St. Nicholas of Casole in the district of Otranto, kept in the Barberini library in Rome, written six hundred or seven hundred years ago. In it on fol. 121 and 124 is given the Typikon, which I gave. With this general and ancient typikon one Greek Typikon does not agree, written by the Reverend Father Bartholomew, a companion of the Reverend Father Nilus and co-founder of the Monastery of Grottaferrata near Rome, kept in that same monastery, which prescribes "As many as have been baptized into Christ" until the Apodosis of the feast. E.g. December 26 gives: Και αντί του Τρισάγιου Οσοι εις Χριστον. Τούτο γαρ λεγομεν έως ου αποδιδοται η εορτή /And instead of the Trisagion As many as have been baptized into Christ. For this we say until the feast is taken leave of/. Does not agree also the new Constantinopolitan Typikon 1851, marked with the seal of the patriarch. See, e.g. on Monday of the Holy Spirit there, where Greek and Slavonic *Triodia* have the Trisagion, this Typikon has "As many as have been baptized into Christ". Regarding Troparia, Mark thus: Sunday, Glory: Troparion to the saint, if he has, Both now: Kontakion of the feast (Καιφ. ξε)/chapter 65/.

units.english_cohort_translation: [183] 2 Ancient Greek Typikon of the Monastery of St. Nicholas των Κασουλων /of Casole/ (Ed. Note: a place in Puglia, southern Italy, where the Monastery of St. Nicholas was located) in the village of Otranto (Bibliotheca Barberina) prescribes "As many as have been baptized into Christ" also on the Transfiguration. And the Greek Typikon of Grottaferrata, that is of the monastery of the reverend father Nilus, near Rome, gives "As many as have been baptized into Christ" not only on the very day of the feast or in Bright Week, but also on all days of the Afterfeast until the Apodosis of the feast; similarly also the new Constantinopolitan Typikon; however, the Greek Typikon, called of St. Sabbas, and following it also Slavonic typikons do not agree with that, for on Thomas Sunday and on Monday after the Descent of the Holy Spirit they explicitly prescribe the Trisagion. Does not agree also the Typikon, called of St. Nicholas.

units.english_cohort_translation: 3. In older Menaia, which our Menaia also follow, troparia and kontakia are not given to every Saint, but in closer times we find them given in our Horologia. Therefore one should not wonder if regarding the use of troparia at the Hours the rubrics in some way do not agree with the *Menaion* and our Horo- or Prayer Book. For when a Saint had a troparion and kontakion, according to the ancient Typikon, they were taken at all Hours; but according to the Typikon of our Horo- and Prayer Books, in order not to repeat at all Hours on all days one and the same troparion and kontakion, for a certain variety at the 1st Hour – the troparion and kontakion of the day of the week, at the 3rd and 9th – of the Saint, and at the 6th – of the Temple.

units.english_cohort_translation: ^[20] However, it is better presented in the Greek Horologia -- only one troparion, that is of the current Saint, or the four aforementioned: "O God of our Fathers" with the three others, without distinction of day. In the Greek Menaia the Saint does not always have a troparion and, when he does not have one, then the general troparia are taken -- "O God of our Fathers"; when he has one, then to the Saint. With us, because the current Saint in the *Menaion* always has a troparion, then, if it were taken always, the troparia "O God of our Fathers" would be superfluous; so that they not be superfluous, they are taken daily, and to the Saints -- only to the Polyeleos ones. The troparion of the day and of the Temple is given only in the Slavonic Typikons.

units.english_cohort_translation: [180] According to the previous typikon: troparion of the Forefeast and to the saint, if he has, Glory: Kontakion to the saint, if he has, Both now: Kontakion of the Forefeast; everything else -- only to the saint, and Apostle-Gospel also of the day, in the first place. Also to the second saint is taken, if he has something. Before the troparia of the saint Slavonic typikons prescribe to the temple of the saint (Pochaiv *Triodion*, fol. 11, on the verso.).

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 3 без диякона 257 якщо ця литургия видправляеться
units.slavonic_diplomatic:
3. Без диякона
257. Якщо ця Літургія відправляється без диякона, священик виголошує все те, що належить до диякона, як про це вже було сказано в уставі вечірні й Божественної Літургії Івана Золотоустого.
units.english_cohort_translation: [285] According to the ancient rule the troparion of the saints is taken with Glory, also on the 1st and 6th hours; but with us today -- only the one of the day.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 260 на великому входи свиченосци якщо таки будут
units.slavonic_diplomatic: 260.  На великому вході свіченосці, якщо такі будуть, обернені до північних дверей і розміщені за чергою, супроводжують Напередосвяченого Агнця. Після того, як прийдуть перед св. двері разом стають обабіч, а потім вертаються на свої місця.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 4 у спивслужинни священикив 261 правила спивслужиння литургии
units.slavonic_diplomatic:
4. У співслужінні священиків
261. Правила співслужіння Літургії Напередосвячених – ті самі, що вечірні й Літургії Золотоустого. Тільки треба мати на увазі, що:
units.english_cohort_translation: Ritual unity is achieved through the observance of unified rubrical prescriptions. From ancient times, the Eastern Churches began to use collections of such prescriptions, that is, Typikons (from the Greek word typikon).

units.english_cohort_translation: [318] According to our most general and Russian typikons, Vespers with the Service of Basil on the Eve of the Nativity of Christ begins at the seventh hour of the day (At one in the afternoon), and on the Eve of Theophany -- at the fifth hour of the day (at eleven before noon, according to the present calculation); but according to other most ancient typikons in both cases: περί ωραν δεκατην της ημέρας/around the tenth hour of the day/ (at four in the afternoon). All-Night Vigil according to the general Slavic [typikon], among which also *Tserkovne Oko* -- at the tenth hour of the night (that is in the morning); according to others, the most ancient, on the Eve of the Nativity: περί ωραν πρωτην της νυκτός /around the first hour of the night/, and Theophany: περί ωραν δεύτερον της νυκτός /around the second hour of the night/. In the Constantinopolitan Patriarchate Vespers begins immediately after the ninth Royal Hour.

units.english_cohort_translation: [91] The Greek Typikon gives the whole service only to the saint, and Apostle and Gospel -- first of the day, and then of the saint; Προκειμενον του κατά την ημεραν Αγιου, Αλληλούια του Αγιου, Ευαγγελιον της ημέρας και του Αγιου. (Καιφ. σ) /Prokeimenon of the saint of the day, Alleluia of the saint, Gospel of the day and of the saint (chapter 6)/. So also in chapter 99, Mark. Although this rubric is given only in the Saturday service, however, it must be understood that also on other days of the week it should be so. Slavonic typikons prescribe the whole service to the day and to the saint, if he has one, and troparia -- also to the temple, if it is of the Lord or of the Theotokos. The Moscow Typikon also prescribes to the temple, if the temple is of a saint (although this does not agree with the rubric of that same Typikon, given on September 26 and January 30); this same Typikon ends the Kontakia with the Kontakion for the Dead *“With the saints give rest”* with the refrain "Glory" and the Kontakion of the temple, if it is of the Lord or of the Theotokos, if -- not, then with the usual "Protection" ("O Undisputed Intercessor") with the refrain "Both now" (chapter 52). This custom we find also among Greek-Italians and Greek-Melkites, but it does not exist among Constantinopolitan Greeks and Athonites, with the exception of some. But, since according to the rubric of the Greek Typikon, two Apostles and two Gospels were to be taken, and according to the Slavonic rubric, also the whole service of the day and of the saint, if he has one, and, since many saints (over one hundred eighty) have an Apostle and Gospel, as follows from the content of the Apostle-Gospel, therefore, in order to shorten the duration of the divine service, followers of the Greek Rite began already many years ago to reject certain rubrics; therefore also our Ruthenians take at the Liturgy only the service of the day, and reject the saint without Polyeleos; some -- conversely: take only the service to the saint, and reject the service of the day, as evidenced by the Pochaiv Sluzhebnik of 1765, which gives the Apostle and Gospel only on Sundays, and on weekdays -- only in Bright Week and in the week after the Descent of the Holy Spirit, similarly as Latin Missals, which give the Apostle and Gospel of the day only in these two mentioned weeks, for Great Lent and for certain other days. This custom we find also among Greek-Italians, observed also by some of those who are called Orthodox, whom the Moscow Typikon accuses, saying: "The Ecumenical Church does not take neither on the Beatitudes, nor at Liturgies the Apostle and Gospel to the saint on every day, only the sequential, that is the pillar throughout the whole year, in sequence, as also of selected saints who have an Apostle and Gospel. And if the Apostle and Gospel of the saint is read every day, then this is from one's own ignorance, and not according to the church typikon" (chapter 58, at the end). Exactly so also in the manuscript of the three-hundred-year-old Gospel that is among us. However, this rubric of the Ecumenical Church is not observed by the Constantinopolitan Hierarch, called Ecumenical, nor by the Churches subject to him, who (according to the testimony of hierarch Benjamin Νεαπολεος /of Neapolis/, who lived in Constantinople and on Mount Athos, who in our times accepted church union) have the custom, also in monasteries, to take the Apostle and Gospel only of the day, if the saint does not have one, if he has, then only to the saint, and in another they adhere to the new Constantinopolitan Typikon, printed in the patriarchal typography in 1851, marked with the patriarchal seal and confirmed by signatures of all patriarchs and hierarchs subject to them. In this Typikon there, where the rubric gives two Apostles and Gospels, one Apostle-Gospel is given, that is the Apostle -- of the first service, and the Gospel -- of the second service. Thus e.g. October 26, November 21, when they fall on a Sunday and on John the Theologian May 8, when it falls on Ascension.

units.english_cohort_translation: This appendix compiles and organizes the extensive historical, theological, and rubrical commentary from the footnotes and structural notes of the Dolnytsky Typikon translation. It serves as an authoritative reference for scholars and translators studying the Kyivan and Byzantine-Ruthenian liturgical traditions.

units.english_cohort_translation: [93] The most important readings, without doubt, -- are the Sunday and Saturday ones, since in the most ancient Gospels readings are given only for these two days of the week, so in the Ostroh one and in two Vatican ones: one Greek of the 9th century and one Slavonic Glagolitic of the 11th century.

units.english_cohort_translation: Although now we do not use the Odes of Holy Scripture presented at the end of the Psalter, excluding the Forty Days, nevertheless, we leave something from them, that is at the 8th Ode, instead of Glory – the refrain 'Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord,' and the refrain to the Katavasia of the 8th Ode: 'We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord, praising and magnifying Him unto all ages,' which is sung according to the tone of the Katavasia; also the Song of the Theotokos 'My soul magnifies' before the Heirmos of the 9th Ode of the canon, which we take also in the time of the Forty Days, and outside of it, with the exception of Feasts of the Lord and of the Theotokos, on which, according to ancient typikons, it is not proper to take [it].

units.english_cohort_translation: 6. Odes and Canons. The Biblical Odes, given at the end of the Psalter, are intertwined with the odes of the canon, as given: before the ode of the canon the corresponding ode of the Psalter is recited, leaving its last verses for refrains to the troparia of the canon, in such quantity as there will be troparia in the ode of the canon, including the heirmos, except two, for to the penultimate troparion we refrain "Glory", and to the last – "Both now". The 2nd Ode is recited in full before the ode of the canon, and to the troparia of its canon we refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee". According to our ancient custom, the Odes of the Psalter are recited only in those odes in which the triodion occurs, and in the other odes we refrain the usual refrains to the troparia of the canon. The Greek Typikon prescribes singing the Odes of the Psalter in the tone of the *Menaion* canon, but now we do not even know what their melody was.

units.english_cohort_translation: [454] Although Greek typikons do not give the blessing of water on this day, however, this custom, inherent to Greek-Slavs, is taken from the Greeks, who once had the custom of performing the blessing of water at the beginning of each month and, accordingly, on 1 August, according to the testimony of Balsamon in the explanation of Canon V of the Trullan Synod: Haec statuente canone, novilunium quidem festum ante annos omnem memoriam supeantes cessavit; eius loco, Dei gratia, ut et ipse propitious reddatur, preces, as Aquae lustrales in Ecclesia a populo fideli fiunt in uniuscuiusque mensis principio (Asseman. Calend. Tom. I. Cap. XI. Pag. 156) /Establishing this canon, truly the new moon feast, which from ancient times erased all memory of it; in its place, thanks be to God, and better prayers take place, and sanctification of water in the church, which the faithful people perform at the beginning of each month (Assemani, Calend., Vol. III, Part I, Chapter XI, p. 156)/.

units.english_cohort_translation: [107] Slavonic typikons, in order not to discard the canon for the dead, transfer it to the Panikhida over the Kolyva, or to Compline (Pochaiv *Octoechos* at the end and Moscow Typikon, chapter 12). The Greek Typikon in chapter 6, instead of the Martyria canon, prescribes the canon for the dead; however, with such a decision the Martyria canon would never be taken: neither on these Saturdays, nor on Souls Saturdays, for even on these Saturdays that same Typikon does not prescribe the Martyria canon. Probably ordinary Octoechoi did not have it.

units.english_cohort_translation: After the 3rd, 6th and 9th Ode of the canon, immediately after the Katavasia, the Small Litany is taken (according to the model given at the first Kathisma of Matins), each with its own exclamation, and after the litany at the 3rd Ode the Sessional Hymn is sung, at the 6th – Kontakion and Ikos, and at the 9th – the Exaposteilarion (Hymn of Light) is read. Both the Kontakion and Ikos are taken once each, the Sessional Hymn on Feasts of the Lord and of the Theotokos – twice, that is once – simply the Sessional Hymn, and the second time – with the refrain Glory, Both now. And the Exaposteilarion on Feasts of the Lord and of the Theotokos is taken three times, that is twice – simply, and the third time – with the refrain Glory, Both now. On the Feast of a Polyeleos or non-Polyeleos Saint, which is celebrated, according to the Slavonic Typikon, on 6, the Sessional Hymn and his Exaposteilarion are taken twice , then Both now: his Theotokion. If the Saint has two Sessional Hymns or Exaposteilaria, then they are taken once each, that is the first – simply, the second – with the refrain Glory, then Both now: his Theotokion . When several services coincide, each with its own Sessional Hymn, Kontakion-Ikos and Exaposteilarion, then they are taken one after another, according to the order of services; however, the Kontakion-Ikos of the first service is taken at the 6th Ode in its place, and the Kontakion-Ikos of the second, according to the Slavonic typikons , is transferred to the 3rd Ode and goes immediately before the Sessional Hymn. The sequence of Sessional Hymns and Exaposteilaria in the middle of a Feast of the Lord and of the Theotokos ends with the Sessional Hymn or Exaposteilarion of the Feast. After the Katavasia of the 9th Ode, according to the Slavonic Typikon, 'It is truly meet' is taken, if it is not Sunday. If it is Sunday, 'It is truly meet' is not taken, but then, between the Small Litany and the Exaposteilarion (Exapostolarion) we sing, according to the tone of the Prokeimenon of the Liturgy, the troparion 'Holy is the Lord our God' (3)" .

Furthermore, the canonical term **Heirmos** (or **Heirmoi**) is never used; instead, Royal Doors exclusively uses the phonetic Slavonic spelling **Heirmos** (561 times) or **Katavasia** (395 times) to designate these canon hymns. Sessional hymns are referred to as **Sessional Hymn** (191 times) or **Kathisma Reading** (136 times).

units.english_cohort_translation: ^[14] Since no Typikon (the Synod testifies) prescribes censing in the temple here, it would be better if the deacons cense from the place of the Litiya when they arrive there. And since this is better, we have placed such a rubric in the text, and we have completely rejected the worse existing local custom of censing the Holy Table and the local icons as at "Lord, I have cried," although the Synod mentions it too. However, if there are icons in the narthex, it is proper to cense them first, for the ancient Typikons prescribe so.

units.english_cohort_translation: [341] Since ancient typikons do not give All-Night Vigil, nothing is mentioned about the troparia at the blessing of loaves; but to sing: troparion to the saint once, Glory, Both now: to the feast, as the Pochaiv *Anthologion* has, does not correspond to the rite, according to which troparia are taken at the All-Night Vigil. -- "If there is no All-Night Vigil, at Compline -- Kontakion to the Saint, Glory, Both now: of the Feast". At Midnight Office, after the 1st Trisagion -- Troparion of the Feast; after the 2nd -- Kontakion of the Feast; we do not say the prayer "Remember", but "Lord, have mercy" (12) and dismissal. Thus in Slavic menaia.

units.english_cohort_translation: This Vespers is celebrated just as Daily [Vespers] , however, without a Kathisma and without litanies, except for the last 'Have mercy on us, O God,' which only the Slavonic Typikons present, but the Greek do not prescribe. The stichera at 'Lord, I have cried' will be only 4. The dismissal, although it can begin from 'Glory to Thee, O Christ God,' yet with us is exclaimed also before that: 'Wisdom!' and 'More honorable' just as at Daily Vespers.

units.english_cohort_translation: [317] The ancient Lviv *Horologion* gives the dismissal of the feast, however, since in all other cases dismissals of feasts begin with Vespers of the feast, rightly the *Tserkovne Oko* and Pochaiv *Menaion* give "dismissal of the day", with commemoration, as it seems to us, also of the saint who falls on this day.

units.english_cohort_translation: [376] Thus in chapter 43 of Mark, *Tserkovne Oko*, Pochaiv *Menaion* and Moscow Typikon; however, if there is to be uniformity in typikons, then we think that here too the 1st Theotokion of the tone should be according to the general rule of the Afterfeast of the Lord and the Theotokos, given at the end of the Pochaiv and Moscow *Octoechos* under the prescription about the temple of the Resurrection of Christ; and if -- not, then also in the Afterfeast of other feasts there should be a stichera of the Feast, which would be in greater conformity with ancient typikons, in which neither on the Forefeast, nor on the Afterfeast, nor on the Apodosis of the Feast is the Dogmatikon given on Friday evening, but only stichera of the Feast, regardless -- whether it is Saturday or another day of the week. (Our handwritten Typikon, chapter 20 and chapter 11 of Mark in the *Tserkovne Oko*), although general Slavic typikons on the Fore- and Afterfeast and on the Apodosis of the Feast give the Dogmatikon. Moscow Typikon 12 September, 24 March, 14 August; *Tserkovne Oko* 12 September, 21 September; Pochaiv *Menaion* 12 September; Typikon of the Lviv University, p. 87.

units.english_cohort_translation: [127] Moscow Typikon, chapter 4, and Peremyshl, page 85. -- Mark in chapters 78 and 79 prescribes after the 3rd Ode the Sessional Hymn of the saint, Glory, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the tone, that is Sunday, after the 6th -- Kontakion of the saint. New Constantinopolitan Typikon after the 3rd Ode: Κοντακιον το αναστασιμον χύμα, είτα ψαλλεται το Κάθισμα του Αγιου, και το θεοτοκιον; μετά δε την εκτην ωδην Κοντακιον και Οίκος του εορταζομενου Αγιου /Kontakion of the resurrection spoken, then is sung the Kathisma of the saint, and the Theotokion; after the 6th Ode Kontakion and Ikos of the celebrated Saint/. Greek Typikon in chapter 2, after the 3rd Ode -- Κάθισμα του Μηναίου /Kathisma of the *Menaion*/, after the 6th -- Κοντακιον του Αγιου /Kontakion of the Saint/, after the 9th -- Εξαποστιλαριον το αναστασιμον και του Αγιου ει εορτάζεται, και το θεοτοκιον /Exaposteilarion of the resurrection and of the Saint if he is celebrated, and the Theotokion/, but does not indicate, which Theotokion; however, Slavonic typikons rightly prescribe the Theotokion of the Sunday Exaposteilarion, for it corresponds to the Sunday Gospel.

units.english_cohort_translation: [279] We find the Service of St. Catherine as having Polyeleos only in our Pochaiv *Menaion* and in the new Greek-Venetian one; but in others -- without Polyeleos. In later Greek typikons we find it given on 25 November with the Apodosis of the Feast of the Entry into the Temple of the Most Holy Theotokos, and in earlier ones -- on the 24th, as it is today among Greek-Slavs. Thus the Greek-Venetian *Menaion* of 1615 gives: Σημειωσαι ουν, ότι ευρομεν εν τισι Τυπικοις των νεωτέρων, ότι εν τιοα των πόλεων ψαλλεται η ακολουθία της αγίας μάρτυρος Αικατερίνης εν τη κε του μηνός, εν η και αποδιδοται η εορτή. Εν ετεροις δε Τυπικοις παλαιοτεροις ευρομεν αυτήν εορτάζεσαι εν τη κδ του αυτού μηνός: εν δε τη κε ψαλλομεν την ακολουθίαν του εν αγιοις Κλημεντος Παπα Ρώμης, και Πέτρου Αλεξανδρείας, εν η και αποδιδοται η εορτή των Εισοδιων /Note, therefore, that we found in some newer typikons, that in some places the service of the holy martyr Catherine is sung on the 25th day of this month, on which the feast is also given up. In other older typikons we found that her memory is celebrated on the 24th of this month, and on the 25th we sing the service of Saints Clement Pope of Rome and Peter of Alexandria, and on this day also the feast of the Entry is given up/. This transfer from the 24th to the 25th day, in the opinion of the Greeks, as explained by the new Greek-Venetian *Menaion* (24 November, p. 158), was done at the wish of the monks of Mount Sinai, so that it would not coincide with the Apodosis of the feast and, so that in this way the memory of the saint would be honored more solemnly. For we know that the body of the holy great martyr was transferred by angelic power to Mount Sinai and buried there.

units.english_cohort_translation: [264] Ancient Greek typikons mention nothing about a deacon, neither at the bringing out, nor at the exaltation, nor at the laying of the precious Cross, but only about one priest. The Greek typikon, similarly to the Slavic ones, prescribes for the priest to vest in all priestly vestments: αλασσει ο Ιερεύς πασαν την ιερατικην στολην /the priest vests in all priestly vestments/. The Greek *Triodion* (Sunday of the Veneration of the Cross) and the new Constantinopolitan Typikon, similarly to Slavic typikons, prescribes for the priest to enter with the cross from the sanctuary to the temple through the northern doors: εκ του αριστερού Βήματος /from the left side of the sanctuary/. Greek typikons, with the exception of the new Constantinopolitan, and the Slavic of the Lviv University, prescribe for the priest, having exited from the sanctuary to the temple, to head to the entrance doors that lead from the temple to the narthex, which are sometimes called royal, and there await the end of the Doxology and from there exclaim "Wisdom, attend", and then head to the tetrapod, which is before the iconostasis. Although these doors are called royal, βασιλικαι /royal/, one must understand that they were called so in the past. Today we call royal the middle doors of the iconostasis, which according to ancient custom are called holy: αγιαι ΰυραι /holy doors/ (chapter 96, Greek Typikon).

units.english_cohort_translation: [754] Ed. note. In ancient times, "Royal Doors" referred to those doors that led from the narthex to the temple, for at them the Patriarch met the Emperor. Later this name was applied with improper meaning to the middle doors of the iconostasis. In the rubrics of modern Greek liturgical books, "holy doors" are given (see Akolouthia tou Esperinou kai tou Orthrou, Roma 1950, p. 16), therefore we also consistently correct "Royal Doors" to "Holy Doors" everywhere in this Typikon.

units.english_cohort_translation: 97. According to the ancient custom of the Eastern Church, only one Holy Liturgy may be celebrated at the same holy table. However, one may depart from this rule if the Divine Liturgy must be repeated for the benefit of the faithful. If there is one or several secondary churches in the parish, then the more solemn Liturgy is celebrated in the main sanctuary, and other liturgies should be celebrated rather in the side sanctuaries.

units.english_cohort_translation: Regarding the troparion "Holy is the Lord our God," neither the ancient Greek Typikons nor the Euchologia prescribe to take it three times, nor do they adduce its verses. However, the Slavonic rubrics and the new Constantinopolitan Typikon prescribe to take it three times; regarding the verses -- they do not agree. Our Sluzhebnik and the new Constantinopolitan Typikon present only one verse; ours: "Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy" (5th verse of the 98th psalm, from the last verse of which this troparion is taken). Constantinopolitan: Υψουτε Κυριον τον θεον ημών /Exalt ye the Lord our God/. The Tserkovne Oko and following it the Moscow Typikons present two verses, namely: 1. "For holy is the Lord our God"; 2. "Over all people is our God." In our opinion, if the troparion must be taken three times, then one verse is not sufficient; therefore it is possible to divide the verse "Exalt ye" into two parts, of which the second would begin from: "And worship at His footstool" etc.

units.english_cohort_translation: [277] Some consider, according to the edition of the Peremyshl Typikon of 1870, p. 271, that neither on St. Michael, nor on St. Prophet Elias, should *“Blessed is the man”* be sung and, that then not a single kathisma is taken, for this kathisma, as the publisher writes about it, is found only in the Pochaiv *Anthologion*, and in the most ancient menaia and Anthologia they are not mentioned; the reason for this is considered to be that "Elias did not die, and St. Michael, as bodiless, is not subject to death". However, this is not enough. For regarding the rule, not only the Pochaiv *Anthologion* (*Anthologion*) of 1777 and the Pochaiv *Menaion* of the same year, but also the Lviv *Anthologion* (*Anthologion*) of 1643 and the Great Typikon, under the title *Tserkovne Oko*, printed in Moscow in 1615, that is more than a century and a half before the Pochaiv *Anthologion*, and the manuscript *Anthologion* of 1736, which we have, and the Typikon of the All-Russian Church, printed in Moscow in 1859, by the decision of its Governing Synod, give also on these two feasts the kathisma *“Blessed is the man”*. Although some rules, like the Moscow *Menaion* of 1782, the Greek-Venetian of 1884 do not give *“Blessed is the man”*, it does not follow from this that no kathisma is needed, for even on Saints without Polyeleos in the *Menaion* a kathisma is not given, but the sequential one is meant; so here one can understand the sequential one, which three ancient handwritten Slavic typikons give: one -- of the Lviv University, the second -- of St. Onuphrius in Lviv, and the third -- of the library of the Chapter of St. George; also *Tserkovne Oko* (which gives two rules: one with *“Blessed is the man”*, and the second with the sequential kathisma). The reason that these rules give for these two feasts a sequential kathisma, may lie in the fact that their service initially had neither All-Night Vigil nor Polyeleos, but gradually, with time, grew into All-Night Vigil. About St. Elias it is written in the Pochaiv *Menaion*: "Let it be known that in printed Greek menaia, in handwritten typikons, and also in Slavic handwritten and printed typikons, the service of the Prophet Elias is given on 6, with *Octoechos*". And regarding St. Michael, the above-mentioned Slavic typikons give him a service only of the Polyeleos type, but incomplete, for they partially combine his service with the service of the *Octoechos*, as for a Saint without Polyeleos.

units.english_cohort_translation: [77] When two kathismata should be read, and when three, we noted in the note to the Order of Daily Matins on page 41. Regarding small litanies which are read between kathismata and sessional hymns, the Lviv Synod, our Horologions and our Sluzhebniks (at the end) give them also at Small Matins, and they are used also by the Greek-Melkites (according to the testimony of their patriarch bl. m. Clement Bahous). Conversely, in the Russian Typikon, approved by their Governing Synod (Moscow edition of 1859), in the Order of Daily Matins it is written that the priest says them only at the Vigil and when the memory of saints having a Polyeleos and Doxology is celebrated; similarly also in the new Wallachian-Bucharest Typikon, in which in the Order of Daily Matins is given: "We take sessional hymns from the *Octoechos* without litanies" (untranslatable); and adds: "In monasteries, usually, between kathismata litanies are taken only on Sunday and when more special saints occur". From the Greek Typikon no conclusion can be made, for in it small litanies are not mentioned neither at Small Matins, nor at Great, nor before the Canon, nor after the Canon. It is assumed in the Typikon that this is known to everyone. From the rubrics of the Greek *Triodion*, given at Matins on Meatfare Saturday, one can conclude that these litanies should be said also at Small Matins. For it gives: η συνηιϊης στιχολογια. Εν δε ταις συναπταις πασαις της στιχολογιας και του Κανόνος, μνημονεύονται πάντες οι προαπελΰοντες Πατέρες και αδελφοί ημων /Ordinary Stichology. In all small litanies of the Stichology and of the Canon, all our fathers and brethren who have passed away before us are commemorated/. Let everyone observe the rubric and custom of his Church. Finally, in our opinion, later typikons reject litanies here only for the sake of greater shortening of the divine service; if the single difference between Small and Great Matins were the rejection or use of litanies, then this difference should have been indicated in some place of ancient liturgical books; however, this is not encountered. What the exclamation of the third litany should be is not indicated in any of the church books. Therefore we are forced to borrow it from Great Matins. At Great Matins in Slavonic books two exclamations are given which are used at the third litany, that is one -- for Sunday "For blessed is" and the second -- for Polyeleos feasts "For holy Art Thou". For the sake of distinguishing the Sunday day from the ordinary day, at Small Matins it is appropriate to use the second "For holy Art Thou", although it would not be bad to use also the first "For blessed is" (Οτι ευλογητοα), for in Greek books we find only this one exclamation, without distinction of day. Regarding Sessional Hymns, they are taken two or three after each stichology, depending on the edition, except the Theotokion. In Lviv editions of the *Octoechos* and in the Greek-Venetian one, only to the Theotokion is sung "Glory, Both now". In the Pochaiv and Moscow ones a separate refrain is also given to every second, or even to the third sessional hymn. This refrain, corresponding to the content of the sessional hymn: on Monday and Tuesday -- Penitential "O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger"; on Wednesday and Friday -- of the Cross, and on Thursday -- of the Apostles; to the third sessional hymn, that is the Martyron -- also the Martyron refrain: "Wondrous is God in His saints".

units.english_cohort_translation: ^[508] Regarding the litany, we do not find unity in the rubrics. For some rubrics are silent about it, others prescribe it, and some exclude it. Those that are silent about it are the manuscript Vatican Typika... Those that prescribe the litany: The Greek Bologna *Triodion* 1724, Kyivan-Pechersk 1640, Lviv 1753 and some manuscripts. Those that exclude it: The Moscow Typikon 1859... *Tserkovne Oko* and the ancient manuscript Typikon... We suppose that the rubrics which do not prescribe the litany are more logical, for at all other Lenten Vespers and Matins this litany is not present...

units.english_cohort_translation: [311] Typikons of some Russian monasteries, given by the *Tserkovne Oko*, prescribe for the deacon at each Hour to sing three litanies, that is "In peace let us pray to the Lord" at the end of the tripalm, the Small Litany before the Prokeimenon and "Let us complete" after the singing of the Gospel. This is not enough for Greek length and with unnecessary additions the Greeks distort the form of the Hours, handed down to us from the beginnings; also ancient Lviv typikons add litanies.

units.english_cohort_translation: 7. If there be several Prokeimena, Alleluias, Apostle-Gospels and Communion Hymns, then one must know how to take them. Know first, that in church typikons more than two are not given, with the exception of Apostle-Gospels, of which only in Slavonic typikons three are given, for the Slavs are richer in supplications than the Greeks. For where three readings coincide, the Greek typikons do not give the sequential one, but the Slavonic ones take it under the refrain of the first reading, as if one with it . When this is impossible, on the occasion of some great feast, then they order to take it on the day before under the refrain with the sequential one . However, this rule has been preserved among us perhaps only in cathedral churches, for in others usually only one Apostle-Gospel is taken, as also one service either of the day, or of the saint, or one for need. If, therefore, there be two Prokeimena and two Alleluias, then both are taken under one heading, that is both Prokeimena – before the refrain of the first reading, both Alleluias – after the completion of the second reading. However, the first Prokeimenon is taken twice, namely: once – before and once – after the verse, the second – only once and without a verse, for in this case the Typikon does not give a verse. Similarly also "Alleluia": both of its verses are taken only of the first service, and of the second – only one first verse . The Heading, that is from whom: from Paul, from Matthew or from another, is taken only of the first reading, and the others usually are not taken, although it would be better to announce the headings of other readings as well, for it is not indifferent to the listeners to know the reading of which holy author is being proclaimed; and for this reason only would the rubric make certain sense, which orders to take the sequential reading under the refrain, for taking one reading under the refrain of another means merging it with the previous one because its heading is not announced. If the heading of the following third reading, which is not taken under the refrain, is not named, then it should have been said that this third reading is also taken under the refrain. "Let us be attentive" is announced only at the beginning of the first reading. If there be two Communion Hymns, then "Alleluia" is repeated only upon the completion of the second .

units.english_cohort_translation: ^[615] According to the ancient rubric of community life the procession goes from the temple into the narthex through the northern doors of this narthex and there, before its central doors leading into the temple, the beginning of Matins is sung. Carried are: Gospel -- by the priest and censer -- by the deacon, preceded by candle-bearers, brethren with lit candles, as you have in the Greek *Pentecostarion*. To this the Pochaiv *Triodion* adds the icon of the Resurrection of Christ, and *Tserkovne Oko* -- also the icon of the Most Holy Theotokos and other holy icons, carried by priests and deacons, so that in such a way the procession would be more majestic, than only with candles. According to the custom of the surroundings of Greece, independent of the Patriarch of Constantinople, before this procession the bishop or priest, standing in the holy doors with a lit candlestick in hand, exclaims in a loud voice: "Come ye, take light from the unwaning light, and glorify Christ, who is risen from the dead", that is "Come, receive light from the unwaning light and kiss Christ, risen from the dead". And so all approach one by one, to light their candles from him, forming after this the procession (The Holy Passions. Athens. 1892)

units.english_cohort_translation: [342] Thus have later editions, namely ours Pochaiv and the Russian, and the most ancient Greek, namely Ευχολογιον /*Euchologion*/ of Benedict, and of the Slavic ones -- Ostromir Gospel, *Tserkovne Oko* and the manuscript give the Prokeimenon only to the Saint, and the Apostle-Gospel -- only to the Circumcision, for the Prokeimenon of the Feast and the Apostle-Gospel to the Saint -- is a later addition of the Slavs. However, now comes the time not of adding new, but of shortening ancient prayers. The ancient typikon has this: "Let the Gospel be taken at Matins to the saint, and at the Liturgy -- to the Circumcision".

units.english_cohort_translation: ^[600] The magnificent rite of the Shroud in ancient *Triodia* and Typika is not given, for it was introduced later; however, today it is used among all followers of the Greek rite, and among us -- also with the exposition of the Holy Mysteries, according to the custom of the Latins of the Austrian State and various German dioceses (Nilles, Calend. T. 2, p. 312). It is described in our Sluzhebniks, published in Pochaiv back under Stanislaus Augustus in 1767, then in Russian Typika and in the new Typikon of the Patriarchate of Constantinople. However, in our Sluzhebniks the procession with the Shroud is given only at Vespers, in Russian rubrics -- only at Saturday Matins, after the Great Doxology, and in the Constantinopolitan Typikon the bringing out into the temple to the tomb is prescribed at Vespers, the procession around the temple -- at Matins.

units.english_cohort_translation: [45] According to the ancient rubric, a saint "on 4" could be of two types: that is, either with a troparion or without a troparion; and when the saint has no troparion, then at Matins, instead of "God is the Lord," "Alleluia" was sung and the divine service had a separate rubric. But in our current Horologia, troparia are given for every day of the month, and therefore at Matins we always sing "God is the Lord," and we limit the "Alleluia" service to Great Lent, as do the Greeks.

units.english_cohort_translation: Regarding the time and place of the placing of the Shroud we do not find an ancient rubric, for this rite is later and different in different regions. According to the custom of our archcathedral church the Shroud remains hung behind the holy table, over the High Place, from Resurrection Matins to the Apodosis of the Resurrection inclusive, that is until Wednesday before the Ascension. According to the custom of our other churches, the Shroud, taken from the Tomb before Resurrection Matins, is placed on the holy table, where it remains during the whole Bright Week, and from the Sunday of Ap. Thomas to the Apodosis of the Resurrection – behind the holy table. According to others – it remains on the altar, the antimension with the Gospel is placed on it and the Liturgy is celebrated on it. However, it is better to place the Shroud behind the holy table, for lying on the altar, it is often significantly damaged by candles, from which wax drips on it.

units.english_cohort_translation: ^[626] So about "Christ is risen" in our Sluzhebniks, except "We have seen", and in its place they have "Christ is risen", however, such is our custom and so in the Pochaiv *Triodion* of 1786... and in the Moscow Typikon of 1859... Ancient Greek rubrics prescribe "Christ is risen" only instead of "Blessed be the name" and instead of the psalm "I will bless the Lord", as in the Slavonic Typikon of the Lviv University. A later custom of the Greeks -- to sing "Christ is risen" after "Blessed is the Kingdom" three times and, instead of "We have seen the true light" and instead of "Blessed be the name of the Lord", -- three times. However, some of them, after "Blessed is the Kingdom" sing "Christ is risen" with its verses, as is given at the beginning of Resurrection Matins. The Moscow Typikon follows them, but the new Constantinopolitan Typikon does not go. What we said about the custom of the Greeks, we took from a description which we have from the island of Corfu, in which is written the following: "After 'Blessed is the kingdom' the priest 'Christ is risen', and successively repeat it, first the right followed by the left choir; and this happens on all the days of Pascha until the Ascension. But on the great Sunday, and on those of the New Week we follow to sing it after its verses unchanged; as was said previously at Matins... Is sung successively 'Christ is risen' – as much on the great Sunday as on the remaining days of Pascha at 'With fear' instead of 'We have seen the light', and before the Dismissal three times flowingly instead of 'Blessed be the name', and at the end, at the Dismissal instead of 'Through the prayers' /After 'Blessed is the Kingdom' the priest: 'Christ is risen', successively again repeat it: first -- the right, then -- and the left choir. And so it will be on all days from the Resurrection to the Ascension. But on the Great Sunday and on the days of Bright Week we continue to sing invariable this with its verses, as is taken at Matins ... Successively is sung 'Christ is risen' on the Great Sunday as much as on the rest of the days of the Resurrection: at 'With fear', instead of 'We have seen the light' and before the dismissal three times flowingly, instead of 'Blessed be the name' and at the end, at the dismissal, instead of 'Through the prayers of our holy fathers'/.

units.english_cohort_translation: [160] According to the ancient typikon, on Sunday, in view of the All-Night Vigil, everything was taken on Small Vespers only of the Sunday, as usual. But on Great Vespers at the Lytia: one sticheron of the temple, and also stichera of the Forefeast from the Aposticha of Matins. At the Blessing of Loaves: Troparion "O Virgin Theotokos" twice and of the Forefeast once (*Menaion* September 7), and Mark: "O Virgin Theotokos" thrice without the Afterfeast (Καιφ. ξε /chapter 65/).

units.english_cohort_translation: [65] Peremyshl Typikon, page 81. -- According to the ancient typikon there was to be a Sunday troparion at all hours, also "Glory" at the 1st and 6th -- Goes also to the first saint, at the 3rd and 9th -- to the second; Kontakia -- alternating: at the 1st and 6th -- to the first, at the 3rd and 9th -- to the second saint (compare John the Theologian on the Sunday of the Holy Fathers). When the Kontakion is only for one saint, then it alone is taken at all [hours]; and when for neither, nor for the feast, then the Hypakoe of the tone is taken; for general Greek editions do not have Sunday Kontakia. Regarding the Hypakoe, you have the rubric in Greek Horologions at the 1st Hour, it and at the other hours must be observed.
